declarations.signature: theorem UpperHalfCarryCapacity.of_boolean_suffix {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} {y : List ℕ} (hylen : y.length = upperHalfRepairLength n - 1) (hybool : ∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) (hyvalue : Nat.ofDigits 2 y = localBinarySuffix D k (n - 1)) : UpperHalfCarryCapacity D k n
declarations.docstring: Booleanity of the already constructed suffix through `n-1` supplies the undershoot automatically: a word on the `upperHalfRepairLength n - 1` available positions has value strictly below that power of two. The remaining global adapter only has to identify the carry `A` with this suffix value.

declarations.name: UpperHalfCarryCapacity.of_boolean_coefficients
declarations.signature: theorem UpperHalfCarryCapacity.of_boolean_coefficients {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (ha : ∀ m, n / 2 < m → m < n → a m = 0 ∨ a m = 1) (hvalue : Nat.ofDigits 2 (upperSuffixWord a (n / 2) (n - 1)) = localBinarySuffix D k (n - 1)) : UpperHalfCarryCapacity D k n
declarations.docstring: Coefficient-level adapter for the global repair process. Booleanity on `(⌊n/2⌋,n-1]` plus the exact carry/suffix identity supplies the local undershoot with no additional analytic estimate.

declarations.name: localRepairInteger_lt_upperHalfCapacity_of_carryCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem localRepairInteger_lt_upperHalfCapacity_of_carryCapacity {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hendpoint : 2 ≤ endpointDivisorContribution D n) (hcapacity : UpperHalfCarryCapacity D k n) : localRepairInteger D k n < (2 ^ upperHalfRepairLength n : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: The strict `H < 2A` estimate turns the supplied lower-prefix undershoot into the exact upper-half capacity bound.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_for_localRepairInteger
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_for_localRepairInteger {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n / 2) (hprefix : RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot D k) (hfit : localRepairInteger D k n < (2 ^ upperHalfRepairLength n : ℕ)) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = upperHalfRepairLength n ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ signedDyadicValue (List.map (fun b : ℕ ↦ (b : ℤ)) y) = localRepairInteger D k n
declarations.docstring: Conditional block realization of the endpoint repair integer. The fractional-part theorem supplies nonnegativity. The only remaining local feasibility input is the genuine capacity bound `H < 2^(n-⌊n/2⌋)`.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_of_repair_inputs
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_of_repair_inputs {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n / 2) (hprefix : RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot D k) (hendpoint : 2 ≤ endpointDivisorContribution D n) (hcapacity : UpperHalfCarryCapacity D k n) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = upperHalfRepairLength n ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ signedDyadicValue (List.map (fun b : ℕ ↦ (b : ℤ)) y) = localRepairInteger D k n
declarations.docstring: Rational half-cutoff undershoot plus the automatically supplied carry capacity yields the actual Boolean repair on `(⌊n/2⌋,n]`.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_of_boolean_suffix
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_of_boolean_suffix {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n / 2) (hprefix : RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot D k) (hendpoint : 2 ≤ endpointDivisorContribution D n) (hn : 0 < n) (ha : ∀ m, n / 2 < m → m < n → a m = 0 ∨ a m = 1) (hvalue : Nat.ofDigits 2 (upperSuffixWord a (n / 2) (n - 1)) = localBinarySuffix D k (n - 1)) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = upperHalfRepairLength n ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ signedDyadicValue (List.map (fun b : ℕ ↦ (b : ℤ)) y) =
declarations.docstring: Coefficient-level form in which upper-half capacity is discharged from the already-Boolean suffix and its exact value. The only analytic hypothesis in this route is `RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot`.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalf_boolean_replacement_of_repair_inputs
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalf_boolean_replacement_of_repair_inputs (a : List ℤ) {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n / 2) (hprefix : RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot D k) (hendpoint : 2 ≤ endpointDivisorContribution D n) (hcapacity : UpperHalfCarryCapacity D k n) (hlen : a.length = upperHalfRepairLength n) (hvalue : signedDyadicValue a = localRepairInteger D k n) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = a.length ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ signedDyadicValue (List.map (fun b : ℕ ↦ (b : ℤ)) y) = signedDyadicValue a
declarations.docstring: Unchanged-value form of the upper-half repair. Once the supplied signed block has endpoint value `H`, the rational undershoot and Boolean-suffix capacity replace it by a Boolean block on the same coordinates without changing its dyadic value.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalf_boolean_replacement_of_boolean_suffix
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalf_boolean_replacement_of_boolean_suffix (block : List ℤ) {D : Finset ℕ} {k n : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hk : k < n) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n / 2) (hprefix : RationalHalfCutoffUndershoot D k) (hendpoint : 2 ≤ endpointDivisorContribution D n) (hn : 0 < n) (ha : ∀ m, n / 2 < m → m < n → a m = 0 ∨ a m = 1) (hsuffix : Nat.ofDigits 2 (upperSuffixWord a (n / 2) (n - 1)) = localBinarySuffix D k (n - 1)) (hlen : block.length = upperHalfRepairLength n) (hblock : signedDyadicValue block = localRepairInteger D k n) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = block.length ∧
declarations.docstring: Final coefficient-level unchanged-value repair theorem. Booleanity and the exact value of the existing upper suffix discharge capacity; a signed block of endpoint value `H` is replaced on the same coordinates by a Boolean block without changing its dyadic value.

declarations.name: upperSupportFromWord
declarations.signature: def upperSupportFromWord : ℕ → List ℕ → Finset ℕ | _, [] => ∅ | M, b :: y => if b = 1 then insert M (upperSupportFromWord (M - 1) y) else upperSupportFromWord (M - 1) y theorem upperSupportFromWord_le_top {M : ℕ} {y : List ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ upperSupportFromWord M y) : d ≤ M
declarations.docstring: The support encoded by a least-significant-digit-first word whose top rank is `M`. The head controls rank `M`, the next digit rank `M-1`, and so on.

declarations.name: upperSupportFromWord_le_top
declarations.signature: theorem upperSupportFromWord_le_top {M : ℕ} {y : List ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ upperSupportFromWord M y) : d ≤ M

declarations.name: upperSupportFromWord_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem upperSupportFromWord_lower_bound {M : ℕ} {y : List ℕ} (hyM : y.length ≤ M) {d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ upperSupportFromWord M y) : M + 1 - y.length ≤ d
declarations.docstring: A word of length at most `M` uses only the final `y.length` positive ranks ending at `M`.

declarations.name: localMersenneQuotient_eq_two_pow_sub_of_half_lt
declarations.signature: theorem localMersenneQuotient_eq_two_pow_sub_of_half_lt {M d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hhalf : M / 2 < d) (hdM : d ≤ M) : localMersenneQuotient M d = 2 ^ (M - d)
declarations.docstring: Above the half cutoff a Mersenne quotient is the corresponding pure power of two.

declarations.name: localPrefixQuotient_upperSupportFromWord
declarations.signature: theorem localPrefixQuotient_upperSupportFromWord {M : ℕ} {y : List ℕ} (hyM : y.length ≤ M) (hybool : ∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) (hlower : M + 1 - y.length > M / 2) (hlower2 : 2 ≤ M + 1 - y.length) : localPrefixQuotient (upperSupportFromWord M y) M = Nat.ofDigits 2 y
declarations.docstring: In the pure upper window, the quotient sum of the support encoded by a Boolean word is exactly the binary value of that word.

declarations.name: exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_two_mul_sub_two_of_skippedCore
declarations.signature: theorem exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_two_mul_sub_two_of_skippedCore {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hskip : (1 / 2 : ℚ) - localMersennePrefixValue D < mersenneWeightRat c) : ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow (2 * c - 2)
declarations.docstring: **Skipped-core exact row.** A finite Boolean support strictly below one half whose deficit is already smaller than the next rank produces an exact finite quotient row at endpoint `2c-2`.

declarations.name: exists_exactRowStrictUpperFill_of_skippedCoreSharpCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem exists_exactRowStrictUpperFill_of_skippedCoreSharpCapacity {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hsharp : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)) : ∃ E : Finset ℕ, D ⊆ E ∧ (∀ d ∈ E, d ∉ D → c < d) ∧ (∀ d ∈ E, 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ 2 * c - 2) ∧ localPrefixQuotient E (2 * c - 2) = 2 ^ ((2 * c - 2) - 1) - 1
declarations.docstring: If the skipped-core suffix fits in only `c-2` bits, its exact repair can be placed strictly above rank `c`. This is the support-separation form needed by the first-crossing consumer: every newly inserted rank is larger than the crossing rank that supplied the core. The premise is deliberately the sharp integer inequality itself. The weaker skipped-core estimate currently proves only `c-1`-bit capacity.

declarations.name: exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_two_mul_sub_two_of_skippedCoreSharpCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_two_mul_sub_two_of_skippedCoreSharpCapacity {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hsharp : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)) : ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow (2 * c - 2)
declarations.docstring: The strict upper fill is, in particular, an exact local half row.

declarations.name: strictUpperFill_filter_le_eq_core
declarations.signature: theorem strictUpperFill_filter_le_eq_core {D E : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, d < c) (hDE : D ⊆ E) (hnew : ∀ d ∈ E, d ∉ D → c < d) : E.filter (fun d ↦ d ≤ c) = D
declarations.docstring: A strict upper fill agrees with its skipped core through rank `c`. This is the exact prefix identity used to force any later crossing rank to be strictly larger than `c`.

declarations.name: CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips
declarations.docstring: Positive skipped ranks of the rational half-greedy support occur arbitrarily far out. Positivity separates the skipped-core construction from the already-terminal case in which a finite greedy prefix equals one half exactly.

declarations.name: exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_of_positiveHalfGreedySkip
declarations.signature: theorem exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_of_positiveHalfGreedySkip {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hpos : 0 < greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 2 : ℚ) (c - 1)) (hskip : greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 2 : ℚ) (c - 1) < mersenneWeightRat c) : ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow (2 * c - 2)
declarations.docstring: One positive rational-greedy skip supplies an actual exact local Mersenne half row.

declarations.name: cofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
declarations.docstring: Cofinal positive rational-greedy skips yield cofinal exact quotient rows. The row endpoints `2c-2` are automatically cofinal with the skipped ranks `c`.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
declarations.docstring: The new exact-row route reaches the closed Mersenne achievement set as soon as the positive-skip supply is cofinal.

declarations.name: localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_iff
declarations.signature: theorem localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_iff {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2) ↔ 2 ^ ((2 * c - 2) - 1) ≤ localPrefixQuotient (insert c D) (2 * c - 2)
declarations.docstring: At the skipped-core endpoint `2c - 2`, fitting the binary repair below the critical `2^(c-2)` threshold is exactly the assertion that adjoining the crossing rank `c` makes the integral quotient reach the half target. The below-half hypothesis is used only to make the truncated natural suffix an honest subtraction. The separate crossing-above hypothesis from the skipped-core construction is deliberately absent: this theorem identifies the remaining quantitative socket rather than assuming it.

declarations.name: halfTarget_le_localPrefixQuotient_of_value_above_fractionMass_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem halfTarget_le_localPrefixQuotient_of_value_above_fractionMass_le_one {E : Finset ℕ} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hE : ∀ d ∈ E, 2 ≤ d) (habove : (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue E) (hfrac : localFractionMass E M ≤ 1) : 2 ^ (M - 1) ≤ localPrefixQuotient E M
declarations.docstring: A scaled prefix which is already above one half must have reached the integral half target as soon as its total fractional mass is at most one. This is the general carry statement behind the skipped-core socket below: failure of the integral carry can only happen when more than one full unit is hidden in the sum of the individual Mersenne residues.

declarations.name: localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_of_insertFractionMass
declarations.signature: theorem localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_of_insertFractionMass {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hcross : (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert c D)) (hfrac : localFractionMass (insert c D) (2 * c - 2) ≤ 1) : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)
declarations.docstring: For a crossing skipped core, the sharp `c-2`-bit repair capacity follows from the single residue estimate that the inserted support carries at most one unit of total fractional mass at endpoint `2c-2`.

declarations.name: localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_of_splitFractionMass
declarations.signature: theorem localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_criticalCapacity_of_splitFractionMass {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hcross : (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert c D)) (hfrac : localFractionMass D (2 * c - 2) + localMersenneFraction (2 * c - 2) c ≤ 1) : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)
declarations.docstring: The same sufficient condition split into the old core residue mass and the newly inserted rank. This isolates a useful analytic subcase; the one-unit bound is not asserted for every crossing core.

declarations.name: one_lt_splitFractionMass_of_criticalCapacity_failure
declarations.signature: theorem one_lt_splitFractionMass_of_criticalCapacity_failure {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hcross : (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert c D)) (hfail : ¬ localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)) : 1 < localFractionMass D (2 * c - 2) + localMersenneFraction (2 * c - 2) c
declarations.docstring: Consequently, failure of the sharp capacity at an actual crossing forces strictly more than one unit of fractional residue mass. This records the precise analytic obstruction without assuming that it can occur.

declarations.name: splitFractionMass_one_bound_not_necessary_fixture
declarations.signature: theorem splitFractionMass_one_bound_not_necessary_fixture : localMersennePrefixValue ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) < (1 / 2 : ℚ) ∧ (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) ∧ 1 < localFractionMass ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 8 + localMersenneFraction 8 5 ∧ localBinarySuffix ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 1 8 < 2 ^ 3
declarations.docstring: The one-unit fractional-mass hypothesis is sufficient, but not necessary. At the genuine crossing `D = {2,3}`, `c = 5`, the combined residue mass is already greater than one while the sharp critical capacity still holds.

declarations.name: localMersenneQuotient_two_mul_sub_two_self
declarations.signature: theorem localMersenneQuotient_two_mul_sub_two_self {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) : localMersenneQuotient (2 * c - 2) c = 2 ^ (c - 2)
declarations.docstring: At row `2c - 2`, the integral quotient of the rank-`c` Mersenne weight is the largest power strictly below the upper-half window.

declarations.name: localMersenneFraction_lt_one_skippedCore
declarations.signature: theorem localMersenneFraction_lt_one_skippedCore {M d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : localMersenneFraction M d < 1
declarations.docstring: Every local Mersenne residue is below one. This local copy keeps the skipped-core producer independent of the later global-repair consumer.

declarations.name: localFractionMass_le_card_skippedCore
declarations.signature: theorem localFractionMass_le_card_skippedCore {D : Finset ℕ} {M : ℕ} (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d) : localFractionMass D M ≤ (D.card : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: The residue mass of a Boolean core is at most its cardinality.

declarations.name: card_le_sub_two_of_mem_lt
declarations.signature: theorem card_le_sub_two_of_mem_lt {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) : D.card ≤ c - 2
declarations.docstring: A support contained in the integer interval `[2,c)` has at most `c-2` elements.

declarations.name: localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_upperHalfCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem localBinarySuffix_two_mul_sub_two_lt_upperHalfCapacity {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hskip : (1 / 2 : ℚ) - localMersennePrefixValue D < mersenneWeightRat c) : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Skipped-core upper-half capacity.** If `D ⊆ [2,c)` lies below one half and the missing mass is smaller than the rank-`c` Mersenne weight, then the exact binary suffix at row `2c-2` fits strictly in `c-1` bits. The proof is the finite identity `A = 2^M (1/2 - value(D)) + fractionalMass(D,M) - 1` with `M=2c-2`. The first term is below `2^(c-2)+1`, while the fractional mass is at most `|D| ≤ c-2 ≤ 2^(c-2)`.

declarations.name: exists_upperHalfBooleanWord_of_skippedCore
declarations.signature: theorem exists_upperHalfBooleanWord_of_skippedCore {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hskip : (1 / 2 : ℚ) - localMersennePrefixValue D < mersenneWeightRat c) : ∃ y : List ℕ, y.length = c - 1 ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ Nat.ofDigits 2 y = localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2)
declarations.docstring: The skipped-core suffix therefore has an exact Boolean word of the whole upper-half width.

declarations.name: halfSkippedPrefix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def halfSkippedPrefix (M : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The skipped exponents visible through level `M`.

declarations.name: finiteMersenneShift
declarations.signature: noncomputable def finiteMersenneShift (F : Finset ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne-rational shift carried by a finite set of exponents.

declarations.name: IsLastHalfGreedySkip
declarations.docstring: `M` is the final exponent skipped by the actual greedy half orbit.

declarations.name: isLastHalfGreedySkip_pos
declarations.signature: theorem isLastHalfGreedySkip_pos {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : 0 < M

declarations.name: coe_halfSkippedPrefix_eq_skippedSupport
declarations.signature: theorem coe_halfSkippedPrefix_eq_skippedSupport {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : (↑(halfSkippedPrefix M) : Set ℕ) = greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (1 / 2 : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Under a last-skip hypothesis, the finite prefix is the complete skipped support.

declarations.name: finiteMersenneShift_eq_cast_finiteErdosSum
declarations.signature: theorem finiteMersenneShift_eq_cast_finiteErdosSum (F : Finset ℕ) : finiteMersenneShift F = ((finiteErdosSum F 2 : ℚ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A finite Mersenne shift is visibly rational.

declarations.name: halfGreedySupportSuffix_eq_tail_of_lastSkip
declarations.signature: theorem halfGreedySupportSuffix_eq_tail_of_lastSkip {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 2 : ℝ)) M = mersenneTail M
declarations.docstring: After a last skip, every term in the remaining suffix is selected.

declarations.name: halfGreedySupportValue_eq_prefix_add_tail_of_lastSkip
declarations.signature: theorem halfGreedySupportValue_eq_prefix_add_tail_of_lastSkip {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : positiveMersenneSupportValue (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 2 : ℝ)) = halfGreedyMersennePrefix M + mersenneTail M
declarations.docstring: The full selected value is the finite selected prefix plus the complete tail after a last skip.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_eq_remainder_sub_tail
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_eq_remainder_sub_tail {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) + finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant = greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) M - mersenneTail M
declarations.docstring: Exact fatal coordinate: the finite-shift displacement is the residual excess above the remaining tail.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_remainder_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_remainder_lt_weight {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) M < mersenneWeight M
declarations.docstring: The last skipped branch leaves the level-`M` residual below `w_M`.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_tail_le_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_tail_le_remainder {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : mersenneTail M ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) M
declarations.docstring: After a last skip the greedy orbit selects every later exponent, so the partial tail sums telescope inside the level-`M` residual: the complete tail is at most the residual.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_nonneg {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : 0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) + finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant
declarations.docstring: The finite-shift displacement is nonnegative for a last skip.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shiftDelta_ne_zero {M : ℕ} (_hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) + finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Irrationality excludes equality at the rational centre of the shifted fatal interval.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shift_fatalInterval
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shift_fatalInterval {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : 0 < (1 / 2 : ℝ) + finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant ∧ (1 / 2 : ℝ) + finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant < mersenneGap M
declarations.docstring: Exact one-sided fatal interval around the rational shift determined by a putative last skip.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shadow_mem_gap
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shadow_mem_gap {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : |halfGreedyMersenneShadow (M - 1) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant| < mersenneGap M
declarations.docstring: The `M-1` shadow uses the same gap as the last skipped exponent `M`. This theorem is the exact index reconciliation for the death-hole picture.

declarations.name: mersenneGap_lt_quarterPow
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneGap_lt_quarterPow {M : ℕ} (hM : 3 ≤ M) : mersenneGap M < ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ M
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne gap is already smaller than the depth-`2M` dyadic scale for `M ≥ 3`.

declarations.name: lastHalfSkip_shifted_mem_dyadicCylinder
declarations.signature: theorem lastHalfSkip_shifted_mem_dyadicCylinder {M : ℕ} (hM : 3 ≤ M) (hlast : IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) - ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ M < erdosBorweinMersenneConstant - finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) ∧ erdosBorweinMersenneConstant - finiteMersenneShift (halfSkippedPrefix M) < (1 / 2 : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A last skip puts the shifted constant inside the depth-`2M` cylinder immediately below `1 / 2`.

declarations.name: campbellQuarterExponent_periodFreeze_noSync
declarations.signature: theorem campbellQuarterExponent_periodFreeze_noSync {d t P : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (htd : t ≤ d) (hP : P ≤ 4 * t) (hAGP : d ^ 4 ≤ P) : False
declarations.docstring: If `d` is the combined prime-progression modulus, `t` is the unavoidable phase factor, and `P` is the prime cap forced by the fatal window, Campbell's quarter-exponent applicability condition is impossible.

declarations.name: campbellPhaseFreeze_parameters_impossible
declarations.signature: theorem campbellPhaseFreeze_parameters_impossible {M q0sq t d P : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q0sq) (htpos : 0 < t) (hd : 2 ≤ d) (ht : M ≤ t * q0sq) (htd : t ≤ d) (hwindow : P * q0sq ≤ 2 * M + 2) (hAGP : d ^ 4 ≤ P) : False
declarations.docstring: Substrate-native parameter map. The hypotheses expose exactly where a future analytic construction must improve: the phase-period factor `t`, the fatal-window cap `P`, or the sublinear modulus exponent.

declarations.name: four_mem_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_half
declarations.docstring: Exponent four is already skipped by the exact greedy recursion. This small evaluator fixes the positive-index convention used by the last-skip endpoint below.

declarations.name: exists_isLastHalfGreedySkip_iff_skippedSupport_finite
declarations.signature: theorem exists_isLastHalfGreedySkip_iff_skippedSupport_finite : (∃ M : ℕ, IsLastHalfGreedySkip M) ↔ (greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (1 / 2 : ℝ)).Finite
declarations.docstring: A final skipped exponent exists exactly when the actual skipped support is finite. Nonemptiness is unconditional because exponent four is skipped.

declarations.name: existsFatalHalfGap_iff_exists_isLastHalfGreedySkip
declarations.signature: theorem existsFatalHalfGap_iff_exists_isLastHalfGreedySkip : ExistsFatalHalfGap ↔ ∃ M : ℕ, IsLastHalfGreedySkip M
declarations.docstring: The cut-locator's arbitrary-word fatal branch is now identified with the canonical dynamical endpoint: it occurs exactly when the actual greedy orbit has a final skipped exponent.

declarations.name: GreedyShiftWindowZero
declarations.docstring: The last-skip-guarded shifted-window interface. Under a putative last skip `M ≥ 3`, the complete finite shift is required to lie outside the all-one depth-`2M` cylinder. The equivalence theorem below shows that this guarded formulation is an endpoint restatement, not an independent arithmetic producer.

declarations.name: not_isLastHalfGreedySkip_of_shiftWindowZero
declarations.signature: theorem not_isLastHalfGreedySkip_of_shiftWindowZero (hzero : GreedyShiftWindowZero) {M : ℕ} (hM : 3 ≤ M) : ¬ IsLastHalfGreedySkip M
declarations.docstring: The shifted-zero producer rules out a final skipped exponent.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_infinite_of_shiftWindowZero
declarations.docstring: The shifted-zero producer forces infinitely many actual skips.

declarations.name: shiftWindowZero_of_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_infinite
declarations.docstring: Infinitely many skipped exponents make the last-skip hypothesis in the shifted-window producer impossible. This closes the converse logical direction without adding any analytic input: the genuine arithmetic content of `GreedyShiftWindowZero` is exactly the exclusion of a final skip.

declarations.name: shiftWindowZero_iff_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_infinite
declarations.docstring: Exact endpoint classification of the Campbell-shift interface. It is equivalent to infinitude of the actual greedy skipped support, rather than a strictly weaker producer waiting for a separate composition theorem.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_shiftWindowZero
declarations.docstring: Composition with the checked greedy endpoint yields exact half membership once the shifted-zero producer is supplied.

declarations.name: shiftWindowZero_iff_half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: The shifted-window formulation is exactly equivalent to the concrete half-achievement endpoint.

declarations.name: totientTail_pos
declarations.docstring: The local totient tail is strictly positive.

declarations.name: totientTail_le
declarations.signature: lemma totientTail_le (M : ℕ) : totientTail M ≤ (M : ℝ) + 2
declarations.docstring: `R_M ≤ M + 2`: the window bound at depth `0`.

declarations.name: abs_tail_diff_lt
declarations.signature: lemma abs_tail_diff_lt (h N : ℕ) : |totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N| < (N : ℝ) + h + 2
declarations.docstring: The tail difference `D_h(N) = R_{N+h} - R_N` is trapped in the open strip `|D_h(N)| < N + h + 2`.

declarations.name: totientTail_succ
declarations.signature: lemma totientTail_succ (M : ℕ) : totientTail (M + 1) = 2 * totientTail M - (Nat.totient (M + 1) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Carry recurrence.** `R_{M+1} = 2·R_M - φ(M+1)`: doubling the tail shifts the window by one and expels the head totient.

declarations.name: totientTail_eq_partial_add_shifted
declarations.signature: lemma totientTail_eq_partial_add_shifted (M L : ℕ) : totientTail M = (∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, (Nat.totient (M + 1 + j) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (j + 1)) + totientTail (M + L) / 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: **Exact tail-window split.** The first `L` binary digits of `R_M` are the finite window already used by the certificate kernel; the remaining endpoint is exactly `2⁻ᴸ R_{M+L}`. This is the general coboundary identity behind every later sliding-suffix specialization.

declarations.name: deltaTotient
declarations.docstring: The window step `a_n = φ(n+h) - φ(n)` driving the carry recurrence.

declarations.name: abs_deltaTotient_le
declarations.signature: lemma abs_deltaTotient_le (h n : ℕ) : |deltaTotient h n| ≤ (n + h : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: The fresh totient forcing letter is bounded by its later argument. This is the arithmetic input that makes the depth barrier strict: at depth `L` the new letter has size at most `N + h + L + 1`, one less than the endpoint corridor radius.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_succ
declarations.signature: lemma windowDiscrepancy_succ (h N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N (L + 1) = 2 * windowDiscrepancy h N L + deltaTotient h (N + L + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Exact depth recurrence for the endpoint word.** Increasing certificate depth doubles the existing signed window and appends exactly one fresh totient-difference letter. This is a depth recurrence with explicit input, not the autonomous temporal recurrence ruled out by the finite-state no-go.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_slide
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_slide (h N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h (N + 1) L = 2 * windowDiscrepancy h N L - deltaTotient h (N + 1) * 2 ^ L + deltaTotient h (N + L + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Exact spatial recurrence for a fixed-depth window.** Sliding the base from `N` to `N+1` expels the head letter with weight `2^L`, doubles the old window, and appends one fresh endpoint letter. Modulo `2^L` only the doubled residue and the fresh endpoint remain. The natural bound `abs_deltaTotient_le` already places that endpoint inside the certificate corridor, so this identity alone is not a one-step anti-trapping theorem.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_succ
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_succ {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : certifiedKill h N (L + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Depth barrier.** Once an endpoint certificate fires, every deeper window fires as well. The proof uses the exact input-driven recurrence and the strict totient bound; no finite state or empirical residue table enters. Equivalently, endpoint survival is prefix-closed in certificate depth.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_add
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_add {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : ∀ k : ℕ, certifiedKill h N (L + k)
declarations.docstring: A successful depth is an absorbing proof state: appending any finite suffix of the totient forcing word cannot recreate an endpoint survivor.

declarations.name: endpointSurvivor
declarations.signature: def endpointSurvivor (h N L : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The signed endpoint-survivor fibre at depth `L`. Its elements are the integer representatives of the exact discrepancy residue that still fit in the analytic endpoint corridor.

declarations.name: no_endpointSurvivor_of_certifiedKill
declarations.signature: theorem no_endpointSurvivor_of_certifiedKill {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : ∀ z : ℤ, ¬ endpointSurvivor h N L z
declarations.docstring: A central-arc certificate empties the signed endpoint-survivor fibre.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_no_endpointSurvivor
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_no_endpointSurvivor {h N L : ℕ} (hroom : (2 * (N + h + L + 2) : ℤ) < 2 ^ L) (hempty : ∀ z : ℤ, ¬ endpointSurvivor h N L z) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Under the natural dyadic-room condition, fibre emptiness is not merely a consequence of `certifiedKill`: it is exactly the central-arc certificate.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_iff_endpointSurvivor_empty
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_iff_endpointSurvivor_empty {h N L : ℕ} (hroom : (2 * (N + h + L + 2) : ℤ) < 2 ^ L) : certifiedKill h N L ↔ ∀ z : ℤ, ¬ endpointSurvivor h N L z
declarations.docstring: Paper-facing form of the survivor-kernel bridge: once the depth floor is available, `certifiedKill` is equivalent to exact emptiness of the signed endpoint fibre.

declarations.name: tail_diff_succ
declarations.signature: lemma tail_diff_succ (h M : ℕ) : totientTail (M + 1 + h) - totientTail (M + 1) = 2 * (totientTail (M + h) - totientTail M) - (deltaTotient h (M + 1) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The tail difference obeys the exact carry recurrence `D_h(M+1) = 2·D_h(M) - a_{M+1}`.

declarations.name: tail_diff_eq_increment_prefix_add_shifted
declarations.signature: lemma tail_diff_eq_increment_prefix_add_shifted (h N L : ℕ) : totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N = (∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, (deltaTotient h (N + 1 + j) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (j + 1)) + (totientTail (N + L + h) - totientTail (N + L)) / 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: **Exact endpoint telescoping for every tail difference.** The first `L` dyadic digits are the signed increment prefix, and the only remainder is the translated tail difference scaled by `2⁻ᴸ`. On the LCM diagonal this is the dyadic-cocycle collapse: sliding a suffix exposes no independent arithmetic sample beyond the original carry orbit.

declarations.name: carryOrbit
declarations.signature: def carryOrbit (h N : ℕ) (d : ℤ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => d | i + 1 => 2 * carryOrbit h N d i - deltaTotient h (N + i + 1) /-- **Orbit tracking.** If the tail difference at `N` is the integer `d`, the carry orbit computes the exact tail-difference sequence: `orbit i = D_h(N+i)`. -/ lemma carryOrbit_eq_tail_diff {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N) (i : ℕ) : (carryOrbit h N d i : ℝ) = totientTail (N + i + h) - totientTail (N + i)
declarations.docstring: The integer carry orbit launched from candidate `d` at position `N`: `orbit 0 = d`, `orbit (i+1) = 2·orbit i - a_{N+i+1}`. If `D_h(N)` is the integer `d`, this orbit equals `D_h(N+i)` forever.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_eq_tail_diff
declarations.signature: lemma carryOrbit_eq_tail_diff {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N) (i : ℕ) : (carryOrbit h N d i : ℝ) = totientTail (N + i + h) - totientTail (N + i)
declarations.docstring: **Orbit tracking.** If the tail difference at `N` is the integer `d`, the carry orbit computes the exact tail-difference sequence: `orbit i = D_h(N+i)`.

declarations.name: survivorKill
declarations.signature: def survivorKill (h N K : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The **carry-survivor certificate**: every integer candidate in the initial box `|d| ≤ N+h+1` — enumerated as `d = j - (N+h+1)` for `j < 2·(N+h+1)+1` — provably escapes the strip `|·| ≤ N+i+h+1` within `K` steps (escape stated as a two-sided disjunction). Finitely many candidates, finitely many steps: decidable.

declarations.name: tail_diff_notMem_int_of_survivorKill
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_notMem_int_of_survivorKill {h N K : ℕ} (hkill : survivorKill h N K) : totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Survivor soundness.** A survivor kill proves the tail difference is not an integer: an integer value `d` would launch an integer carry orbit equal to the true tail-difference sequence, which stays inside the strip `|D_h(N+i)| < N+i+h+2` forever — but the certificate says every candidate provably escapes within `K` steps. This is the machine-checked form of the wave-21 bounded-orbit reformulation.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mul
declarations.signature: lemma tail_diff_mul (h N m : ℕ) : totientTail (N + m * h) - totientTail N = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range m, (totientTail (N + i * h + h) - totientTail (N + i * h))
declarations.docstring: **Period-ray telescoping.** The `m·h` tail difference is the sum of `m` translated `h` tail differences: integrality flows down every multiple.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mul_mem_int
declarations.signature: lemma tail_diff_mul_mem_int {h N₀ : ℕ} (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) (m N : ℕ) (hN : N₀ ≤ N) : totientTail (N + m * h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Integrality propagates down every period ray: if every `h`-difference from `N₀` on is an integer, so is every `m·h`-difference.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_multiple_survivor_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_multiple_survivor_supply (hsupply : ∀ h₀ : ℕ, 0 < h₀ → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ m, 0 < m ∧ ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ∃ K, survivorKill (m * h₀) N K) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **The wave-22 reduction: multiple-period survivor supply.** The weakest supply hypothesis in the ladder so far: for every primitive period `h₀` it suffices to certify a survivor kill along ANY multiple `m·h₀`, at arbitrarily large `N`. Rationality forces integrality along the whole period ray, so one dead multiple kills the primitive.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_multiple_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_multiple_certificate_supply (hsupply : ∀ h₀ : ℕ, 0 < h₀ → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ m, 0 < m ∧ ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill (m * h₀) N L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The endpoint-certificate variant of the multiple-period reduction: one certified window kill along any multiple of each primitive period suffices.

declarations.docstring: **One-parameter collapse of the throat.** Survivor kills along the single family `lcm(1..t)` — arbitrarily large `t`, arbitrarily large `N` — prove #249. Rationality would give SOME period `h₀`; every `h₀ ≤ t` divides `lcm(1..t)`, so the whole `∀ h₀` obligation lands on one ℕ-indexed ray.

declarations.name: coprime_base_reducedDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_base_reducedDenominator (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Nat.Coprime b (reducedDenominator F b)

declarations.name: finite_period_noncollapse
declarations.signature: theorem finite_period_noncollapse (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : orderOf (ZMod.unitOfCoprime b (coprime_base_reducedDenominator F b h0 hb)) = F.lcm id
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional finite period non-collapse.** For every finite nonempty set `F` of positive exponents and every base `b ≥ 2`, the reduced denominator `Q` of `∑_{n ∈ F} 1 / (b ^ n - 1)` satisfies `ord_Q(b) = lcm F`. No witness-supply hypothesis remains: exact-order prime-power witnesses are constructed for every selector row via the cyclotomic route.

declarations.name: pow_sub_one_pos_of_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem pow_sub_one_pos_of_ne_zero (b n : Nat) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hn : n ≠ 0) : 0 < b ^ n - 1
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional finite period non-collapse.** For every finite nonempty set `F` of positive exponents and every base `b ≥ 2`, the reduced denominator `Q` of `∑_{n ∈ F} 1 / (b ^ n - 1)` satisfies `ord_Q(b) = lcm F`. No witness-supply hypothesis remains: exact-order prime-power witnesses are constructed for every selector row via the cyclotomic route. -/ theorem finite_period_noncollapse (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : orderOf (ZMod.unitOfCoprime b (coprime_base_reducedDenominator F b h0 hb)) = F.lcm id := by refine finite_period_noncollapse_from_exact_order_witness_supply F (F.lcm id) (commonNumerator F b) (commonDenominator F b) (reducedDenominator F b) b (coprime_base_reducedDenominator F b h0 hb) hF h0 hb rfl rfl rfl rfl ?_ intro n _ hn2 _ exact exists_exactOrderPrimePowerWitness hb hn2 /-! ## Rational-denominator bridge and denominator growth The unconditional theorem above speaks about `reducedDenominator F b`, a `Nat`-valued construction. T

declarations.name: natCast_pow_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem natCast_pow_sub_one (b n : Nat) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ((b ^ n - 1 : Nat) : Rat) = (b : Rat) ^ n - 1

declarations.name: finiteErdosSum
declarations.signature: def finiteErdosSum (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) : Rat
declarations.docstring: The finite Erdős partial sum `∑_{n ∈ F} 1 / (b ^ n - 1)` as a rational number, stated with subtraction in `ℚ` so the statement reads exactly like the mathematical series.

declarations.name: lcm_ne_zero_of_zero_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_ne_zero_of_zero_not_mem (F : Finset Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) : F.lcm id ≠ 0

declarations.name: finiteErdosSum_eq_commonNumerator_div_commonDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem finiteErdosSum_eq_commonNumerator_div_commonDenominator (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : finiteErdosSum F b = (commonNumerator F b : Rat) / (commonDenominator F b : Rat)
declarations.docstring: The rational partial sum equals the audited common fraction `commonNumerator / commonDenominator`.

declarations.name: den_natCast_div_natCast_of_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem den_natCast_div_natCast_of_coprime (x y : Nat) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hcop : Nat.Coprime x y) : ((x : Rat) / (y : Rat)).den = y
declarations.docstring: Denominator of a quotient of coprime naturals.

declarations.name: mul_div_cross_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem mul_div_cross_of_dvd (g a d : Nat) (hg : 0 < g) (ha : g ∣ a) (hd : g ∣ d) : a * (d / g) = a / g * d

declarations.name: den_natCast_div_natCast
declarations.signature: theorem den_natCast_div_natCast (a d : Nat) (hd : d ≠ 0) : ((a : Rat) / (d : Rat)).den = d / Nat.gcd a d
declarations.docstring: Denominator of a quotient of naturals, via the gcd.

declarations.name: finiteErdosSum_den_eq_reducedDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem finiteErdosSum_den_eq_reducedDenominator (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : (finiteErdosSum F b).den = reducedDenominator F b
declarations.docstring: **Statement-faithfulness bridge.** The audited `reducedDenominator F b` is literally `Rat.den` of the rational partial sum `∑_{n ∈ F} 1 / (b^n - 1)`: the theorem about the constructed denominator is a theorem about the actual reduced denominator of the actual rational number.

declarations.name: coprime_base_den_finiteErdosSum
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_base_den_finiteErdosSum (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Nat.Coprime b (finiteErdosSum F b).den

declarations.name: finite_period_noncollapse_concrete
declarations.signature: theorem finite_period_noncollapse_concrete (F : Finset Nat) (b L Q : Nat) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hL : L = F.lcm id) (hQ : Q = reducedDenominator F b) (hcop : Nat.Coprime b Q) : orderOf (ZMod.unitOfCoprime b hcop) = L
declarations.docstring: Concrete-transport wrapper: the unconditional theorem restated over any naturals `L`, `Q` proven equal to `lcm F` and the reduced denominator. This is the thin interface a theorem-route certificate emitter instantiates: a generated target supplies `F`, `b`, the two normalisation equalities, and a coprimality witness, and receives the exact-order conclusion with no per-prime witness rows.

declarations.name: finite_period_noncollapse_rat_den
declarations.signature: theorem finite_period_noncollapse_rat_den (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : orderOf (ZMod.unitOfCoprime b (coprime_base_den_finiteErdosSum F b h0 hb)) = F.lcm id
declarations.docstring: The unconditional finite theorem stated over `Rat.den` of the literal rational partial sum: `ord_Q(b) = lcm F` where `Q` is the denominator in lowest terms of `∑_{n ∈ F} 1 / (b ^ n - 1)` as a rational number.

declarations.name: lcm_lt_den_finiteErdosSum
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_lt_den_finiteErdosSum (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (h2 : 2 ≤ F.lcm id) : F.lcm id < (finiteErdosSum F b).den
declarations.docstring: **Denominator growth.** The reduced denominator of the finite Erdős partial sum strictly dominates `lcm F`: since `ord_Q(b) = lcm F` and the order divides `φ(Q) < Q`, the denominator can never collapse below the lcm. This is the quantitative engine an irrationality attack on the infinite series needs from the finite layer.

declarations.name: lcm_Icc_lt_den_erdosPartialSum
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_Icc_lt_den_erdosPartialSum (b N : Nat) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hN : 2 ≤ N) : (Finset.Icc 1 N).lcm id < (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, 1 / ((b : Rat) ^ n - 1)).den
declarations.docstring: **Denominator growth for the classical partial sums.** For every base `b ≥ 2` and every `N ≥ 2`, the reduced denominator of `∑_{n=1}^{N} 1 / (b ^ n - 1)` strictly exceeds `lcm(1, …, N)`. Stated in pure Mathlib vocabulary: no project-local definition appears in the statement.

declarations.name: strictMono_add_le_apply
declarations.signature: theorem strictMono_add_le_apply {a : ℕ → ℕ} (ha : StrictMono a) (k i : ℕ) : a k + i ≤ a (k + i)
declarations.docstring: A strictly monotone `ℕ`-sequence gains at least one per step: `a k + i ≤ a (k + i)`.

declarations.name: one_div_den_mul_den_le_abs_sub
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_den_mul_den_le_abs_sub {q r : ℚ} (h : q ≠ r) : (1 : ℝ) / ((q.den : ℝ) * (r.den : ℝ)) ≤ |(q : ℝ) - (r : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: **Rational gap.** Two distinct rationals are at least `1 / (den · den)` apart as real numbers.

declarations.name: irrational_of_den_mul_abs_sub_tendsto_zero
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_of_den_mul_abs_sub_tendsto_zero {x : ℝ} {u : ℕ → ℚ} (hne : ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ((u k : ℝ)) ≠ x) (h0 : Tendsto (fun k => ((u k).den : ℝ) * |x - (u k : ℝ)|) atTop (nhds 0)) : Irrational x
declarations.docstring: **Irrationality criterion.** If a sequence of rationals is eventually never equal to `x` and `den(u k) * |x - u k| → 0`, then `x` is irrational. This is the Dirichlet-gap argument stated over `Rat.den` — the same denominator object the finite kernel theorems audit.

declarations.name: den_finiteErdosSum_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem den_finiteErdosSum_dvd (F : Finset Nat) (b : Nat) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : (finiteErdosSum F b).den ∣ b ^ (F.lcm id) - 1
declarations.docstring: The reduced denominator of the finite Erdős partial sum divides the common denominator `b ^ lcm F - 1`.

declarations.name: summable_erdos_term
declarations.signature: theorem summable_erdos_term (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) : Summable (fun k => (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a k) - 1))
declarations.docstring: Summability of the Erdős terms along any strictly monotone support with positive first element.

declarations.name: summable_erdos_term_shift
declarations.signature: theorem summable_erdos_term_shift (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) (k : ℕ) : Summable (fun i => (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a (i + k)) - 1))
declarations.docstring: The shifted-tail terms are summable.

declarations.name: erdos_term_pos
declarations.signature: theorem erdos_term_pos (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a j) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Positivity of every Erdős term.

declarations.name: erdos_tail_pos
declarations.signature: theorem erdos_tail_pos (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) (k : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) < ∑' i, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a (i + k)) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The tail after `k` terms is strictly positive.

declarations.name: erdos_tail_le
declarations.signature: theorem erdos_tail_le (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) (k : ℕ) : ∑' i, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a (i + k)) - 1) ≤ 4 * ((1 : ℝ) / b) ^ (a k)
declarations.docstring: Geometric tail estimate: the tail after `k` terms is at most `4 * (1/b) ^ (a k)`.

declarations.name: finiteErdosSum_image_range_cast
declarations.signature: theorem finiteErdosSum_image_range_cast (b : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (k : ℕ) : ((finiteErdosSum ((Finset.range k).image a) b : ℚ) : ℝ) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a i) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Casting the finite Erdős sum over the image support to the reals gives the real partial sum.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha0 : 1 ≤ a 0) (hgap : Tendsto (fun k => a k - ((Finset.range k).image a).lcm id) atTop atTop) : Irrational (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (a k) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Infinite bridge, class form.** For every base `b ≥ 2` and every strictly monotone support `a` with `a 0 ≥ 1`, if the gap between `a k` and `lcm {a 0, …, a (k-1)}` tends to infinity, then the infinite series `∑ 1 / (b ^ (a k) - 1)` is irrational. The reduced denominators of the partial sums — the objects the finite kernel theorems audit — are the `q` of the Dirichlet gap argument.

declarations.name: lcm_image_factorial_succ
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_image_factorial_succ (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : ((Finset.range k).image (fun i => Nat.factorial (i + 1))).lcm id = Nat.factorial k
declarations.docstring: lcm of the factorial support prefix `{1!, …, k!}` is `k!`.

declarations.name: lcm_image_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_image_two_pow (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : ((Finset.range k).image (fun i => 2 ^ i)).lcm id = 2 ^ (k - 1)
declarations.docstring: lcm of the two-power support prefix `{2^0, …, 2^(k-1)}` is `2^(k-1)`.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_factorial_support
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_factorial_support (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Irrational (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (Nat.factorial (k + 1)) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **First infinite-support instance: factorial support.** For every base `b ≥ 2`, the infinite series `∑_{k≥0} 1 / (b ^ (k+1)! - 1)` is irrational. Stated in pure Mathlib vocabulary. The support `{n! : n ≥ 1}` is not pairwise coprime (each factorial divides the next), so this instance is outside the classical coprime-support family.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_two_pow_support
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_two_pow_support (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Irrational (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (2 ^ k) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **First infinite-support instance: geometric support.** For every base `b ≥ 2`, the infinite series `∑_{k≥0} 1 / (b ^ (2^k) - 1)` is irrational. The gap `2^k - lcm = 2^(k-1)` has bounded ratio to the lcm, so this instance is *not* reachable by a Liouville-number shortcut; the denominator-gap criterion handles it uniformly.

declarations.name: erdos257_family_factorial_instance
declarations.signature: theorem erdos257_family_factorial_instance : Irrational (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (Nat.factorial (k + 1)) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Erdős #257 family, factorial instance at base 2.** The literal series `∑ 1 / (2^(n!) - 1)` over the infinite support `A = {n! : n ≥ 1}` is irrational. This is an instance of the statement family of Erdős problem #257 (which asks the same for *every* infinite support); the universal problem remains open and is not claimed.

declarations.name: erdos257_family_two_pow_instance
declarations.signature: theorem erdos257_family_two_pow_instance : Irrational (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (2 ^ k) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Erdős #257 family, geometric instance at base 2.** The literal series `∑ 1 / (2^(2^n) - 1)` over the infinite support `A = {2^n : n ≥ 0}` is irrational. An instance of the #257 statement family; the universal problem remains open and is not claimed.

declarations.name: irrational_of_int_mul_near_int
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_of_int_mul_near_int {ξ : ℝ} (h : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ m z : ℤ, 0 < |(m : ℝ) * ξ - (z : ℝ)| ∧ |(m : ℝ) * ξ - (z : ℝ)| < 1 / (q : ℝ)) : Irrational ξ
declarations.docstring: **Second irrationality engine: integer-dilation near-integer criterion.** If for every positive `q` some integer dilation `m * ξ` lies within `1 / q` of an integer without being one, then `ξ` is irrational. For rational `ξ` with reduced denominator `d`, any `m * ξ` that is not an integer sits at distance at least `1 / d` from every integer, so the witnesses force the reduced denominator past every bound. This is the classical criterion shape behind digit/carry irrationality proofs (Erdős 1948).

declarations.name: irrational_of_pow_mul_near_int
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_of_pow_mul_near_int (b : ℕ) {ξ : ℝ} (h : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ), 0 < |(b : ℝ) ^ n * ξ - (z : ℝ)| ∧ |(b : ℝ) ^ n * ξ - (z : ℝ)| < 1 / (q : ℝ)) : Irrational ξ
declarations.docstring: Base-power specialisation of the near-integer criterion: witnesses of the form `b ^ n * ξ` suffice. This is the interface a digit/carry construction in base `b` feeds.

declarations.name: summable_divisor_count_term
declarations.signature: theorem summable_divisor_count_term (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Summable (fun m : ℕ => (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1))
declarations.docstring: Summability of the divisor-count series `∑ τ(m+1) / b^(m+1)`: `τ(n) ≤ n` and `∑ n · r^n` converges geometrically.

declarations.name: erdosSum_full_support_eq_tsum_divisor_count
declarations.signature: theorem erdosSum_full_support_eq_tsum_divisor_count (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1) = ∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Full-support Lambert bridge.** For every base `b ≥ 2`, the full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (b^n - 1)` equals the divisor-count series `∑_{m≥1} τ(m) / b^m`. This is the classical Lambert-series identity (Mathlib's `tsum_pow_div_one_sub_eq_tsum_sigma` at `k = 0`, `r = 1/b`), restated in the kernel's own series vocabulary: the left side is the `a k = k + 1` (full-support) member of the Erdős #257 statement family — the Erdős–Borwein shape.

declarations.name: erdosBorwein_constant_lambert_identity
declarations.signature: theorem erdosBorwein_constant_lambert_identity : ∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1) = ∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (2 : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Erdős–Borwein constant, Lambert form.** The literal base-2 full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (2^n - 1)` — the Erdős–Borwein constant, the `A = ℕ` member of the Erdős #257 statement family — equals the divisor-count series `∑_{m≥1} τ(m) / 2^m`.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_near_int
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_near_int (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (h : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ), 0 < |(b : ℝ) ^ n * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| ∧ |(b : ℝ) ^ n * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| < 1 / (q : ℝ)) : Irrational (∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Reduction of full-support (Erdős–Borwein) irrationality to near-integer witnesses.** For every base `b ≥ 2`: if the divisor-count series `∑ τ(m) / b^m` admits, for every `q`, a base-power dilation lying within `1/q` of an integer without being one, then the full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (b^n - 1)` is irrational. The hypothesis is exactly the obligation Erdős's 1948 congruence construction discharges; producing those witnesses in Lean is the named remaining step of the full-support lane, and is *not* claimed here.

declarations.name: lcm_gap_hypothesis_fails_full_support
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_gap_hypothesis_fails_full_support : ¬ Tendsto (fun k => (k + 1) - ((Finset.range k).image (fun i => i + 1)).lcm id) atTop atTop
declarations.docstring: **Machine-checked boundary: the lcm-gap criterion cannot fire on full support.** For the full support `a k = k + 1`, the prefix lcm `lcm {1, …, k}` contains the coprime pair `k - 1, k`, hence is at least `(k - 1) * k ≥ k + 2` for `k ≥ 3` — so the (truncated) gap `(k + 1) - lcm {1, …, k}` is eventually `0` and does not tend to infinity. The hypothesis of `irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap` therefore fails at full support: reaching the Erdős–Borwein case needs a different engine, which is what the near-integer criterion above provides the interface for.

declarations.name: summable_divisor_count_shift_tail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_divisor_count_shift_tail (b N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Summable (fun r : ℕ => (((N + r + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (r + 1))
declarations.docstring: Summability of the shifted divisor-count tail `∑_r τ(N+r+1) / b^(r+1)`: the `b^N`-dilated remainder series of the divisor-count series past index `N`.

declarations.name: bpow_mul_divisor_count_series_eq_int_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem bpow_mul_divisor_count_series_eq_int_add_tail (b N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∃ z : ℤ, (b : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) = (z : ℝ) + ∑' r : ℕ, (((N + r + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (r + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Shifted-tail decomposition.** Dilating the divisor-count series by `b^N` splits it into an integer (the first `N` terms clear their denominators) plus the shifted tail `∑_r τ(N+r+1) / b^(r+1)`. This is the base-`b` carry skeleton behind Erdős's 1948 argument.

declarations.name: summable_const_add_mul_geometric
declarations.signature: theorem summable_const_add_mul_geometric (C : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) : Summable (fun t : ℕ => ((C : ℝ) + (t : ℝ)) * x ^ t)
declarations.docstring: Summability of `(C + t) · x^t` for `0 ≤ x < 1`: a constant plus linear coefficient against a geometric envelope.

declarations.name: tsum_const_add_mul_geometric_le
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_const_add_mul_geometric_le (C : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx2 : x ≤ 1 / 2) : ∑' t : ℕ, ((C : ℝ) + (t : ℝ)) * x ^ t ≤ 2 * (C : ℝ) + 2
declarations.docstring: Geometric envelope bound: for `0 ≤ x ≤ 1/2`, `∑_t (C + t) · x^t ≤ 2C + 2` (equality at `x = 1/2`). The closed forms are `C/(1-x)` and `x/(1-x)^2`, each at most `2C` and `2` on this range.

declarations.name: divisor_count_far_tail_le
declarations.signature: theorem divisor_count_far_tail_le (b N L : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∑' t : ℕ, (((N + L + 1 + t).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (L + 1 + t) ≤ ((N + L + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (b : ℝ) ^ L
declarations.docstring: **Crude far-tail bound.** Past index `L`, bounding `τ(n) ≤ n` and summing the linear-times-geometric envelope gives `∑_t τ(N+L+1+t) / b^(L+1+t) ≤ (N+L+2) / b^L` for every base `b ≥ 2`. This is the certificate's third window: it needs no divisor information at all.

declarations.name: bpow_dvd_card_divisors_of_exact_prime_block
declarations.signature: theorem bpow_dvd_card_divisors_of_exact_prime_block (b n : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hn : n ≠ 0) (P : Finset ℕ) (hexact : ∀ p ∈ P, n.factorization p = b - 1) : b ^ P.card ∣ n.divisors.card
declarations.docstring: **Multiplicativity hinge for the first block.** If `P` is a set of primes at which `n` has exact valuation `b - 1`, then `b ^ |P|` divides `τ(n)`: each such prime contributes a factor `b` to `τ(n) = ∏_p (v_p(n) + 1)`. This is how Erdős's 1948 congruence construction forces the first-block divisibility — many small exact valuations, never one huge one.

declarations.name: near_int_witness_of_divisor_block_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem near_int_witness_of_divisor_block_certificate (b q N K L B : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hq : 0 < q) (hKL : K ≤ L) (hblock : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (N + r).divisors.card) (hmiddle : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card ≤ B) (harith : q * (B * b ^ (L - K) + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : ∃ z : ℤ, 0 < |(b : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| ∧ |(b : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| < 1 / (q : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Certificate consumer.** A divisor block certificate `(N, K, L, B)` for precision `q` — first-block divisibility, middle window bounded by `B`, and the ℕ-arithmetic inequality — yields a near-integer witness for the `b^N`-dilated divisor-count series: the first block lands in ℤ, the middle window contributes at most `B / b^K`, the far tail at most `(N+L+2) / b^L`, and the remainder is strictly positive because every divisor count is.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_block_certificates
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_block_certificates (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hcert : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L B : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (N + r).divisors.card) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card ≤ B) ∧ q * (B * b ^ (L - K) + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : Irrational (∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Full-support (Erdős–Borwein) irrationality from block certificates.** If for every precision `q` some divisor block certificate `(N, K, L, B)` exists, then the full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (b^n - 1)` is irrational. This composes the certificate consumer with the landed near-integer reduction: the remaining open obligation of the full-support lane is now the purely finite arithmetic statement that certificates exist for every `q` — which is what Erdős's 1948 congruence construction produces, and is NOT claimed here.

declarations.name: geom_sum_range_le_pow
declarations.signature: theorem geom_sum_range_le_pow (b m : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range m, b ^ j ≤ b ^ m
declarations.docstring: **Full-support (Erdős–Borwein) irrationality from block certificates.** If for every precision `q` some divisor block certificate `(N, K, L, B)` exists, then the full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (b^n - 1)` is irrational. This composes the certificate consumer with the landed near-integer reduction: the remaining open obligation of the full-support lane is now the purely finite arithmetic statement that certificates exist for every `q` — which is what Erdős's 1948 congruence construction produces, and is NOT claimed here. -/ theorem irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_block_certificates (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hcert : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L B : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (N + r).divisors.card) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card ≤ B) ∧ q * (B * b ^ (L - K) + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : Irrational (∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1)) := by refine irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_near_int b hb fun q hq => ?_ obtain ⟨N, K, L, B, hKL, hblock, hmiddle,

declarations.name: weighted_middle_bound_of_pointwise
declarations.signature: theorem weighted_middle_bound_of_pointwise (b N K L B : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hmiddle : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card ≤ B) : ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card * b ^ (L - r) ≤ B * b ^ (L - K)
declarations.docstring: **Weighted middle bound from the pointwise one.** A uniform bound `B` on the middle window gives `∑ τ(N+r)·b^(L-r) ≤ B·b^(L-K)`: the weighted interface is never worse than the pointwise interface.

declarations.name: weighted_block_certificate_of_pointwise
declarations.signature: theorem weighted_block_certificate_of_pointwise (b q N K L B : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hmiddle : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card ≤ B) (harith : q * (B * b ^ (L - K) + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : ∃ C : ℕ, (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) ∧ q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L
declarations.docstring: **Weighted certificates subsume pointwise certificates.** Classical `(N, K, L, B)` divisor block certificate data yields weighted-middle certificate data with `C = B·b^(L-K)` under the same arithmetic inequality.

declarations.name: near_int_witness_of_weighted_divisor_block_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem near_int_witness_of_weighted_divisor_block_certificate (b q N K L C : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hq : 0 < q) (hKL : K ≤ L) (hblock : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (N + r).divisors.card) (hmiddle : ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) (harith : q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : ∃ z : ℤ, 0 < |(b : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| ∧ |(b : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ, (((m + 1).divisors.card : ℝ)) / (b : ℝ) ^ (m + 1)) - (z : ℝ)| < 1 / (q : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Weighted certificate consumer.** A weighted divisor block certificate `(N, K, L, C)` for precision `q` — first-block divisibility, the exact weighted middle sum `∑_{r=K+1}^{L} τ(N+r)·b^(L-r) ≤ C`, and the ℕ-arithmetic inequality `q·(C + (N+L+2)) < b^L` — yields a near-integer witness for the `b^N`-dilated divisor-count series. The middle window is paid at its exact weighted value rather than through a pointwise bound: this is the certificate shape an averaging argument naturally produces, and it subsumes the pointwise interface via `weighted_block_certificate_of_pointwise`.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_weighted_block_certificates
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSum_full_support_of_weighted_block_certificates (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hcert : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L C : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (N + r).divisors.card) ∧ (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (N + r).divisors.card * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) ∧ q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : Irrational (∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Full-support (Erdős–Borwein) irrationality from weighted block certificates.** If for every precision `q` some weighted divisor block certificate `(N, K, L, C)` exists, the full-support series `∑_{n≥1} 1 / (b^n - 1)` is irrational. The weighted middle hypothesis is implied by the pointwise one (`weighted_block_certificate_of_pointwise`), so this closure is at least as strong as the landed pointwise closure; certificate existence itself is NOT claimed.

declarations.name: factorization_eq_of_modEq_prod_pow
declarations.signature: theorem factorization_eq_of_modEq_prod_pow (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hπ : 2 ≤ ∏ p ∈ P, p) (n : ℕ) (hmod : n ≡ (∏ p ∈ P, p) ^ (b - 1) [MOD (∏ p ∈ P, p) ^ b]) : ∀ p ∈ P, n.factorization p = b - 1
declarations.docstring: **Exact valuation from a product congruence.** If `n ≡ π^(b-1) [MOD π^b]` where `π = ∏ P` is a product of distinct primes, then every `p ∈ P` has exact valuation `b - 1` in `n`: writing `n = π^b·t + π^(b-1) = π^(b-1)·(π·t + 1)`, the cofactor is prime to `p`.

declarations.name: exists_prime_finset_card_gt
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_finset_card_gt (r M : ℕ) : ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = r ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, M < p

declarations.name: exists_exact_valuation_progression
declarations.signature: theorem exists_exact_valuation_progression (b L : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (K : ℕ) : ∃ x A : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = r ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, L < p) ∧ ∀ y : ℕ, ∀ p ∈ P, (x + y * A + r).factorization p = b - 1
declarations.docstring: **CRT block construction (exact-valuation form).** For every window length `K` there are `x` and a positive modulus `A` such that along the whole progression `x + y·A`, every slot `r ∈ [1, K]` carries a set of `r` distinct primes, all above the prescribed bound `L`, at which `x + y·A + r` has exact valuation `b - 1`. Blocks are added one at a time: each new slot imposes a single congruence `x + r ≡ π^(b-1) [MOD π^b]` with `π` the product of a fresh prime block, glued to the accumulated modulus by binary CRT.

declarations.name: exists_first_block_divisibility_progression
declarations.signature: theorem exists_first_block_divisibility_progression (b K L : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∃ x A : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ y : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (x + y * A + r).divisors.card
declarations.docstring: **First-block divisibility along a full arithmetic progression.** For every base `b ≥ 2`, window length `K`, and prime floor `L`, there are `x` and a positive modulus `A` with `b^r ∣ τ(x + y·A + r)` for every `y` and every `r ∈ [1, K]` — the first-block half of the divisor block certificate obligation, produced by CRT from exact prime valuations via the multiplicativity hinge, with every construction prime above `L`.

declarations.name: exists_exact_valuation_progression_with_support
declarations.signature: theorem exists_exact_valuation_progression_with_support (b L : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (K : ℕ) : ∃ x A : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ A → L < p ∧ ∃ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, p ∣ x + r) ∧ ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = r ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, L < p) ∧ ∀ y : ℕ, ∀ p ∈ P, (x + y * A + r).factorization p = b - 1
declarations.docstring: **CRT block construction with exposed modulus support.** The same construction as `exists_exact_valuation_progression`, additionally exposing the arithmetic of the modulus: every prime divisor of `A` lies above `L` and divides `x + r` for some first-block slot `r ∈ [1, K]`. This is the frame fact the middle-window analysis consumes — first-block primes cannot touch the middle window.

declarations.name: coprime_middle_of_first_block_support
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_middle_of_first_block_support (x A K L s : ℕ) (hsupp : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ A → L < p ∧ ∃ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, p ∣ x + r) (hs1 : K < s) (hs2 : s ≤ L) : Nat.Coprime A (x + s)
declarations.docstring: **Middle-window coprimality from modulus support.** If every prime of `A` lies above `L` and divides `x + r` for some `r ∈ [1, K]`, then `A` is coprime to every middle-window shift `x + s` with `K < s ≤ L`: a common prime would divide `s - r`, which is positive and below `L < p`. This is the free lemma the CRT frame buys — the construction primes force the first block and then vanish from the middle window.

declarations.name: card_filter_dvd_progression_le
declarations.signature: theorem card_filter_dvd_progression_le (A c d Y : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hcop : Nat.Coprime d A) : ((Finset.range Y).filter (fun y => d ∣ A * y + c)).card ≤ Y / d + 1
declarations.docstring: **Single-residue-class divisor counting along a progression.** A modulus `d` coprime to the step `A` divides `A·y + c` for at most `Y/d + 1` of the window values `y < Y`: any two solutions differ by a multiple of `d`. This is the exact-arithmetic engine behind the divisor-sum average — no analytic number theory enters.

declarations.name: card_divisors_le_two_mul_card_small_divisors
declarations.signature: theorem card_divisors_le_two_mul_card_small_divisors (n X : ℕ) (hnX : n ≤ X) : n.divisors.card ≤ 2 * ((Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.sqrt X)).filter (fun d => d ∣ n)).card
declarations.docstring: **Divisor pairing against a square bound.** For `n ≤ X`, the divisor count of `n` is at most twice the number of divisors of `n` up to `√X`: divisors pair as `d·(n/d) = n`, and both partners cannot exceed `√X`.

declarations.name: sum_card_divisors_progression_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_card_divisors_progression_le (A c Y X : ℕ) (hcop : Nat.Coprime A c) (hX : ∀ y ∈ Finset.range Y, A * y + c ≤ X) : ∑ y ∈ Finset.range Y, (A * y + c).divisors.card ≤ 2 * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.sqrt X), (Y / d + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Elementary divisor-sum average along a coprime progression.** With `gcd(A, c) = 1` and all window values bounded by `X`, the divisor counts of `A·y + c` over `y < Y` sum to at most `2·∑_{d ≤ √X} (Y/d + 1)`: divisor pairing plus single-residue-class counting. PNT-free.

declarations.name: sum_pow_weight_middle_window_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_pow_weight_middle_window_le (b K L : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : ∑ s ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, b ^ (L - s) ≤ b ^ (L - K)
declarations.docstring: Geometric weight of the middle window: `∑_{s=K+1}^{L} b^(L-s) ≤ b^(L-K)`.

declarations.name: sum_weighted_middle_window_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_weighted_middle_window_le (b x A K L Y X : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hsupp : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ A → L < p ∧ ∃ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, p ∣ x + r) (hX : ∀ y ∈ Finset.range Y, x + y * A + L ≤ X) : ∑ y ∈ Finset.range Y, ∑ s ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (x + y * A + s).divisors.card * b ^ (L - s) ≤ b ^ (L - K) * (2 * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.sqrt X), (Y / d + 1))
declarations.docstring: **Weighted middle-window total along the progression.** Summing the weighted middle sums over the window `y < Y` costs at most `b^(L-K) · (2·∑_{d ≤ √X} (Y/d + 1))`: middle-window coprimality from the modulus support, then the elementary progression average, then the geometric weight.

declarations.name: exists_le_div_of_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem exists_le_div_of_sum_le (Y T : ℕ) (hY : 0 < Y) (W : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∑ y ∈ Finset.range Y, W y ≤ T) : ∃ y : ℕ, y < Y ∧ W y ≤ T / Y
declarations.docstring: **Pigeonhole selection.** If `Y` window values sum to at most `T`, some value is at most `T / Y`.

declarations.name: exists_first_block_progression_with_selected_weighted_middle
declarations.signature: theorem exists_first_block_progression_with_selected_weighted_middle (b K L Y : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hY : 0 < Y) : ∃ x A : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ (∀ y : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (x + y * A + r).divisors.card) ∧ ∃ y : ℕ, y < Y ∧ ∑ s ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (x + y * A + s).divisors.card * b ^ (L - s) ≤ (b ^ (L - K) * (2 * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.sqrt (x + Y * A + L)), (Y / d + 1))) / Y
declarations.docstring: **First-block progression with a selected small weighted middle.** Unconditionally, for every base `b ≥ 2`, window shape `(K, L)`, and averaging range `Y > 0`, the CRT construction yields `x` and `A > 0` with first-block divisibility along the whole progression, together with some `y < Y` whose weighted middle sum is bounded by the elementary divisor-pair average `(b^(L-K) · 2·∑_{d ≤ √(x+Y·A+L)} (Y/d + 1)) / Y`. This is the middle-window selection half of the Erdős 1948 route in certificate shape; what remains for full certificate existence is explicit size control of `x` and `A` (and hence parameter closure in `q`).

declarations.name: param_linear_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem param_linear_le_two_pow (c e : ℕ) : c * (3 * c + e) + e ≤ 2 ^ (3 * c + e)
declarations.docstring: **Parameter closure kernel.** The linear function `c·κ + e` is dominated by `2^κ` at `κ = 3c + e`: cube `c + 1 ≤ 2^c` and absorb the slack.

declarations.name: harmonic_div_sum_core
declarations.signature: theorem harmonic_div_sum_core (J : ℕ) : ∀ S Y : ℕ, S ≤ 2 ^ J → ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S, Y / d ≤ Y * (J + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Dyadic harmonic core.** `∑_{d=1}^{S} ⌊Y/d⌋ ≤ Y·(J+1)` whenever `S ≤ 2^J`: each dyadic bucket `(2^j, 2^{j+1}]` contributes at most `Y`.

declarations.name: harmonic_div_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem harmonic_div_sum_le (S Y J : ℕ) (hS : S ≤ 2 ^ J) : ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S, (Y / d + 1) ≤ Y * (J + 1) + S
declarations.docstring: **Dyadic harmonic compression.** `∑_{d=1}^{S} (⌊Y/d⌋ + 1) ≤ Y·(J+1) + S` for `S ≤ 2^J` — the closed form that turns the raw progression divisor average into a parameter-usable middle bound.

declarations.name: exists_bertrand_prime_block
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bertrand_prime_block (m r : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : ∃ Q : Finset ℕ, Q.card = r ∧ (∀ p ∈ Q, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ p ∈ Q, m < p) ∧ (∀ p ∈ Q, p ≤ 2 ^ r * m)
declarations.docstring: **Bertrand prime block.** `r` distinct primes in `(m, 2^r·m]`, produced by chaining Bertrand's postulate — bounded fresh prime supply with no prime-counting input.

declarations.name: exists_bounded_disjoint_prime_blocks
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bounded_disjoint_prime_blocks (L K : ℕ) : ∃ (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ), L + 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ 2 ^ (K * (K + 1)) * (L + 1) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, (P r).card = r) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ∀ p ∈ P r, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ∀ p ∈ P r, L < p) ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ∀ p ∈ P r, p ≤ m) ∧ (∀ r s, r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K → s ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K → r ≠ s → Disjoint (P r) (P s))
declarations.docstring: **Bounded disjoint prime blocks.** A triangular family of pairwise disjoint prime blocks — block `r` has `r` primes — all in `(L, m]` with the explicit global ceiling `m ≤ 2^(K(K+1))·(L+1)`. Disjointness comes from stacking Bertrand intervals, never from primes exceeding an accumulated modulus.

declarations.name: exists_bounded_crt_residue
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bounded_crt_residue (K : ℕ) (m c : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, 0 < m r) (hcop : ∀ r s, r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K → s ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K → r ≠ s → Nat.Coprime (m r) (m s)) : ∃ x : ℕ, x < ∏ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, m r ∧ ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, x ≡ c r [MOD m r]
declarations.docstring: **Normalised simultaneous CRT.** Pairwise coprime moduli share a common residue *below the product of the moduli* — the height-aware form: old congruences transfer by divisibility, and the representative never leaves `[0, ∏ m_r)`.

declarations.name: exists_bounded_first_block_frame
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bounded_first_block_frame (b L K : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hK : 1 ≤ K) (hKL : K ≤ L) : ∃ x A : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ x < A ∧ L + 1 ≤ A ∧ A ≤ (2 ^ (K * (K + 1)) * (L + 1)) ^ (b * K ^ 2) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ A → L < p ∧ ∃ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, p ∣ x + r) ∧ (∀ y : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ (x + y * A + r).divisors.card)
declarations.docstring: **Bounded first-block frame.** The height-aware replacement for the qualitative CRT supply: `x < A`, the modulus support is exposed (every prime of `A` is above `L` and meets the first block), first-block divisibility holds along the whole progression, and — decisively — `A` carries the explicit bound `(2^(K(K+1))·(L+1))^(b·K²)`. Disjoint Bertrand blocks replace "fresh prime above the accumulated modulus".

declarations.name: selected_weighted_middle_of_supported_frame
declarations.signature: theorem selected_weighted_middle_of_supported_frame (b x A K L Y : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hY : 0 < Y) (hsupp : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ A → L < p ∧ ∃ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, p ∣ x + r) : ∃ y : ℕ, y < Y ∧ ∑ s ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, (x + y * A + s).divisors.card * b ^ (L - s) ≤ (b ^ (L - K) * (2 * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.sqrt (x + Y * A + L)), (Y / d + 1))) / Y
declarations.docstring: **Selected weighted middle for an external supported frame.** The middle-window selection argument, freed from the internal CRT supply: any `x, A` with exposed support yield some `y < Y` whose weighted middle sum is bounded by the elementary divisor-pair average. This is the consumer the bounded frame feeds.

declarations.name: certificate_param_arithmetic
declarations.signature: theorem certificate_param_arithmetic (b q K κ E : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hq : 0 < q) (hK : K = 9 * (q + b + 100)) (hκ : κ = 3 * (2 * b * K ^ 2 + 1) + (2 * b * K ^ 2 * (K * (K + 1) + 1) + q + 4)) (hE : E = b * K ^ 2 * (K * (K + 1) + κ + 1)) : 4 * q * (E + κ + 5) ≤ b ^ K ∧ 2 * E + κ + q + 4 ≤ 2 ^ κ ∧ 1 ≤ K ∧ K ≤ 2 ^ κ
