declarations.signature: def dyadicResidualIntNumerator (p r : ℤ) (c D : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Integer residual numerator. This is the algebraically natural core: unlike the interface natural specialization below, it needs no ordering hypothesis on the subtraction.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualIntRat
declarations.signature: def dyadicResidualIntRat (p r : ℤ) (c D : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Integer displayed residual normalized by `Rat.divInt`.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualIntNumerator_coprime_oddDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicResidualIntNumerator_coprime_oddDenominator (p r : ℤ) (c D : ℕ) (hDodd : Odd D) (hrD : r.natAbs.Coprime D) : (dyadicResidualIntNumerator p r c D).natAbs.Coprime D
declarations.docstring: The decisive congruence argument in `ℤ`: adding the multiple `pD` to `-2^c r` preserves coprimality with the odd modulus `D`.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualInt_denominator_sandwich
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicResidualInt_denominator_sandwich (p r : ℤ) (c D : ℕ) (hDpos : 0 < D) (hND : (dyadicResidualIntNumerator p r c D).natAbs.Coprime D) : D ∣ (dyadicResidualIntRat p r c D).den ∧ (dyadicResidualIntRat p r c D).den ∣ 2 ^ c * D
declarations.docstring: Integer form of the exact denominator sandwich. It works for positive, zero, or negative displayed residual numerators once coprimality with `D` is known.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualNumerator
declarations.signature: def dyadicResidualNumerator (p r c D : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Numerator left after subtracting a reduced finite prefix `r / D` from a dyadic rational `p / 2^c`. The transport theorem below assumes the subtraction is nonnegative, so natural subtraction is exact.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualRat
declarations.signature: def dyadicResidualRat (p r c D : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The displayed residual rational before its remaining power-of-two cancellation is normalized by `Rat`.

declarations.name: dyadicResidualNumerator_coprime_oddDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicResidualNumerator_coprime_oddDenominator (p r c D : ℕ) (hDodd : Odd D) (hrD : r.Coprime D) (hle : 2 ^ c * r ≤ p * D) : (dyadicResidualNumerator p r c D).Coprime D
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a reduced odd-denominator fraction from a dyadic fraction cannot cancel any factor of the odd denominator.

declarations.name: dyadicResidual_denominator_sandwich
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicResidual_denominator_sandwich (p r c D : ℕ) (hDpos : 0 < D) (hDodd : Odd D) (hrD : r.Coprime D) (hle : 2 ^ c * r ≤ p * D) : D ∣ (dyadicResidualRat p r c D).den ∧ (dyadicResidualRat p r c D).den ∣ 2 ^ c * D
declarations.docstring: Exact denominator sandwich. If `Q` is the normalized denominator of the residual, then `D ∣ Q ∣ 2^c D`. This is the division-free statement that the odd part inherited from the finite prefix is exactly `D`.

declarations.name: nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator
declarations.signature: def nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: For a displayed residual `p / (2L)`, the integer numerator of its excess above the next dyadic point `2^-(n+1)`. Indeed, `p/(2L) - 2^-(n+1) = E/(2^(n+1)L)`. Keeping `E` integral makes the unresolved skipped-branch comparison an exact Diophantine inequality rather than a real-valued phase estimate.

declarations.name: nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator_succ
declarations.signature: theorem nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator_succ (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p (n + 1) L = 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L + (L : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: With displayed numerator and denominator fixed across one skipped rank, the next dyadic excess doubles and receives one denominator increment.

declarations.name: nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator_add
declarations.signature: theorem nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator_add (p : ℤ) (n k L : ℕ) : nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p (n + k) L = (((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L) + ((((2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1) * (L : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: Closed form of the unchanged-denominator skip-run recurrence.

declarations.name: divInt_sub_nextDyadic_eq_excess_divInt
declarations.signature: theorem divInt_sub_nextDyadic_eq_excess_divInt (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) - (1 / (2 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1)) = Rat.divInt (nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L) (((2 ^ (n + 1) * L : ℕ) : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: Exact rational identity represented by `nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator`.

declarations.name: divInt_le_nextDyadic_iff_excess_nonpos
declarations.signature: theorem divInt_le_nextDyadic_iff_excess_nonpos (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ 1 / (2 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) ↔ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L ≤ 0
declarations.docstring: The displayed residual is on the dyadic-safe side exactly when its integer excess numerator is nonpositive.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRat_succ_le_divInt_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRat_succ_le_divInt_iff_excess (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) ≤ Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) ↔ p ≤ 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L
declarations.docstring: At the prospective rank `n+1`, selection of the Mersenne weight is the complementary exact inequality `p ≤ 2E`. Together with the dyadic sign test, this identifies the entire forbidden sliver using one integer numerator.

declarations.name: divInt_lt_mersenneWeightRat_succ_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem divInt_lt_mersenneWeightRat_succ_iff_excess (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) < mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) ↔ 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L < p
declarations.docstring: A skipped prospective rank is exactly the strict complementary excess inequality `2E < p`.

declarations.name: divInt_mem_nextMersenneDyadicSliver_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem divInt_mem_nextMersenneDyadicSliver_iff_excess (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : (1 / (2 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) < Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧ Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) < mersenneWeightRat (n + 1)) ↔ (0 < nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L ∧ 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L < p)
declarations.docstring: Exact forbidden-sliver classifier for a displayed residual. A skipped rank is dyadically unsafe precisely in the finite integer window `0 < E` and `2E < p`.

declarations.name: nextMersenneDecisionDefect
declarations.signature: def nextMersenneDecisionDefect (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The cross-multiplied defect at prospective rank `n+1`.

declarations.name: nextMersenneDecisionDefect_eq_two_excess_sub
declarations.signature: theorem nextMersenneDecisionDefect_eq_two_excess_sub (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : nextMersenneDecisionDefect p n L = 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L - p
declarations.docstring: The decision defect is exactly `2E-p`.

declarations.name: nextMersenneDecisionDefect_le_neg_iff_excess_nonpos
declarations.signature: theorem nextMersenneDecisionDefect_le_neg_iff_excess_nonpos (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : nextMersenneDecisionDefect p n L ≤ -p ↔ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L ≤ 0
declarations.docstring: A skipped decision is dyadically safe exactly when its raw defect is at least one full displayed numerator below zero.

declarations.name: le_nextMersenneDecisionDefect_iff_le_excess
declarations.signature: theorem le_nextMersenneDecisionDefect_iff_le_excess (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : p ≤ nextMersenneDecisionDefect p n L ↔ p ≤ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L
declarations.docstring: The strengthened taken branch `E ≥ p` is the symmetric unit-margin condition on the positive raw defect.

declarations.name: nextMersenneDecisionDefect_mem_neg_unit_window_iff
declarations.signature: theorem nextMersenneDecisionDefect_mem_neg_unit_window_iff (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) : (-p < nextMersenneDecisionDefect p n L ∧ nextMersenneDecisionDefect p n L < 0) ↔ (0 < nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L ∧ 2 * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L < p)
declarations.docstring: The unresolved unsafe-skip window is the open unit neighbourhood below the Mersenne threshold, expressed without division.

declarations.name: BlockTakeAt
declarations.signature: def BlockTakeAt (p D k : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne term at rank `k` is taken by the displayed residual `p/(2D)`, in cross-multiplied natural coordinates.

declarations.name: BlockDyadicSafeAt
declarations.signature: def BlockDyadicSafeAt (p D k : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The displayed residual lies below the dyadic skeleton `2^-k`.

declarations.name: IsFirstBlockTakeAfter
declarations.signature: def IsFirstBlockTakeAfter (p D a b : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: `b` is the first taken rank strictly after `a`.

declarations.name: all_intermediate_BlockDyadicSafeAt_iff_last
declarations.signature: theorem all_intermediate_BlockDyadicSafeAt_iff_last (p D a b : ℕ) (hab : a < b) : (∀ k : ℕ, a < k → k < b → BlockDyadicSafeAt p D k) ↔ b = a + 1 ∨ BlockDyadicSafeAt p D (b - 1)
declarations.docstring: Over a constant-residual skip block, dyadic safety is monotone in the rank. Hence every intermediate skip is safe iff either the block is empty or its last rank is safe.

declarations.name: firstBlockTake_predecessor_open_bound
declarations.signature: theorem firstBlockTake_predecessor_open_bound {p D a b : ℕ} (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p D a b) (hgap : a + 1 < b) : p * (2 ^ (b - 1) - 1) < 2 * D
declarations.docstring: Minimality of a non-adjacent next take supplies only the open Mersenne predecessor bound. The missing skip-sign theorem must strengthen this by exactly one unit, from `2^(b-1)-1` to `2^(b-1)`.

declarations.name: firstBlockTake_all_skips_safe_iff_last_margin
declarations.signature: theorem firstBlockTake_all_skips_safe_iff_last_margin {p D a b : ℕ} (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p D a b) : (∀ k : ℕ, a < k → k < b → BlockDyadicSafeAt p D k) ↔ b = a + 1 ∨ p * 2 ^ (b - 1) ≤ 2 * D
declarations.docstring: Exact block compression under the first-take hypothesis.

declarations.name: rawTakenResidualNumerator
declarations.signature: def rawTakenResidualNumerator (p D b : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Raw positive numerator produced by taking rank `b`.

declarations.name: rawTakenResidualDenominator
declarations.docstring: Raw odd-denominator coordinate produced by taking rank `b`.

declarations.name: blockTakeAt_commonFactor_iff
declarations.signature: theorem blockTakeAt_commonFactor_iff {H B g p D k : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hH : H = g * p) (hB : B = g * D) : BlockTakeAt p D k ↔ BlockTakeAt H B k
declarations.docstring: A common positive reduction factor cancels out of the next take test.

declarations.name: blockDyadicSafeAt_commonFactor_iff
declarations.signature: theorem blockDyadicSafeAt_commonFactor_iff {H B g p D k : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hH : H = g * p) (hB : B = g * D) : BlockDyadicSafeAt p D k ↔ BlockDyadicSafeAt H B k
declarations.docstring: The same common factor cancels out of the dyadic-safe margin.

declarations.name: firstBlockTakeAfter_commonFactor_iff
declarations.signature: theorem firstBlockTakeAfter_commonFactor_iff {H B g p D a b : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hH : H = g * p) (hB : B = g * D) : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p D a b ↔ IsFirstBlockTakeAfter H B a b
declarations.docstring: A common reduction factor therefore also cancels out of the identity of the next taken rank.

declarations.name: reduced_nextBlock_all_skips_safe_iff_gcdFree
declarations.signature: theorem reduced_nextBlock_all_skips_safe_iff_gcdFree {b H B g p' D' c : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hHred : H = g * p') (hBred : B = g * D') (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p' D' b c) : (∀ k : ℕ, b < k → k < c → BlockDyadicSafeAt p' D' k) ↔ c = b + 1 ∨ H * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * B
declarations.docstring: **GCD-free taken-block reduction.** Suppose taking rank `b` creates raw coordinates `(H,B)`, and reducing them by any positive common factor gives the next displayed state `(p',D')`. If `c` is its next taken rank, all intervening skips are dyadically safe iff either there are no intervening skips or the single raw inequality `H*2^(c-1) ≤ 2B` holds. No gcd or cancellation factor remains in the proof obligation.

declarations.name: reduced_nextBlock_gcdFree_margin_expanded
declarations.signature: theorem reduced_nextBlock_gcdFree_margin_expanded {p D b H B c : ℕ} (hHraw : H = rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b) (hBraw : B = rawTakenResidualDenominator D b) : (H * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * B) ↔ (p * (2 ^ b - 1) - 2 * D) * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * (D * (2 ^ b - 1))
declarations.docstring: Expanded form of the raw gcd-free margin after taking rank `b`.

declarations.name: takenBlock_all_next_skips_safe_iff_raw_margin
declarations.signature: theorem takenBlock_all_next_skips_safe_iff_raw_margin {p D b g p' D' c : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hnum : rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b = g * p') (hden : rawTakenResidualDenominator D b = g * D') (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p' D' b c) : (∀ k : ℕ, b < k → k < c → BlockDyadicSafeAt p' D' k) ↔ c = b + 1 ∨ (p * (2 ^ b - 1) - 2 * D) * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * (D * (2 ^ b - 1))
declarations.docstring: Direct source-state form: the reduced next residual may have arbitrary positive cancellation, but the complete intervening-skip obligation is the single raw inequality displayed on the right.

declarations.name: rawTakenResidual_adjacent_margin_of_predecessor_safe
declarations.signature: theorem rawTakenResidual_adjacent_margin_of_predecessor_safe {p D b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (hsafe : BlockDyadicSafeAt p D (b - 1)) (htake : BlockTakeAt p D b) : rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b * 2 ^ b ≤ 2 * rawTakenResidualDenominator D b
declarations.docstring: The block margin is automatically inductive across an adjacent pair of takes. If the state before taking `b` was safe at its predecessor dyadic scale, the raw state after the take is safe at scale `b`. Thus only nonadjacent successor blocks require new orbit arithmetic.

declarations.name: firstBlockTake_margin_iff_reciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem firstBlockTake_margin_iff_reciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne {p D a b : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p D a b) (hgap : a + 1 < b) : BlockDyadicSafeAt p D (b - 1) ↔ (2 * D) / p ≠ 2 ^ (b - 1) - 1
declarations.docstring: At a nonadjacent first-take block, the missing dyadic margin is exactly avoidance of the lower Mersenne value by the integer part of the reciprocal residual.

declarations.name: takenBlock_rawMargin_iff_reciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem takenBlock_rawMargin_iff_reciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne {p D b c : ℕ} (hpos : 0 < rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b) (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter (rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b) (rawTakenResidualDenominator D b) b c) (hgap : b + 1 < c) : ((p * (2 ^ b - 1) - 2 * D) * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * (D * (2 ^ b - 1))) ↔ (2 * rawTakenResidualDenominator D b) / rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b ≠ 2 ^ (c - 1) - 1
declarations.docstring: Source-coordinate specialization of the same exact quotient obstruction. All cancellation is absent: only the raw post-take numerator and denominator enter the quotient.

declarations.name: takenBlock_rawMargin_iff_reducedReciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem takenBlock_rawMargin_iff_reducedReciprocalFloor_ne_mersenne {p D b g p' D' c : ℕ} (hg : 0 < g) (hp' : 0 < p') (hnum : rawTakenResidualNumerator p D b = g * p') (hden : rawTakenResidualDenominator D b = g * D') (hfirst : IsFirstBlockTakeAfter p' D' b c) (hgap : b + 1 < c) : ((p * (2 ^ b - 1) - 2 * D) * 2 ^ (c - 1) ≤ 2 * (D * (2 ^ b - 1))) ↔ (2 * D') / p' ≠ 2 ^ (c - 1) - 1
declarations.docstring: Cancellation-aware form matching an actual taken block. The raw source margin is equivalent to Mersenne-floor avoidance in the reduced post-take state; the common reduction factor disappears from both sides.

declarations.name: invariant
declarations.signature: inductive invariant. The state `7/(2*17)` takes rank `3`, producing `15/(2*119)`, but rank `4` is an unsafe skip with exact excess `1`. -/ theorem safeBracket_and_numeratorMonotone_not_inductive_fixture : BlockDyadicSafeAt 7 17 2 ∧ BlockTakeAt 7 17 3 ∧ rawTakenResidualNumerator 7 17 3 = 15 ∧ rawTakenResidualDenominator 17 3 = 119 ∧ 7 ≤ 15 ∧ ¬ BlockTakeAt 15 119 4 ∧ ¬ BlockDyadicSafeAt 15 119 4 ∧ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator 15 3 119 = 1 ∧ BlockTakeAt 15 119 5

declarations.name: safeBracket_and_numeratorMonotone_not_inductive_fixture
declarations.signature: theorem safeBracket_and_numeratorMonotone_not_inductive_fixture : BlockDyadicSafeAt 7 17 2 ∧ BlockTakeAt 7 17 3 ∧ rawTakenResidualNumerator 7 17 3 = 15 ∧ rawTakenResidualDenominator 17 3 = 119 ∧ 7 ≤ 15 ∧ ¬ BlockTakeAt 15 119 4 ∧ ¬ BlockDyadicSafeAt 15 119 4 ∧ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator 15 3 119 = 1 ∧ BlockTakeAt 15 119 5
declarations.docstring: Safe bracketing plus nondecrease of the displayed numerator is not an inductive invariant. The state `7/(2*17)` takes rank `3`, producing `15/(2*119)`, but rank `4` is an unsafe skip with exact excess `1`.

declarations.name: mersenneLcm_through_seven_eq
declarations.docstring: The denominator in the second fixture is already saturated by every Mersenne denominator through rank `7`.

declarations.name: lcmSaturated_safeBracket_not_inductive_fixture
declarations.signature: theorem lcmSaturated_safeBracket_not_inductive_fixture : BlockDyadicSafeAt 12149 1240155 7 ∧ BlockTakeAt 12149 1240155 8 ∧ rawTakenResidualNumerator 12149 1240155 8 = 15 * 41179 ∧ rawTakenResidualDenominator 1240155 8 = 15 * 21082635 ∧ 12149 ≤ 41179 ∧ ¬ BlockTakeAt 41179 21082635 9 ∧ ¬ BlockTakeAt 41179 21082635 10 ∧ ¬ BlockDyadicSafeAt 41179 21082635 10 ∧ nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator 41179 9 21082635 = 1013 ∧ BlockTakeAt 41179 21082635 11
declarations.docstring: Even full initial-LCM denominator saturation, safe current bracketing, positive cancellation, and numerator increase do not make the block margin inductive. After the rank-`8` take, rank `10` is skipped but has exact positive excess `1013`.

declarations.name: divInt_le_nextTwoChannelCap_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem divInt_le_nextTwoChannelCap_iff_excess (p : ℤ) (n L : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) : Rat.divInt p ((2 * L : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ (1 / (2 : ℚ)) ^ (n + 1) + (1 / 3 : ℚ) * (1 / 4 : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) ↔ 3 * (((2 ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) * nextDyadicExcessIntNumerator p n L) ≤ (L : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The two-channel cap at the next exponent is exactly one integer inequality. This is the division-free form `3 * 2^(n+1) * E ≤ L` for the displayed residual `p/(2L)`.

declarations.name: halfGreedyPrefixRat
declarations.docstring: The exact finite greedy prefix used to display the half residual.

declarations.name: halfGreedyPrefixDenominator
declarations.docstring: The inherited odd denominator of the exact finite greedy prefix.

declarations.name: halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator
declarations.docstring: Displayed numerator `p_n` in `r_n = p_n / (2 * halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n)`.

declarations.name: halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator
declarations.docstring: The actual greedy half-orbit specialization of the integral excess numerator. At level `n`, it measures excess above `2^-(n+1)`.

declarations.name: greedyHalfRemainderRat_eq_displayed_divInt
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalfRemainderRat_eq_displayed_divInt (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 2 : ℚ) n = Rat.divInt (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n) ((2 * halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The rational greedy half residual has the exact displayed numerator and odd prefix denominator above.

declarations.name: greedyHalfRemainder_le_twoChannelCap_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalfRemainder_le_twoChannelCap_iff_excess (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1) ↔ 3 * (((2 ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) * halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n) ≤ (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The exact actual-orbit cap socket: the real two-channel cap is equivalent to a single integer inequality in the greedy prefix numerator and its odd denominator.

declarations.name: greedyHalfRemainder_le_nextDyadic_iff_excess_nonpos
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalfRemainder_le_nextDyadic_iff_excess_nonpos (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ halfDyadicCap (n + 1) ↔ halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n ≤ 0
declarations.docstring: The stronger dyadic-safe predicate is simply the sign of the same exact integer numerator.

declarations.name: nextDyadic_lt_greedyHalfRemainder_iff_excess_pos
declarations.signature: theorem nextDyadic_lt_greedyHalfRemainder_iff_excess_pos (n : ℕ) : halfDyadicCap (n + 1) < greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ↔ 0 < halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n
declarations.docstring: A genuine landing in the next Mersenne--dyadic sliver is detected by a positive integer numerator. The skipped-branch hypothesis supplies the independent strict upper bound by the next Mersenne weight.

declarations.name: greedyHalfRemainder_lt_mersenneWeight_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalfRemainder_lt_mersenneWeight_iff_excess (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n < mersenneWeight (n + 1) ↔ 2 * halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n < halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n
declarations.docstring: The actual half orbit skips rank `n+1` exactly when its displayed excess satisfies `2E_n < p_n`.

declarations.name: greedyHalf_mem_nextMersenneDyadicSliver_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalf_mem_nextMersenneDyadicSliver_iff_excess (n : ℕ) : (halfDyadicCap (n + 1) < greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ∧ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n < mersenneWeight (n + 1)) ↔ (0 < halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n ∧ 2 * halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n < halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n)
declarations.docstring: The actual forbidden Mersenne--dyadic sliver is the finite integer window `0 < E_n` and `2E_n < p_n`. This is the exact last-skip comparison that any run-compressed producer must exclude.

declarations.name: twoChannelCap_lt_greedyHalfRemainder_iff_excess
declarations.signature: theorem twoChannelCap_lt_greedyHalfRemainder_iff_excess (n : ℕ) : halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1) < greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ↔ (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n : ℤ) < 3 * (((2 ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) * halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n)
declarations.docstring: Exact hard falsifier for the two-channel producer: a cap violation is the reverse strict integer inequality, with no numerical approximation.

declarations.name: HalfGreedySkippedExcessBound
declarations.docstring: Division-free producer for the only branch on which the greedy two-channel cap has arithmetic content.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_excessBound
declarations.docstring: The integer skipped-rank producer plugs directly into the landed greedy membership consumer.

declarations.name: mersennePrefix_doubleDepth_lt_halfDyadicCap
declarations.signature: theorem mersennePrefix_doubleDepth_lt_halfDyadicCap {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), mersenneWeight (m + k + 1)) < halfDyadicCap m
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne mass through twice the current depth is already smaller than the current dyadic cap. This converts a dyadically unsafe skipped remainder into a long forced block of subsequent greedy selections.

declarations.name: greedyMersenne_forcedBlock_selected
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenne_forcedBlock_selected {x : ℝ} {m J : ℕ} (hblock : (∑ k ∈ Finset.range J, mersenneWeight (m + k + 1)) < greedyMersenneRemainder x m) : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range J, mersenneWeight (m + j + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x (m + j)
declarations.docstring: If a finite block weighs less than the current remainder, greedy must select every term in that block.

declarations.name: forcedBlock_tailExcess_eq
declarations.signature: theorem forcedBlock_tailExcess_eq (m J : ℕ) (r : ℝ) : (r - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range J, mersenneWeight (m + k + 1))) - mersenneTail (m + J) = r - mersenneTail m
declarations.docstring: Consecutive selections preserve signed distance from the exact tail separatrix. This explains why a forced take block alone cannot produce a contradiction: both the remainder and the true tail lose the same prefix.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainder_le_four_thirds
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainder_le_four_thirds {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : mersenneWeightRemainder n ≤ (4 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n
declarations.docstring: Starting at exponent at least two improves the crude factor-two envelope on each higher-channel term to `4/3`.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainderTail_le_four_twentyone
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainderTail_le_four_twentyone {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : mersenneWeightRemainderTail m ≤ (4 / 21 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ m
declarations.docstring: At positive starting depth, the accumulated channels of order at least three are bounded by `(4/21)·8⁻ᵐ`.

declarations.name: remainderTail_lt_tripleDyadic
declarations.signature: theorem remainderTail_lt_tripleDyadic {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : mersenneWeightRemainderTail m < ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (3 * m + 2)
declarations.docstring: The higher-channel tail at depth `m` is strictly smaller than the dyadic tail at depth `3m+2`.

declarations.name: mersennePrefix_threeDepth_add_two_lt_halfTwoChannelCap
declarations.signature: theorem mersennePrefix_threeDepth_add_two_lt_halfTwoChannelCap {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (2 * m + 2), mersenneWeight (m + k + 1)) < halfTwoChannelCap m
declarations.docstring: The complete consecutive block through exponent `3m+2` is still strictly lighter than the two-channel cap at depth `m`.

declarations.name: capViolation_forces_threeDepthBlock
declarations.signature: theorem capViolation_forces_threeDepthBlock {x : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hcap : halfTwoChannelCap m < greedyMersenneRemainder x m) : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (2 * m + 2), mersenneWeight (m + j + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x (m + j)
declarations.docstring: A two-channel-cap violation forces the consecutive greedy take block through exponent `3m+2`.

declarations.name: tripleDepthTail_lt_thirdChannel
declarations.signature: theorem tripleDepthTail_lt_thirdChannel {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : mersenneTail (3 * m + 3) < (1 / 7 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ m
declarations.docstring: At the first depth beyond the forced block, the full remaining tail is already smaller than the third-channel contribution at the starting depth.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap_lt_mersennePrefix_threeDepth_add_three
declarations.signature: theorem halfTwoChannelCap_lt_mersennePrefix_threeDepth_add_three {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : halfTwoChannelCap m < (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (2 * m + 3), mersenneWeight (m + k + 1))
declarations.docstring: The two-channel cap lies strictly before the next (`2m+3`)-term prefix. Together with the preceding lower bracket, this pins its exact prefix cell.

declarations.name: exists_relaxed_capViolation_exact_block
declarations.signature: theorem exists_relaxed_capViolation_exact_block {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : ∃ r : ℝ, halfTwoChannelCap m < r ∧ r < mersenneWeight m ∧ (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (2 * m + 2), mersenneWeight (m + k + 1)) < r ∧ r - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (2 * m + 2), mersenneWeight (m + k + 1)) < mersenneWeight (3 * m + 3)
declarations.docstring: Hard local falsifier: there is an open relaxed-state cell above the two-channel cap which takes every exponent through `3m+2` and then skips `3m+3`. Hence skip-plus-forced-run geometry alone cannot close the producer; some arithmetic property of the actual greedy prefix is indispensable.

declarations.name: greedyHalf_unsafeSkip_forces_doubleBlock
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalf_unsafeSkip_forces_doubleBlock (n : ℕ) (hskip : ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n) (hunsafe : halfDyadicCap (n + 1) < greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n) : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 2), mersenneWeight (n + j + 2) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (n + j + 1)
declarations.docstring: A skipped half-orbit rank above its dyadic cap forces selection of every one of the next `n + 2` exponents.

declarations.name: greedyHalf_capViolationSkip_forces_threeDepthBlock
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalf_capViolationSkip_forces_threeDepthBlock (n : ℕ) (hskip : ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n) (hcap : halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1) < greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n) : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 4), mersenneWeight (n + j + 2) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (n + j + 1)
declarations.docstring: On the actual half orbit, a skipped rank which violates the two-channel cap forces the maximal uniform block supplied by tail geometry: all following exponents through `3(n+1)+2`.

declarations.name: HalfGreedyThreeDepthTakeRunExcessBound
declarations.docstring: Strongest run-compressed arithmetic producer supplied by the uniform tail geometry. The exact excess inequality is required only when a skipped rank is followed by the entire forced take block through exponent `3n+5`.

declarations.name: halfGreedySkippedExcessBound_of_threeDepthTakeRun
declarations.docstring: The triple-depth run producer is sufficient for the original skipped-rank excess bound. If the displayed run fails, the cap violation itself is impossible by `greedyHalf_capViolationSkip_forces_threeDepthBlock`.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_threeDepthTakeRunExcessBound
declarations.docstring: The strongest run-compressed producer feeds the half-membership consumer.

declarations.name: HalfGreedyLongTakeRunExcessBound
declarations.docstring: Earlier, weaker run-compressed producer retained for compatibility. It uses only the dyadic unsafe-skip block through twice the current depth; the triple-depth producer above has a strictly narrower exceptional branch.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_longTakeRunExcessBound
declarations.docstring: The long-take-run producer feeds the existing exact half-membership consumer.

declarations.name: finiteErdosSum_den_odd
declarations.signature: theorem finiteErdosSum_den_odd (F : Finset ℕ) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) : Odd (finiteErdosSum F 2).den
declarations.docstring: At base two, the actual reduced denominator of every positive finite Erdős fragment is odd.

declarations.name: halfGreedyPrefixDenominator_odd
declarations.docstring: The denominator used by the skipped-rank numerator is genuinely odd, because the finite greedy prefix contains no exponent zero.

declarations.name: oddDoublingOrder_finiteErdosSum_den_eq_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem oddDoublingOrder_finiteErdosSum_den_eq_lcm (F : Finset ℕ) (hF : F.Nonempty) (h0 : 0 ∉ F) : oddDoublingOrder (finiteErdosSum F 2).den (finiteErdosSum_den_odd F h0) = F.lcm id
declarations.docstring: The existing finite noncollapse theorem rewritten in the T9 order API: the order of two modulo the actual reduced denominator is `lcm F`.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_finset_eq_cast_finiteErdosSum
declarations.signature: theorem erdosSupportSeries_finset_eq_cast_finiteErdosSum (F : Finset ℕ) : erdosSupportSeries 2 (↑F : Set ℕ) = ((finiteErdosSum F 2 : ℚ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A finite support series is the real cast of the audited rational `finiteErdosSum`.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_diff_finset

declarations.signature: theorem halfGreedy_coordinates_add_of_all_skips (b j : ℕ) (hskip : ∀ t : ℕ, t < j → ¬ mersenneWeight (b + t + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (b + t)) : halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator (b + j) = halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator b ∧ halfGreedyPrefixDenominator (b + j) = halfGreedyPrefixDenominator b
declarations.docstring: A run of actual skipped decisions leaves both reduced displayed coordinates unchanged.

declarations.name: HalfGreedySkippedActualRawMarginWitness
declarations.docstring: The arithmetically meaningful remaining producer: every actual skipped rank is bracketed by consecutive actual takes whose source-coordinate raw margin holds.

declarations.name: HalfGreedySkippedRawBlockWitness
declarations.docstring: Exact actual-state witness needed to consume one raw taken-block margin at a skipped rank. The source coordinates are the state immediately before the earlier take; the target coordinates are the live state at the skipped rank.

declarations.name: halfGreedy_rawBlockWitness_of_actualRawMarginWitness
declarations.signature: theorem halfGreedy_rawBlockWitness_of_actualRawMarginWitness {n : ℕ} (h : HalfGreedySkippedActualRawMarginWitness n) : Nonempty (HalfGreedySkippedRawBlockWitness n)
declarations.docstring: All state-identification and cancellation fields required by the generic raw block theorem follow from an actual consecutive-take witness.

declarations.name: HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipActualRawMarginSupply
declarations.docstring: Minimal producer form: a raw block witness is required only for a putative skipped rank that is not already dyadically safe.

declarations.name: halfGreedy_BlockSafe_of_rawBlockWitness
declarations.signature: theorem halfGreedy_BlockSafe_of_rawBlockWitness {n : ℕ} (h : HalfGreedySkippedRawBlockWitness n) : BlockDyadicSafeAt (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n).natAbs (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n) (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The raw block theorem turns the actual-state witness into the precise dyadic safety fact consumed by greedy membership.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skippedRawBlockMarginSupply
declarations.docstring: A universal actual raw taken-block margin supply closes exact half-membership.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skippedActualRawMarginSupply
declarations.docstring: Actual consecutive takes plus the single raw gcd-free margin at every skipped rank are sufficient for exact half-membership.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_unsafeSkipActualRawMarginSupply
declarations.docstring: The minimal unsafe-skip actual raw-margin producer closes exact half-membership: a witness converts through actual state/cancellation into the generic raw theorem and contradicts the alleged unsafe state.

declarations.name: blockDyadicSafeAt_iff_rawPredecessorOvershoot
declarations.signature: theorem blockDyadicSafeAt_iff_rawPredecessorOvershoot (p D k : ℕ) : BlockDyadicSafeAt p D k ↔ p ≤ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ k - 1)
declarations.docstring: Raw dyadic safety is exactly the unscaled predecessor-overshoot bound. This is the condition measured by the rigorous interval receipt.

declarations.name: rawPredecessorOvershoot_of_gcdScaled
declarations.signature: theorem rawPredecessorOvershoot_of_gcdScaled {p D k : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (hscaled : Nat.gcd D (2 ^ k - 1) * p ≤ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ k - 1)) : p ≤ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ k - 1)
declarations.docstring: A positive denominator makes the predecessor gcd at least one, so the gcd-scaled overshoot bound implies the exact raw bound.

declarations.name: rawSafe_but_not_gcdScaled_fixture
declarations.docstring: The gcd-scaled producer is strictly stronger than raw dyadic safety, even for coprime displayed coordinates.

declarations.name: firstTake_rank9_after_rank5_fixture
declarations.docstring: In the non-inductivity fixture, ranks `6,7,8` are skipped and rank `9` is the first take after the rank-`5` update.

declarations.name: factorEleven_predecessorOvershoot_not_inductive_fixture
declarations.signature: theorem factorEleven_predecessorOvershoot_not_inductive_fixture : BlockDyadicSafeAt 39 539 4 ∧ 11 * 39 ≤ 2 * 539 - 39 * (2 ^ 4 - 1) ∧ BlockTakeAt 39 539 5 ∧ rawTakenResidualNumerator 39 539 5 = 131 ∧ rawTakenResidualDenominator 539 5 = 16709 ∧ Nat.gcd 131 16709 = 1 ∧ Nat.gcd 16709 (2 ^ (9 - 1) - 1) = 1 ∧ 10 * 9 ≤ (2 ^ (9 - 1) - 1) / Nat.gcd 16709 (2 ^ (9 - 1) - 1) ∧ IsFirstBlockTakeAfter 131 16709 5 9 ∧ 2 * 16709 - 131 * (2 ^ (9 - 1) - 1) = 13 ∧ ¬ BlockDyadicSafeAt 131 16709 (9 - 1) ∧ ¬ Nat.gcd 16709 (2 ^ (9 - 1) - 1) * 131 ≤
declarations.docstring: Exact one-step falsifier for generic propagation of the sharp empirical factor `11`. The source `(39,539)` is predecessor-safe and has overshoot `493 ≥ 11*39`; taking rank `5` gives the reduced state `(131,16709)`, whose first next take is rank `9`, but its predecessor overshoot is only `13`. The target fresh quotient is already `255 ≥ 10*9`, so its size alone does not repair the failed margin.

declarations.name: gcd_dvd_predecessorOvershoot
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_dvd_predecessorOvershoot (p D c : ℕ) : Nat.gcd D (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1) ∣ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The predecessor gcd divides the exact positive-side overshoot numerator; there is no hidden floor in its primitive quotient.

declarations.name: unsafeSandwich_consecutive_gcd_lt
declarations.signature: theorem unsafeSandwich_consecutive_gcd_lt {p D c : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (hc : 0 < c) (hpodd : Odd p) (hskip : p * (2 ^ c - 1) < 2 * D) (hunsafe : 2 * D < p * 2 ^ c) : Nat.gcd D (2 ^ c - 1) < p ∧ Nat.gcd D (2 ^ (c + 1) - 1) < p
declarations.docstring: An unsafe Mersenne sandwich forces both adjacent Mersenne gcds to be strictly smaller than the displayed numerator. For the lower gcd this is the positive overshoot `delta = 2D - p(2^c - 1)`. For the next gcd, the same divisor divides `|2 delta - p|`; oddness of `p` makes this difference nonzero, while `0 < delta < p` keeps it strictly below `p`.

declarations.name: greedyHalf_unsafeSkip_consecutive_gcd_lt
declarations.signature: theorem greedyHalf_unsafeSkip_consecutive_gcd_lt (n : ℕ) (hskip : ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n) (hunsafe : ¬ BlockDyadicSafeAt (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n).natAbs (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n) (n + 1)) : Nat.gcd (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n) (2 ^ (n + 1) - 1) < (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n).natAbs ∧ Nat.gcd (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n) (2 ^ (n + 2) - 1) < (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n).natAbs
declarations.docstring: Actual half-greedy specialization: every putative dyadically unsafe skipped rank makes the two consecutive Mersenne gcds smaller than the current displayed residual numerator.

declarations.name: gcdScaled_predecessorOvershoot_iff_primitiveQuotient
declarations.signature: theorem gcdScaled_predecessorOvershoot_iff_primitiveQuotient {p D c : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) : Nat.gcd D (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1) * p ≤ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1) ↔ p ≤ (2 * D - p * (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1)) / Nat.gcd D (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The gcd-scaled overshoot inequality is exactly the lower bound on the primitive quotient used by the executable actual-orbit replay.

declarations.name: blockDyadicSafeAt_of_gcdScaled_predecessorOvershoot
declarations.signature: theorem blockDyadicSafeAt_of_gcdScaled_predecessorOvershoot {p D c : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hD : 0 < D) (hc : 1 < c) (hover : Nat.gcd D (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1) * p ≤ 2 * D - p * (2 ^ (c - 1) - 1)) : BlockDyadicSafeAt p D (c - 1)
declarations.docstring: A gcd-scaled primitive overshoot at the predecessor Mersenne threshold forces the missing dyadic margin.

declarations.name: HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipGcdOvershootSupply

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_unsafeSkipGcdOvershootSupply

declarations.name: HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipPrimitiveOvershootSupply

declarations.name: unsafeSkipGcdOvershootSupply_iff_primitive

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_unsafeSkipPrimitiveOvershootSupply

declarations.name: HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipElevenGcdOvershootSupply

declarations.name: squarefree_dvd_mul_iff_of_dvd

declarations.name: windowFirstCos_gt_of_not_certifiedKill

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_of_first_harmonic_gap_subset
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_of_first_harmonic_gap_subset {h X L : ℕ} (T : Finset ℕ) (hTlt : ∀ N ∈ T, N < 2 * X) (hTne : T.Nonempty) (hroom : 16 * (2 * X + h + L + 2) ≤ 2 ^ L) (hgap : (∑ N ∈ T, windowFirstCos h N L) ≤ (9 / 10 : ℝ) * T.card) : ∃ N ∈ T, certifiedKill h N L

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_of_first_harmonic_gap
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_of_first_harmonic_gap {h X L : ℕ} (hX : 0 < X) (hroom : 16 * (2 * X + h + L + 2) ≤ 2 ^ L) (hgap : (∑ N ∈ Finset.Ico X (2 * X), windowFirstCos h N L) ≤ (9 / 10 : ℝ) * X) : ∃ N ∈ Finset.Ico X (2 * X), certifiedKill h N L

declarations.signature: theorem tsum_pos_pair_both_dvd_half_eq_inv_mersenne_sq (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : (∑' p : ℕ × ℕ, if 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ d ∣ p.1 ∧ d ∣ p.2 then ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (p.1 + p.2) else 0) = 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: **Divisibility of the pair factorizes**: the fair-coin mass of `{(a,b) : a,b ≥ 1, d ∣ a, d ∣ b}` is exactly `1/(2ᵈ-1)²` — i.e. `P(d ∣ gcd(X,Y)) = P(d ∣ X)·P(d ∣ Y)`. This is the foundation stone of the squared kernel: `L₂(f) = ∑ f(d)·P(d ∣ gcd)`, and it is also why the Stern–Brocot cylinder closed form `1/((2ᵃ-1)(2ᵇ-1))` is a product of one-variable divisor probabilities.

declarations.signature: theorem tsum_pos_coprime_inv_mersenne_eq_one : (∑' p : ℕ × ℕ, if 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ Nat.Coprime p.1 p.2 then 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (p.1 + p.2) - 1) else 0) = 1
declarations.docstring: **The reduced-direction law**: `∑_{(a,b) coprime, a,b ≥ 1} 1/(2^{a+b}-1) = 1`. Every positive pair `(X,Y)` has a unique reduced slope, and `P(slope = a/b) = ∑_g 2^{-g(a+b)} = 1/(2^{a+b}-1)` for coprime `(a,b)`; the masses sum to one. Proved by expanding each Mersenne reciprocal as its geometric layer series and swapping with the wave-19 gcd-layer normalization. This is the root cylinder of the Stern–Brocot law: `M(1,1) = 1`.

declarations.name: cylinderMass
declarations.signature: noncomputable def cylinderMass (a b : ℕ+) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The closed-form cylinder mass at the coprime node `(a,b)`: `M(a,b) = 1/((2ᵃ-1)(2ᵇ-1)) = P(a ∣ X)·P(b ∣ Y)`.

declarations.name: sternBrocotDepthMass
declarations.signature: noncomputable def sternBrocotDepthMass : ℕ → ℕ+ → ℕ+ → ℝ | 0, _, _ => 0 | (dp + 1), a, b => 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((a : ℕ) + (b : ℕ)) - 1) + sternBrocotDepthMass dp (a + b) b + sternBrocotDepthMass dp a (a + b) private lemma two_le_two_pow (a : ℕ+) : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (a : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: The depth-`d` finite unfolding of the mediant recursion: sum the stop mass `1/(2^{a+b}-1)` at every node of the first `d` generations of the subtree rooted at `(a,b)`, under the children `(a+b, b)` and `(a, a+b)`.

declarations.name: two_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: private lemma two_le_two_pow (a : ℕ+) : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (a : ℕ)

declarations.name: cylinderMass_pos
declarations.signature: theorem cylinderMass_pos (a b : ℕ+) : 0 < cylinderMass a b

declarations.name: cylinderMass_split
declarations.signature: theorem cylinderMass_split (a b : ℕ+) : cylinderMass a b = 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((a : ℕ) + (b : ℕ)) - 1) + cylinderMass (a + b) b + cylinderMass a (a + b)
declarations.docstring: **The exact telescoping recursion of the cylinder mass**: `M(a,b) = 1/(2^{a+b}-1) + M(a+b, b) + M(a, a+b)`. With `A = 2ᵃ`, `B = 2ᵇ` this is `1/((A-1)(B-1)) = 1/(AB-1) + 1/((AB-1)(B-1)) + 1/((A-1)(AB-1))` — the algebra that makes the reduced-direction distribution an exact rational Markov measure on the Stern–Brocot tree.

declarations.name: stop_ge_third_cylinderMass
declarations.signature: private lemma stop_ge_third_cylinderMass (a b : ℕ+) : (1 / 3) * cylinderMass a b ≤ 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((a : ℕ) + (b : ℕ)) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The stop mass at a node is at least a third of its cylinder mass: `(1/3)·M(a,b) ≤ 1/(2^{a+b}-1)`, i.e. `2^{a+b} - 1 ≤ 3(2ᵃ-1)(2ᵇ-1)` — equality exactly at the root `(1,1)`.

declarations.name: cylinderMass_children_le
declarations.signature: theorem cylinderMass_children_le (a b : ℕ+) : cylinderMass (a + b) b + cylinderMass a (a + b) ≤ (2 / 3) * cylinderMass a b
declarations.docstring: The two children carry at most `2/3` of the parent cylinder mass.

declarations.name: sternBrocotDepthMass_error
declarations.signature: theorem sternBrocotDepthMass_error (dp : ℕ) : ∀ a b : ℕ+, 0 ≤ cylinderMass a b - sternBrocotDepthMass dp a b ∧ cylinderMass a b - sternBrocotDepthMass dp a b ≤ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ^ dp * cylinderMass a b
declarations.docstring: **Finite-depth cylinder approximation with explicit geometric rate**: `0 ≤ M(a,b) - M_d(a,b) ≤ (2/3)ᵈ·M(a,b)`. The depth-`d` unfolding of the mediant recursion exhausts the closed form at rate `(2/3)ᵈ`, uniformly over all nodes — the error at depth `d` is exactly the frontier mass, and each generation retains at most `2/3` of its parent mass.

declarations.name: tendsto_sternBrocotDepthMass
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_sternBrocotDepthMass (a b : ℕ+) : Filter.Tendsto (fun dp : ℕ => sternBrocotDepthMass dp a b) Filter.atTop (nhds (cylinderMass a b))
declarations.docstring: **The Stern–Brocot cylinder law, limit form**: the depth-`d` unfolding of the mediant recursion at `(a,b)` converges to the closed form `M(a,b) = 1/((2ᵃ-1)(2ᵇ-1))`, with explicit rate `(2/3)ᵈ` from `sternBrocotDepthMass_error`. declarations.name: says
declarations.signature: theorem says that `X_c` is rational exactly when there is a positive integer `v` and an integer orbit `u(N+1) = 2*u(N) - v*c(N+1)` whose growth is tempered

declarations.name: binaryCoeffSeries
declarations.signature: noncomputable def binaryCoeffSeries (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The binary coefficient series `X_c = ∑_{n≥1} c(n)/2^n`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail
declarations.signature: noncomputable def binaryCoeffTail (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The scaled tail `T_c(N) = ∑_{j≥1} c(N+j)/2^j`.

declarations.name: HasRationalValue
declarations.docstring: A real number represented by an integer numerator and a positive natural denominator. This is the explicit positive-denominator form of membership in `ℚ`; it keeps the carry multiplier visible in theorem statements.

declarations.name: hasRationalValue_iff_not_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem hasRationalValue_iff_not_irrational (x : ℝ) : HasRationalValue x ↔ ¬ Irrational x
declarations.docstring: The explicit positive-denominator predicate is exactly standard rationality (`¬ Irrational x`).

declarations.name: IsTemperedBinaryOrbit
declarations.signature: def IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (c : ℕ → ℕ) (v : ℕ) (u : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The exact integer recurrence together with the subexponential boundary `u(N) = o(2^N)`, expressed as convergence of the quotient.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem binaryCoeffTail_zero (c : ℕ → ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail c 0 = binaryCoeffSeries c
declarations.docstring: The scaled tail at `N = 0` is the original coefficient series.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_nonneg (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N : ℕ) : 0 ≤ binaryCoeffTail c N
declarations.docstring: Nonnegative coefficients give a nonnegative scaled tail.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_le
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_le (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail c N ≤ (N : ℝ) + 2
declarations.docstring: A linear-growth coefficient sequence has the uniform tail bound `T_c(N) ≤ N+2`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_div_pow_tendsto_zero

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_succ

declarations.name: balancedPulseCoeff
declarations.signature: def balancedPulseCoeff (m r : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
declarations.docstring: A two-site pulse whose mass can be moved from position `m` to `m+1` without changing its binary-series value.

declarations.name: balancedPulseCoeff_at_left
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem balancedPulseCoeff_at_left (m r : ℕ) : balancedPulseCoeff m r m = balancedPulseRadius m - r

declarations.name: balancedPulseCoeff_le_self

declarations.name: balancedPulse_weighted_pair

declarations.docstring: Exact cancellation: all pulse parameters have the same two-site binary numerator. This is the finite algebra behind equality of the rational series and of every tail strictly before `m`.

declarations.name: balancedPulse_endpoint_fanout

declarations.docstring: The first tail after the left pulse site decodes the fresh parameter exactly.

declarations.name: balancedPulse_label_injective

declarations.docstring: Any exact label/decoder for the balanced-pulse successors is injective. Consequently its label range has at least `balancedPulseRadius m + 1` elements, which is unbounded with `m`.

declarations.name: balancedPulse_label_card_lower_bound

declarations.name: balancedPulse_fanout_unbounded
declarations.signature: theorem balancedPulse_fanout_unbounded (k : ℕ) : k + 1 ≤ balancedPulseRadius (2 * k) + 1
declarations.docstring: The exact successor fan-out is unbounded along the even pulse locations.

declarations.name: balancedPulse_no_autonomous_decoder

declarations.docstring: **Finite-state no-go.** If a proposed predecessor state identifies all members of one balanced-pulse family (as every state determined by the common pre-`m` history must), no autonomous decoder can recover every exact successor. Layer `g` is the mass of `{gcd = g}`; the `g = 1` layer at `r = 1/2` is the open #249 value `S - 1/2`.

Thus coprime restriction, exact Stern--Brocot splitting, and geometric cylinder decay alone cannot imply irrationality at a rational parameter.

declarations.name: tsum_gcd_layer_pos_coprime_half_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_gcd_layer_pos_coprime_half_eq_one : ∑' g : ℕ, (∑' p : ℕ × ℕ, if 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ Nat.Coprime p.1 p.2 then (((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (g + 1)) ^ (p.1 + p.2) else 0) = 1
declarations.docstring: **The fair-coin gcd law is exactly normalized.** At `r = 1/2` the layer masses are genuine probabilities — layer `g` is `P(gcd(X,Y) = g+1)` for independent fair-coin waiting times — and they sum to `1`: the gcd is finite almost surely. Through the visible-coprime bridge this is precisely the probabilistic content of the wave-18 rational rung `L(φ) = 2`.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRat
declarations.docstring: The exact rational Mersenne weight `1 / (2^n - 1)`. Its meaningful support indices are positive; at index zero Lean's division convention gives zero.

declarations.name: mersenneWeight
declarations.docstring: The real Mersenne weight `1 / (2^n - 1)`.

declarations.name: cast_mersenneWeightRat
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem cast_mersenneWeightRat (n : ℕ) : ((mersenneWeightRat n : ℚ) : ℝ) = mersenneWeight n

declarations.name: mersenneWeight_pos
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeight_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < mersenneWeight n

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRat_pos
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRat_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < mersenneWeightRat n

declarations.name: summable_mersenneWeight
declarations.signature: theorem summable_mersenneWeight : Summable (fun k : ℕ => mersenneWeight (k + 1))
declarations.docstring: The positive-index Mersenne weights form a summable real series.

declarations.name: mersenneTail
declarations.docstring: The remaining mass after processing exponents `1, ..., n`.

declarations.name: summable_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_mersenneTail (n : ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => mersenneWeight (n + k + 1))

declarations.name: mersenneTail_eq_weight_add
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_eq_weight_add (n : ℕ) : mersenneTail n = mersenneWeight (n + 1) + mersenneTail (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Splitting off the next positive exponent gives the exact tail recurrence.

declarations.name: two_mul_mersenneWeight_succ_lt
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_mersenneWeight_succ_lt {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 2 * mersenneWeight (n + 1) < mersenneWeight n
declarations.docstring: Adjacent weights shrink by strictly more than a factor of two.

declarations.name: mersenneWeight_add_le_geometric
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeight_add_le_geometric (n j : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : mersenneWeight (n + j) ≤ mersenneWeight n * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ j
declarations.docstring: Iterating the adjacent ratio gives a geometric envelope.

declarations.name: mersenneTail_le_two_mul_weight
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_le_two_mul_weight (n : ℕ) : mersenneTail n ≤ 2 * mersenneWeight (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: A simple exact-rational upper enclosure for the remaining infinite tail.

declarations.name: mersenneTail_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_lt_weight {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : mersenneTail n < mersenneWeight n
declarations.docstring: **Strict superincreasingness.** Every positive-index weight is larger than the entire tail following it.

declarations.name: mersenneTail_lt_two_mul_weight
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_lt_two_mul_weight (n : ℕ) : mersenneTail n < 2 * mersenneWeight (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The one-step enclosure is in fact strict.

declarations.name: tendsto_mersenneTail_zero
declarations.docstring: The remaining Mersenne mass tends to zero.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainder
declarations.docstring: The contribution of geometric channels of order at least three in one Mersenne weight.

declarations.name: mersenneWeight_eq_two_channels_add_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeight_eq_two_channels_add_remainder {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : mersenneWeight n = ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n + ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n + mersenneWeightRemainder n
declarations.docstring: Exact separation of the first two geometric channels.

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainder_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainder_nonneg {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 ≤ mersenneWeightRemainder n

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainder_pos
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainder_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < mersenneWeightRemainder n

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainder_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : mersenneWeightRemainder n ≤ 2 * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n
declarations.docstring: Uniform third-channel bound for one weight.

declarations.name: tsum_geometric_nat_add_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_geometric_nat_add_succ (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1) (n : ℕ) : ∑' k : ℕ, r ^ (n + k + 1) = r ^ (n + 1) * (1 - r)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: A shifted geometric series in the form used by all three channels.

declarations.name: tsum_half_nat_add_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_half_nat_add_succ (n : ℕ) : ∑' k : ℕ, ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (n + k + 1) = ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n

declarations.name: tsum_quarter_nat_add_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_quarter_nat_add_succ (n : ℕ) : ∑' k : ℕ, ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ (n + k + 1) = (1 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n

declarations.name: tsum_eighth_nat_add_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_eighth_nat_add_succ (n : ℕ) : ∑' k : ℕ, ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ (n + k + 1) = (1 / 7 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainderTail
declarations.docstring: The accumulated contribution of channels of order at least three after exponent `n`.

declarations.name: summable_mersenneWeightRemainderTail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_mersenneWeightRemainderTail (n : ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => mersenneWeightRemainder (n + k + 1))

declarations.name: mersenneWeightRemainderTail_le
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeightRemainderTail_le (n : ℕ) : mersenneWeightRemainderTail n ≤ (2 / 7 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n
declarations.docstring: The accumulated higher-channel tail is at most `(2/7)·8⁻ⁿ`.

declarations.name: one_seventh_eighth_pow_lt_mersenneWeightRemainderTail
declarations.signature: theorem one_seventh_eighth_pow_lt_mersenneWeightRemainderTail (n : ℕ) : (1 / 7 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n < mersenneWeightRemainderTail n
declarations.docstring: The third geometric channel is a strict lower enclosure of the complete higher-channel tail.

declarations.name: mersenneTail_eq_two_channels_add_remainderTail
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_eq_two_channels_add_remainderTail (n : ℕ) : mersenneTail n = ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n + (1 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n + mersenneWeightRemainderTail n
declarations.docstring: Exact tail expansion through the second geometric channel.

declarations.name: mersenneGap_sub_main_eq_remainder_sub_tail
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneGap_sub_main_eq_remainder_sub_tail {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : (mersenneWeight n - mersenneTail n) - (2 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n = mersenneWeightRemainder n - mersenneWeightRemainderTail n
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne gap has leading term `(2/3)·4⁻ⁿ`; its exact error is the difference of the one-weight and tail higher-channel remainders.

declarations.name: mersenneGap_asymptotic_bound
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneGap_asymptotic_bound {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : ‖(mersenneWeight n - mersenneTail n) - (2 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n‖ ≤ 3 * ‖((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n‖
declarations.docstring: Explicit norm certificate for the formal development.s gap asymptotic.

declarations.name: mersenneGap_isBigOWith
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneGap_isBigOWith : Asymptotics.IsBigOWith 3 atTop (fun n : ℕ => (mersenneWeight n - mersenneTail n) - (2 / 3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ^ n) (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **gap asymptotic.** In positive indexing, `w_n - T_n = (2/3)·4⁻ⁿ + O(8⁻ⁿ)`, with an explicit valid `O` constant `3`.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def positiveMersenneSupportValue (A : Set ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The value coded by a set of positive exponents. The sequence index is zero-based while the exponent supplied to the weight is `k+1`.

declarations.name: summable_positiveMersenneSupportIndicator
declarations.signature: theorem summable_positiveMersenneSupportIndicator (A : Set ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => Set.indicator A mersenneWeight (k + 1))

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def positiveMersenneSupportSuffix (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The portion of a support code strictly after exponent `n`.

declarations.name: summable_positiveMersenneSupportSuffix
declarations.signature: theorem summable_positiveMersenneSupportSuffix (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => Set.indicator A mersenneWeight (n + k + 1))

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_nonneg (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_le_tail
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_le_tail (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n ≤ mersenneTail n

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_eq_indicator_add
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_eq_indicator_add (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n = Set.indicator A mersenneWeight (n + 1) + positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact recurrence for a coded support suffix.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_prefix_add_suffix
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_prefix_add_suffix (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportValue A = (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Set.indicator A mersenneWeight (k + 1)) + positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n
declarations.docstring: Finite-prefix decomposition of a normalized support code.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_erdosSupportSeries
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_erdosSupportSeries (A : Set ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportValue A = erdosSupportSeries 2 A
declarations.docstring: The reindexed support value is exactly the existing #257 support series.

declarations.name: mersenneAchievementSet

declarations.name: continuous_positiveMersenneDigitValue
declarations.docstring: The binary support coding is continuous in the product topology.

declarations.name: range_positiveMersenneDigitValue_eq
declarations.docstring: The binary coding has exactly the normalized Mersenne achievement set as its range.

declarations.name: isCompact_mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: **compactness.** The achievement set is the continuous image of compact binary sequence space.

declarations.name: mersenneCylinderStageFrom
declarations.signature: noncomputable def mersenneCylinderStageFrom (n : ℕ) : ℕ → Set ℝ | 0 => Set.Icc 0 (mersenneTail n) | depth + 1 => mersenneCylinderStageFrom (n + 1) depth ∪ (fun x : ℝ => mersenneWeight (n + 1) + x) '' mersenneCylinderStageFrom (n + 1) depth /-- The depth-`n` cylinder enclosure of the full achievement set. -/ noncomputable def mersenneCylinderStage (depth : ℕ) : Set ℝ

declarations.name: mersenneCylinderStage
declarations.signature: noncomputable def mersenneCylinderStage (depth : ℕ) : Set ℝ

declarations.name: mersenneCylinderStageFrom_subset_Icc
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneCylinderStageFrom_subset_Icc (n depth : ℕ) : mersenneCylinderStageFrom n depth ⊆ Set.Icc 0 (mersenneTail n)
declarations.docstring: Every tail-cylinder stage stays inside its unresolved convex hull.

declarations.name: isCompact_mersenneCylinderStageFrom

declarations.name: isClosed_mersenneCylinderStageFrom

declarations.name: disjoint_mersenneCylinderStageFrom_split
declarations.signature: theorem disjoint_mersenneCylinderStageFrom_split (n depth : ℕ) : Disjoint (mersenneCylinderStageFrom (n + 1) depth) ((fun x : ℝ => mersenneWeight (n + 1) + x) '' mersenneCylinderStageFrom (n + 1) depth)

declarations.name: mersenneCylinderStageFrom_succ_subset

declarations.docstring: Increasing the retained depth shrinks the cylinder enclosure.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_zero_index
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_zero_index (A : Set ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A 0 = positiveMersenneSupportValue A

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_diff_current
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_diff_current (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix (A \ {n + 1}) n = positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A (n + 1)

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_insert_current
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_insert_current (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix (insert (n + 1) A) n = mersenneWeight (n + 1) + positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Inserting the current exponent splits off exactly its weight.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_mem_cylinderStageFrom
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportSuffix_mem_cylinderStageFrom (A : Set ℕ) (n depth : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n ∈ mersenneCylinderStageFrom n depth
declarations.docstring: Every coded suffix belongs to every corresponding finite-cylinder enclosure.

declarations.name: exists_normalized_support_near_of_mem_cylinderStageFrom
declarations.signature: theorem exists_normalized_support_near_of_mem_cylinderStageFrom {x : ℝ} {n depth : ℕ} (hx : x ∈ mersenneCylinderStageFrom n depth) : ∃ A : Set ℕ, 0 ∉ A ∧ dist x (positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n) ≤ mersenneTail (n + depth)

declarations.name: mersenneAchievementSet_eq_iInter_cylinderStage

declarations.name: volume_mersenneCylinderStageFrom

declarations.name: volume_mersenneCylinderStage

declarations.name: tendsto_two_pow_mul_mersenneWeightRemainderTail_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_two_pow_mul_mersenneWeightRemainderTail_zero : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n * mersenneWeightRemainderTail n) atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: The higher-channel part of the scaled unresolved tail vanishes.

declarations.name: tendsto_two_pow_mul_mersenneTail_one
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_two_pow_mul_mersenneTail_one : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n * mersenneTail n) atTop (nhds 1)
declarations.docstring: The total length of the level-`n` cylinder cover tends to one.

declarations.name: tendsto_volume_mersenneCylinderStage_one
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_volume_mersenneCylinderStage_one : Tendsto (fun depth : ℕ => volume (mersenneCylinderStage depth)) atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.name: volume_mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: **measure one.** Continuity from above transfers the exact cylinder measures to their decreasing intersection.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder
declarations.signature: noncomputable def greedyMersenneRemainder (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => x | n + 1 => if mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n then greedyMersenneRemainder x n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) else greedyMersenneRemainder x n /-- Exact rational version of the greedy residual. -/ def greedyMersenneRemainderRat (x : ℚ) : ℕ → ℚ | 0 => x | n + 1 => if mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n then greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n - mersenneWeightRat (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Real greedy residual after processing exponents `1, ..., n`.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainderRat
declarations.signature: def greedyMersenneRemainderRat (x : ℚ) : ℕ → ℚ | 0 => x | n + 1 => if mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n then greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n - mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) else greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n @[simp] theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_zero (x : ℝ) : greedyMersenneRemainder x 0 = x
declarations.docstring: Exact rational version of the greedy residual.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_zero (x : ℝ) : greedyMersenneRemainder x 0 = x

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainderRat_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem greedyMersenneRemainderRat_zero (x : ℚ) : greedyMersenneRemainderRat x 0 = x

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_succ
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_succ (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder x (n + 1) = if mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n then greedyMersenneRemainder x n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) else greedyMersenneRemainder x n

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainderRat_succ
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainderRat_succ (x : ℚ) (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainderRat x (n + 1) = if mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n then greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n - mersenneWeightRat (n + 1) else greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n

declarations.name: mersenneSliverCoordinateRat
declarations.docstring: Undoubled excess above the dyadic point at scale `n`. This is the coordinate whose finite-level selected-step law has constant term `-1`. Keeping it separate from the doubled coordinate prevents the two limiting fixed points from being compared under different normalizations.

declarations.name: sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat
declarations.docstring: Doubled excess above the dyadic point at scale `n`. For an exact rational remainder `r`, this is `2 * (2^n * r - 1) * (2^n - 1)`.

declarations.name: sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat_eq_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat_eq_two_mul (n : ℕ) (r : ℚ) : sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat n r = 2 * mersenneSliverCoordinateRat n r

declarations.name: mersenneSliverCoordinateRat_selected_step
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneSliverCoordinateRat_selected_step {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (r : ℚ) : mersenneSliverCoordinateRat (n + 1) (r - mersenneWeightRat (n + 1)) = (4 + 2 / ((2 : ℚ) ^ n - 1)) * mersenneSliverCoordinateRat n r - 1
declarations.docstring: Exact selected-step law for the undoubled coordinate. Its limiting map is `ρ ↦ 4 * ρ - 1`, with limiting fixed point `1 / 3`; the `-2` and `2 / 3` constants belong to `sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat`.

declarations.name: sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat_selected_step
declarations.signature: theorem sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat_selected_step {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (r : ℚ) : sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat (n + 1) (r - mersenneWeightRat (n + 1)) = 4 * sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat n r - 2 + 2 * sharpMersenneSliverCoordinateRat n r / ((2 : ℚ) ^ n - 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite-level selected-step law for the doubled sliver coordinate. The final term is the complete finite-level correction to the limiting map `ρ ↦ 4 * ρ - 2`; no asymptotic estimate is used here.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_nonneg {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n
declarations.docstring: Greedy subtraction preserves nonnegativity.

declarations.name: cast_greedyMersenneRemainderRat
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem cast_greedyMersenneRemainderRat (x : ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ((greedyMersenneRemainderRat x n : ℚ) : ℝ) = greedyMersenneRemainder (x : ℝ) n
declarations.docstring: Rational and real greedy execution agree exactly under casting.

declarations.name: halfDyadicCap
declarations.docstring: The first geometric channel of the Mersenne tail.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap
declarations.docstring: The first two geometric channels of the Mersenne tail. This cap is strictly weaker than the dyadic cap while still lying below the full tail.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_le_cap_of_skipBarrier
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_le_cap_of_skipBarrier (c : ℕ → ℝ) (hbase : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) 0 ≤ c 0) (hselected : ∀ n : ℕ, c n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ c (n + 1)) (hskipped : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n → greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ c (n + 1)) : ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ c n
declarations.docstring: If selected greedy branches transport a cap and skipped branches satisfy the next cap directly, then the cap holds at every level. This isolates the only branch on which a channel-cap proof has a genuine arithmetic burden.

declarations.name: halfDyadicCap_le_halfTwoChannelCap
declarations.signature: theorem halfDyadicCap_le_halfTwoChannelCap (n : ℕ) : halfDyadicCap n ≤ halfTwoChannelCap n
declarations.docstring: The one-channel cap is contained in the two-channel cap.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap_le_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem halfTwoChannelCap_le_mersenneTail (n : ℕ) : halfTwoChannelCap n ≤ mersenneTail n
declarations.docstring: The two-channel cap is a lower enclosure of the exact Mersenne tail.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap_lt_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem halfTwoChannelCap_lt_mersenneTail (n : ℕ) : halfTwoChannelCap n < mersenneTail n
declarations.docstring: The two-channel truncation is strictly below the true tail. The omitted higher channels are the exact positive gap, rather than a factor-two margin against a `2 / 3` sliver threshold.

declarations.name: halfDyadicCap_selected_strict
declarations.signature: theorem halfDyadicCap_selected_strict (n : ℕ) : halfDyadicCap n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) < halfDyadicCap (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: A selected greedy branch transports the dyadic cap strictly.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap_selected_strict
declarations.signature: theorem halfTwoChannelCap_selected_strict (n : ℕ) : halfTwoChannelCap n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) < halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: A selected greedy branch transports the two-channel cap strictly.

declarations.name: halfDyadicCap_selected
declarations.signature: theorem halfDyadicCap_selected (n : ℕ) : halfDyadicCap n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ halfDyadicCap (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Non-strict transport form consumed by the generic skip barrier.

declarations.name: halfTwoChannelCap_selected
declarations.signature: theorem halfTwoChannelCap_selected (n : ℕ) : halfTwoChannelCap n - mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Non-strict transport form consumed by the generic skip barrier.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneSupport
declarations.signature: noncomputable def greedyMersenneSupport (x : ℝ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: The set of positive exponents selected by the real greedy recursion.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneSkippedSupport
declarations.signature: noncomputable def greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (x : ℝ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: The positive exponents omitted by the real greedy recursion.

declarations.name: succ_mem_greedyMersenneSupport_iff
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem succ_mem_greedyMersenneSupport_iff (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x ↔ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n

declarations.name: succ_mem_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_iff
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem succ_mem_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_iff (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ∈ greedyMersenneSkippedSupport x ↔ ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n

declarations.name: greedyMersenne_prefix_add_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenne_prefix_add_remainder (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : x = (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Set.indicator (greedyMersenneSupport x) mersenneWeight (k + 1)) + greedyMersenneRemainder x n
declarations.docstring: Exact finite-prefix identity for the real greedy recursion.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_supportValue
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_supportValue (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (positiveMersenneSupportValue A) n = positiveMersenneSupportSuffix A n
declarations.docstring: On a genuine support value, the greedy residual is exactly the unprocessed support suffix.

declarations.name: succ_mem_greedySupport_supportValue_iff
declarations.signature: theorem succ_mem_greedySupport_supportValue_iff (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ∈ greedyMersenneSupport (positiveMersenneSupportValue A) ↔ n + 1 ∈ A
declarations.docstring: Greedy selection recovers every positive bit of a representing support.

declarations.name: greedySupport_supportValue_eq
declarations.signature: theorem greedySupport_supportValue_eq (A : Set ℕ) (hA0 : 0 ∉ A) : greedyMersenneSupport (positiveMersenneSupportValue A) = A
declarations.docstring: A normalized support is recovered exactly, including the forced-zero bit at exponent zero.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_nonneg (A : Set ℕ) : 0 ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue A
declarations.docstring: Every support value is nonnegative.

declarations.name: greedy_survives_of_mem_mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_survives_of_mem_mersenneAchievementSet {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet) : 0 ≤ x ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n
declarations.docstring: Membership implies the exact all-level upper-tail survival inequalities.

declarations.name: tendsto_greedyMersenneRemainder_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_greedyMersenneRemainder_zero {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hsurvive : ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n) : Tendsto (greedyMersenneRemainder x) atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: If all greedy residuals stay below the remaining mass, they converge to zero. The nonnegativity guard excludes the false negative-target variant.

declarations.name: mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedy_survival
declarations.signature: theorem mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedy_survival {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hsurvive : ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n) : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: All-level survival constructs a genuine normalized support code.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n → greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1)) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: It is enough to establish the two-channel cap only when the actual greedy orbit skips the next exponent. Selected branches and the final membership composition are discharged here.

declarations.name: half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n → greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≤ halfDyadicCap (n + 1)) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: The stronger one-channel skipped-branch obligation is therefore also a sufficient membership criterion.

declarations.name: mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedy_survival
declarations.signature: theorem mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedy_survival (x : ℝ) : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet ↔ 0 ≤ x ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n
declarations.docstring: **Greedy membership criterion.** A real target belongs to the Mersenne achievement set exactly when it is nonnegative and every residual is at most the full remaining tail.

declarations.name: GreedyMersenneFatalAt
declarations.docstring: A greedy state is fatal when its residual is already larger than all remaining Mersenne mass.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneFatalAt_iff_not_survives
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneFatalAt_iff_not_survives (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n ↔ ¬ greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n

declarations.name: greedyMersenneFatalAt_succ
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneFatalAt_succ {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n) : mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n ∧ GreedyMersenneFatalAt x (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Fatality is absorbing: the next exponent is selected and the next state is fatal again.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneFatalAt_add
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneFatalAt_add {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n) (k : ℕ) : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x (n + k)
declarations.docstring: Once a fatal state is reached, every later state is fatal.

declarations.name: mem_greedyMersenneSupport_of_fatalAt_add_succ
declarations.signature: theorem mem_greedyMersenneSupport_of_fatalAt_add_succ {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n) (k : ℕ) : n + k + 1 ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x
declarations.docstring: Every exponent after a fatal state is selected by the greedy recursion.

declarations.name: finite_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_of_fatalAt
declarations.signature: theorem finite_greedyMersenneSkippedSupport_of_fatalAt {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n) : (greedyMersenneSkippedSupport x).Finite
declarations.docstring: A fatal state leaves only finitely many omitted exponents.

declarations.name: mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
declarations.signature: theorem mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedySkippedSupport_infinite {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hskips : (greedyMersenneSkippedSupport x).Infinite) : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Infinitely many omitted exponents rule out every fatal state and hence force exact achievement-set membership.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_injective_normalized
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_injective_normalized {A B : Set ℕ} (hA0 : 0 ∉ A) (hB0 : 0 ∉ B) (hvalue : positiveMersenneSupportValue A = positiveMersenneSupportValue B) : A = B
declarations.docstring: Strict superincreasingness makes normalized support coding injective.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_two_injective_normalized
declarations.signature: theorem erdosSupportSeries_two_injective_normalized {A B : Set ℕ} (hA0 : 0 ∉ A) (hB0 : 0 ∉ B) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = erdosSupportSeries 2 B) : A = B
declarations.docstring: The support coding through the existing #257 series is likewise unique after the zero-bit normalization.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneDigitValue_injective
declarations.docstring: Strict superincreasingness makes the binary coding injective.

declarations.name: mersenneBitFlip
declarations.docstring: Flip one binary coordinate.

declarations.name: mersenneBitFlip_ne
