declarations.name: linearIndependent_totientOddKernelFamily
declarations.signature: theorem linearIndependent_totientOddKernelFamily (e : ℕ) (hcanon : LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientOddKernelFamily e)
declarations.docstring: Linear independence of the full canonical family restricts to the odd canonical channels.

declarations.name: linearIndependent_totientOddKernelFamily_of_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem linearIndependent_totientOddKernelFamily_of_certificate (e : ℕ) (cert : SeparatedMinorCertificate (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientOddKernelFamily e)
declarations.docstring: A separated minor for the canonical family already certifies independence of all its odd channels.

declarations.name: canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_eq_smul_totient
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_eq_smul_totient {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (e : ℕ) : canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily u e = fun i => (v : ℚ) • canonicalTotientOddKernelFamily e i
declarations.docstring: The recurrence identifies the canonical carry differences with the odd totient channels, scaled by the orbit multiplier.

declarations.name: canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_mem_span
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_mem_span (u : ℕ → ℤ) (e : ℕ) (i : TotientOddIndex e) : canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily u e i ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e))
declarations.docstring: Every canonical carry difference lies in the span of the full finite-level carry family.

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_linearIndependent
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_linearIndependent {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hv : 0 < v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (e : ℕ) (hcanon : LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: **Finite-level carry anti-compression.** A nonzero-multiplier orbit whose canonical totient family is linearly independent must retain at least `2^e-1` dimensions among its carry sections through level `e`. Temperedness is not used beyond supplying the exact recurrence through the existing orbit interface.

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_certificate {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hv : 0 < v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (e : ℕ) (cert : SeparatedMinorCertificate (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: Certificate-facing form of `finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_linearIndependent`. This is immediately usable with the existing finite separated-minor owner.

declarations.name: not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_unbounded_carryRank
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_unbounded_carryRank (hcanon : ∀ e : ℕ, LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) (hirr : ¬ Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries Nat.totient)) : ∃ v : ℕ, 0 < v ∧ ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: Rationality of the totient coefficient series, together with an all-level canonical independence producer, yields one tempered integral carry whose finite-level section ranks grow at least as `2^e-1`.

declarations.name: not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_unbounded_carryRank_unconditional
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_unbounded_carryRank_unconditional (hirr : ¬ Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries Nat.totient)) : ∃ v : ℕ, 0 < v ∧ ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional anti-compression consequence of the CRT--Dirichlet minor.** If the totient series were rational, its tempered integral carry would have unbounded dyadic section rank. This does not by itself prove irrationality: a separate theorem bounding the dyadic section rank of every rationality-supplied tempered carry is still required, and no such finite-rank compression theorem follows from the recurrence and temperedness alone.

declarations.name: exponent_mul_primeFactors_card_lt
declarations.signature: theorem exponent_mul_primeFactors_card_lt {a n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hrough : ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ n → 2 ^ a < r) (hnPow : n < 2 ^ (2 * 2 ^ a)) : a * n.primeFactors.card < 2 * 2 ^ a
declarations.docstring: A `2^a`-rough integer below the actual-LCM height range has at most `2/a` as many distinct prime factors as the roughness cutoff. This is the vanishing version of the fixed `1/4` estimate used by the sign corridor.

declarations.name: one_sub_two_div_lt_totient_density_of_rough
declarations.signature: theorem one_sub_two_div_lt_totient_density_of_rough {a n : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hn : 0 < n) (hrough : ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ n → 2 ^ a < r) (hnPow : n < 2 ^ (2 * 2 ^ a)) : (n : ℚ) * (1 - (2 : ℚ) / a) < Nat.totient n
declarations.docstring: Quantitative rough Euler-density estimate. The defect is less than `2/a`, so the density tends to one along the power-of-two LCM scale without using the prime number theorem.

declarations.name: clean_periodLcm_divisor_of_sq_le
declarations.signature: theorem clean_periodLcm_divisor_of_sq_le {t j : ℕ} (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ t) : j ∣ periodLcm t ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ j → p ∣ periodLcm t / j
declarations.docstring: If `j² ≤ t`, then `j` is not merely a divisor of `L(t)`: every prime of `j` still occurs in the complementary cofactor `L(t) / j`. The square cutoff is the elementary uniform range in which the exact ray factorisation can be used without inspecting the prime-power exponents of `j`.

declarations.name: three_mul_periodLcm_add_one_lt_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem three_mul_periodLcm_add_one_lt_two_pow {a : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) : 3 * periodLcm (2 ^ a) + 1 < 2 ^ (2 * 2 ^ a)
declarations.docstring: The three fixed ray endpoints fit below the rough-density height range. The twelve-bit saving for the actual LCM makes this a completely elementary consequence, with ample room for the additive endpoint.

declarations.name: clean_ray_cofactor_primeFactors_gt
declarations.signature: theorem clean_ray_cofactor_primeFactors_gt {t j q r : ℕ} (hj : j ∣ periodLcm t) (hclean : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ j → p ∣ periodLcm t / j) (hr : Nat.Prime r) (hrdvd : r ∣ q * (periodLcm t / j) + 1) : t < r
declarations.docstring: A clean LCM-ray cofactor has no prime at or below the LCM cutoff.

declarations.name: fixed_rank_clean_endpoint_totient_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem fixed_rank_clean_endpoint_totient_bounds {a j q : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ 2 ^ a) (hq : q ≤ 3) : let H
declarations.docstring: Uniform fixed-rank ray estimate. On every clean offset `j² ≤ 2^a` and every rank `q ≤ 3`, the exact endpoint totient differs from its affine main term `φ(j)·(q·(H/j)+1)` by a relative amount below `2/a`. This is the quantitative input needed to make every fixed-rank second difference `o(H)`; unlike the earlier fixed `3/4` corridor, its error tends to zero with the LCM scale.

declarations.name: fixedRankEndpointDefect
declarations.signature: def fixedRankEndpointDefect (a j q : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The nonnegative loss from the affine fixed-rank main term.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference
declarations.docstring: The integral second difference across the first three positive LCM ranks. Its coefficient vector `(1,-2,1)` has `ℓ¹` height four.

declarations.name: MiddleRankTotientExtremal
declarations.docstring: The exact ordering socket for the fixed-rank curvature: the rank-two totient is strictly below both outer ranks or strictly above both of them. This is the local conclusion supplied by any factor-separated ordering of the three nonproportional linear forms. The unresolved arithmetic step for Erdős #249 is to force this socket on cofinally many prescribed LCM heights, not merely on a positive-density set of unrestricted heights.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_pos_of_middle_strict_min
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_pos_of_middle_strict_min {H j : ℕ} (hleft : Nat.totient (2 * H + j) < Nat.totient (H + j)) (hright : Nat.totient (2 * H + j) < Nat.totient (3 * H + j)) : 0 < fixedRankSecondDifference H j
declarations.docstring: If the middle-rank totient is the strict minimum, the primitive three-rank curvature is positive.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_neg_of_middle_strict_max
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_neg_of_middle_strict_max {H j : ℕ} (hleft : Nat.totient (H + j) < Nat.totient (2 * H + j)) (hright : Nat.totient (3 * H + j) < Nat.totient (2 * H + j)) : fixedRankSecondDifference H j < 0
declarations.docstring: If the middle-rank totient is the strict maximum, the primitive three-rank curvature is negative.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_ne_zero_of_middleRankTotientExtremal
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_ne_zero_of_middleRankTotientExtremal {H j : ℕ} (h : MiddleRankTotientExtremal H j) : fixedRankSecondDifference H j ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: A middle-extremal ordering is already enough to separate the normalized fixed-rank curvature from zero; no quantitative gap is required.

declarations.name: PowerTwoLcmMiddleRankExtremalSupply
declarations.docstring: The specified sparse-orbit input suggested by simultaneous totient ordering results: a fixed offset whose rank-two value is extremal at arbitrarily large power-of-two LCM heights.

declarations.name: cofinal_fixedRankSecondDifference_ne_zero_of_middleRankExtremalSupply
declarations.signature: theorem cofinal_fixedRankSecondDifference_ne_zero_of_middleRankExtremalSupply {j : ℕ} (h : PowerTwoLcmMiddleRankExtremalSupply j) : ∀ A : ℕ, ∃ a : ℕ, A ≤ a ∧ fixedRankSecondDifference (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) j ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The exact Lean consumer of the sparse-orbit ordering wish. Once the middle-extremal ordering is transferred to cofinally many LCM heights, the primitive fixed-rank curvature is nonzero at those same heights.

declarations.name: affine_rank_three_kernel_classification
declarations.signature: theorem affine_rank_three_kernel_classification {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℤ} (hzero : c₁ + c₂ + c₃ = 0) (hlinear : c₁ + 2 * c₂ + 3 * c₃ = 0) : c₁ = c₃ ∧ c₂ = -2 * c₃ ∧ |c₁| + |c₂| + |c₃| = 4 * |c₃|
declarations.docstring: The primitive three-coordinate kernel annihilating both the constant and linear rank moments is unique. The pivot minor on the first two columns is `1`, hence odd; no hidden lattice index enlarges the primitive kernel.

declarations.name: affine_rank_three_pivotMinor_odd
declarations.docstring: The chosen affine-moment pivot minor is an odd unit.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_two_mul_even
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_two_mul_even {H j : ℕ} (hH : Even H) (hj : Even j) : fixedRankSecondDifference (2 * H) (2 * j) = 2 * fixedRankSecondDifference H j
declarations.docstring: Exact dyadic scaling of the primitive rank curvature when the reduced height and offset are even.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_two_mul_odd
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_two_mul_odd {H j : ℕ} (hH : Even H) (hj : Odd j) : fixedRankSecondDifference (2 * H) (2 * j) = fixedRankSecondDifference H j
declarations.docstring: Exact dyadic scaling of the primitive rank curvature at an odd reduced offset: the final factor of two does not enlarge the curvature.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_two_pow_succ_mul
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_two_pow_succ_mul (H j n : ℕ) (hH : Even H) (hj : Odd j) : fixedRankSecondDifference (2 ^ (n + 1) * H) (2 ^ (n + 1) * j) = (2 : ℤ) ^ n * fixedRankSecondDifference H j
declarations.docstring: Iterating the parity split gives the exact valuation contribution of a dyadically scaled odd offset.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_even
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_even {H j : ℕ} (hH : 2 ≤ H) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : Even (fixedRankSecondDifference H j)
declarations.docstring: Every positive-offset curvature above height two is even.

declarations.name: two_pow_succ_dvd_fixedRankSecondDifference
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_succ_dvd_fixedRankSecondDifference (H j n : ℕ) (hH : Even H) (hHtwo : 2 ≤ H) (hj : Odd j) : (2 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1) ∣ fixedRankSecondDifference (2 ^ (n + 1) * H) (2 ^ (n + 1) * j)
declarations.docstring: The primitive rank kernel acquires exactly the expected growing dyadic divisor on scaled odd offsets.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_dyadic_fixture_exact
declarations.docstring: Sharpness of the two-adic theorem: the normalized one-by-one minor is odd at every depth. Thus the bounded-height primitive kernel alone cannot force even one additional factor of two.

declarations.name: fixedRankEndpointDefect_nonneg_and_lt
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankEndpointDefect_nonneg_and_lt {a j q : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ 2 ^ a) (hq : q ≤ 3) : 0 ≤ fixedRankEndpointDefect a j q ∧ fixedRankEndpointDefect a j q < (Nat.totient j : ℚ) * ((q * (periodLcm (2 ^ a) / j) + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) * (2 / (a : ℚ))
declarations.docstring: The fixed-rank endpoint defect is nonnegative and has relative size strictly below `2/a`.

declarations.name: fixedRankSecondDifference_periodLcm_eq_mul
declarations.signature: theorem fixedRankSecondDifference_periodLcm_eq_mul {t j : ℕ} (hjdvd : j ∣ periodLcm t) (hclean : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ j → p ∣ periodLcm t / j) : fixedRankSecondDifference (periodLcm t) j = (Nat.totient j : ℤ) * ((Nat.totient (3 * (periodLcm t / j) + 1) : ℤ) - 2 * Nat.totient (2 * (periodLcm t / j) + 1) + Nat.totient (periodLcm t / j + 1))
declarations.docstring: Exact clean-ray factorisation of the primitive rank curvature.

declarations.name: two_mul_totient_dvd_fixedRankSecondDifference
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_totient_dvd_fixedRankSecondDifference {a j : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ 2 ^ a) : (2 * (Nat.totient j : ℤ)) ∣ fixedRankSecondDifference (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) j
declarations.docstring: On the square-root clean window the primitive curvature is divisible by `2·φ(j)`. The factor `φ(j)` is the exact local ray factor; the extra `2` comes from parity of the three odd rough cofactors.

declarations.name: fixed_rank_secondDifference_abs_lt
declarations.signature: theorem fixed_rank_secondDifference_abs_lt {a j : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ 2 ^ a) : let H
declarations.docstring: **Fixed-offset second-rank cancellation.** On every clean offset in the square-root window, the three endpoint ranks have an affine main term, so its second difference vanishes. What remains is bounded by the sum of three nonnegative rough-Euler defects, hence is `O(H/a)` with an explicit constant. This is a rigorous nonlinear normalization unavailable to any fixed-density estimate: the right-hand side is `o(H)` for every fixed offset `j`.

declarations.name: exists_primitive_fixedRankCurvature_with_bound
declarations.signature: theorem exists_primitive_fixedRankCurvature_with_bound {a j : ℕ} (ha : 4 ≤ a) (hj : 0 < j) (hsq : j * j ≤ 2 ^ a) : ∃ z : ℤ, fixedRankSecondDifference (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) j = (2 * (Nat.totient j : ℤ)) * z ∧ |(z : ℚ)| < ((8 * (periodLcm (2 ^ a) / j) + 4 : ℕ) : ℚ) / a ∧ (z = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ |z|)
declarations.docstring: **Primitive localized curvature.** After removing the exact local factor `2·φ(j)`, the three-rank curvature is an integer whose Archimedean height is strictly below `(8·H/j+4)/a`. The final disjunction is the exact second-order anti-concentration boundary: the normalized curvature either vanishes, or its absolute value is at least one. Thus any future argument only has to separate this primitive integer from zero; no coefficient gcd or hidden lattice index remains.

declarations.name: totientKernelSeq
declarations.signature: def totientKernelSeq (j r : ℕ) : ℕ → ℚ
declarations.docstring: The `(j,r)` dyadic-kernel channel of Euler's totient, viewed over `ℚ`.

declarations.name: TotientCanonicalIndex
declarations.docstring: The canonical channels through level `e`: the two zero-residue base channels, followed by every odd residue at levels `1,...,e`.

declarations.name: canonicalTotientKernelFamily

declarations.docstring: The canonical family indexed without duplicate even-residue channels.

declarations.name: card_totientCanonicalIndex
declarations.signature: theorem card_totientCanonicalIndex (e : ℕ) : Fintype.card (TotientCanonicalIndex e) = 2 ^ e + 1
declarations.docstring: The canonical family has exactly `2^e+1` channels.

declarations.name: linearIndependent_of_separatedMinorCertificate

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq_of_linearIndependent
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq_of_linearIndependent (e : ℕ) (hcanon : LinearIndependent ℚ (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e))) = 2 ^ e + 1

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq_of_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq_of_certificate (e : ℕ) (cert : SeparatedMinorCertificate (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e)) : finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e))) = 2 ^ e + 1
declarations.docstring: A separated minor for the canonical family gives the exact finite-level dimension promised by the dyadic rank route.

declarations.name: totient_two_pow_succ_mul_of_odd
declarations.signature: theorem totient_two_pow_succ_mul_of_odd (t m : ℕ) (hm : Odd m) : Nat.totient (2 ^ (t + 1) * m) = 2 ^ t * Nat.totient m

declarations.name: totient_two_pow_mul_two

declarations.name: totientKernel_zero_residue

declarations.name: TotientAffineIndex

declarations.name: totientAffineResidue
declarations.signature: def totientAffineResidue {e : ℕ} : TotientAffineIndex e → ℕ | none => 0 | some ⟨_, r⟩ => 2 * r.val + 1 /-- The natural-valued normalized affine channel. -/ def totientAffineValue {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Residue of a normalized affine totient channel.

declarations.name: totientAffineValue
declarations.signature: def totientAffineValue {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The natural-valued normalized affine channel.

declarations.name: totientAffineFamily
declarations.signature: def totientAffineFamily (e : ℕ) : TotientAffineIndex e → ℕ → ℚ
declarations.docstring: The normalized family of totient sequences used on odd evaluation rows.

declarations.name: totientAffineOddFamily
declarations.signature: def totientAffineOddFamily (e : ℕ) : TotientAffineIndex e → ℕ → ℚ

declarations.name: totientAffineSlope_pos
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineSlope_pos {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : 0 < totientAffineSlope i

declarations.name: totientAffineResidue_lt_slope
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineResidue_lt_slope {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : totientAffineResidue i < totientAffineSlope i

declarations.name: totientAffineSlope_coprime_residue
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineSlope_coprime_residue {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : (totientAffineSlope i).Coprime (totientAffineResidue i)

declarations.name: totientAffine_parameters_injective
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffine_parameters_injective (e : ℕ) : Function.Injective (fun i : TotientAffineIndex e => (totientAffineSlope i, totientAffineResidue i))
declarations.docstring: The slope-residue pair uniquely identifies a normalized channel.

declarations.name: totientAffine_cross_ne
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffine_cross_ne {e : ℕ} {i j : TotientAffineIndex e} (hij : i ≠ j) : totientAffineSlope j * totientAffineResidue i ≠ totientAffineSlope i * totientAffineResidue j
declarations.docstring: Distinct normalized affine channels have nonzero cross determinant.

declarations.name: totientAffineBaseResidue
declarations.signature: def totientAffineBaseResidue {e : ℕ} : TotientAffineIndex e → ℕ | none => 3 | some _ => 1 theorem totientAffineBaseResidue_odd {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : Odd (totientAffineBaseResidue i)
declarations.docstring: The prescribed residue class for an evaluation input. The zero channel uses `3 mod 2^(e+3)` so that a prime value has totient exactly `2 mod 4`; every positive-slope odd channel uses `1`.

declarations.name: totientAffineBaseResidue_odd
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineBaseResidue_odd {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : Odd (totientAffineBaseResidue i)

declarations.name: totientAffineCore
declarations.signature: def totientAffineCore {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The fixed low two-adic part of the target prime minus one.

declarations.name: totientAffineBaseResidue_lt_modulus
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineBaseResidue_lt_modulus {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : totientAffineBaseResidue i < 2 ^ (e + 3)

declarations.name: totientAffineCore_pos
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineCore_pos {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : 0 < totientAffineCore i

declarations.name: totientAffineCore_even
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineCore_even {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : Even (totientAffineCore i)

declarations.name: totientAffineCore_lt_depthBound
declarations.signature: theorem totientAffineCore_lt_depthBound {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : totientAffineCore i < 2 ^ (e + 2)

declarations.name: exists_totientAffineCore_depth
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientAffineCore_depth {e : ℕ} (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : ∃ d u : ℕ, d < e + 2 ∧ Odd u ∧ totientAffineCore i = 2 ^ d * u
declarations.docstring: Exact two-adic depth of the target core, bounded strictly below the depth forced on every off-target column.

declarations.name: exists_large_distinct_primes_modEq_one
declarations.signature: theorem exists_large_distinct_primes_modEq_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (K B : ℕ) : ∃ q : ι → ℕ, Function.Injective q ∧ ∀ i, (q i).Prime ∧ q i ≡ 1 [MOD 2 ^ K] ∧ B < q i
declarations.docstring: Uniformly choose distinct fresh primes in the class `1 mod 2^K` for a finite collection of off-target channels.

declarations.name: exists_affine_root_mod_prime
declarations.signature: theorem exists_affine_root_mod_prime {a r q : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (haq : a < q) (hq : q.Prime) : ∃ x < q, q ∣ a * x + r
declarations.docstring: A nonzero affine slope has a root modulo any larger prime.

declarations.name: affine_target_coprime_of_cross
declarations.signature: theorem affine_target_coprime_of_cross {ai ri aj rj q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hcross : aj * ri ≠ ai * rj) (hleft : aj * ri < q) (hright : ai * rj < q) (hoff : q ∣ aj * n + rj) : (ai * n + ri).Coprime q
declarations.docstring: If one affine value vanishes modulo a prime and the cross determinant is nonzero and smaller than that prime, then the other affine value is coprime to the prime.

declarations.name: TotientAffinePrimeRow
declarations.docstring: A CRT--Dirichlet row: the target affine value is prime, while every other affine value has a distinct prime divisor congruent to one modulo the common dyadic modulus.

declarations.name: exists_totientAffinePrimeRow
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientAffinePrimeRow (e : ℕ) (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : Nonempty (TotientAffinePrimeRow e i)
declarations.docstring: CRT plus Dirichlet constructs a prime row for every target channel. Only one value is required to be prime; the off-target values merely receive fresh prime divisors.

declarations.name: TotientAffineParityRow
declarations.docstring: The parity data extracted from a prime row.

declarations.name: exists_totientAffineParityRow
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientAffineParityRow (e : ℕ) (i : TotientAffineIndex e) : Nonempty (TotientAffineParityRow e i)
declarations.docstring: A prime row gives one low-depth diagonal entry and uniformly high-depth off-diagonal entries.

declarations.name: paritySeparatedMatrix_det_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem paritySeparatedMatrix_det_ne_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Matrix ι ι ℕ) (depth : ι → ℕ) (hdiv : ∀ i j, 2 ^ depth j ∣ M i j) (hdiag : ∀ i, Odd (M i i / 2 ^ depth i)) (hoff : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Even (M i j / 2 ^ depth j)) : Matrix.det (fun i j => (M i j : ℚ)) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: A square natural matrix whose columns admit fixed powers of two and whose quotient is the identity modulo two has nonzero determinant over `ℚ`. This is the finite linear-algebra consumer for the CRT--Dirichlet rows below: the target entry in column `j` has exact two-adic depth `depth j`, while every off-target entry has at least one additional factor of two.

declarations.name: exists_separatedMinorCertificate_totientAffineOddFamily
declarations.docstring: The CRT--Dirichlet rows assemble into a nonzero evaluation minor for the normalized family on odd inputs.

declarations.name: linearIndependent_totientAffineOddFamily
declarations.signature: theorem linearIndependent_totientAffineOddFamily (e : ℕ) : LinearIndependent ℚ (totientAffineOddFamily e)
declarations.docstring: Unconditional linear independence of the normalized odd-input totient channels at every finite dyadic level.

declarations.name: linearIndependent_canonicalTotientKernelFamily
declarations.docstring: The full canonical family is linearly independent. Odd inputs first separate the combined pair `φ(n), φ(2n)` from every odd residue channel; the single even input `n = 2` then separates those two remaining columns.

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalTotientKernel_eq (e : ℕ) : finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e))) = 2 ^ e + 1
declarations.docstring: Exact unconditional finite-level rank of the canonical totient kernel.

declarations.name: TotientDyadicKernelIndex
declarations.docstring: The full dyadic kernel index, with the canonical residue range `0 ≤ r < 2^j` at every level `j`.

declarations.name: fullTotientKernelFamily
declarations.signature: def fullTotientKernelFamily : TotientDyadicKernelIndex → ℕ → ℚ | ⟨j, r⟩ => totientKernelSeq j r.val /-- The canonical independent family through level `e` embeds into the full dyadic kernel. -/ def canonicalTotientKernelToFull {e : ℕ} : TotientCanonicalIndex e → TotientDyadicKernelIndex | Sum.inl i => ⟨i.val, ⟨0,
declarations.docstring: Every canonical dyadic section of Euler's totient.

declarations.name: canonicalTotientKernelToFull
declarations.signature: def canonicalTotientKernelToFull {e : ℕ} : TotientCanonicalIndex e → TotientDyadicKernelIndex | Sum.inl i => ⟨i.val, ⟨0,
declarations.docstring: The canonical independent family through level `e` embeds into the full dyadic kernel.

declarations.name: fullTotientKernelFamily_canonicalTotientKernelToFull
declarations.signature: theorem fullTotientKernelFamily_canonicalTotientKernelToFull {e : ℕ} (i : TotientCanonicalIndex e) : fullTotientKernelFamily (canonicalTotientKernelToFull i) = canonicalTotientKernelFamily e i

declarations.name: range_canonicalTotientKernelFamily_subset_full
declarations.signature: theorem range_canonicalTotientKernelFamily_subset_full (e : ℕ) : Set.range (canonicalTotientKernelFamily e) ⊆ Set.range fullTotientKernelFamily
declarations.docstring: Every canonical finite-level channel is a member of the full dyadic kernel.

declarations.name: nat_le_two_pow_self
declarations.signature: private theorem nat_le_two_pow_self (n : ℕ) : n ≤ 2 ^ n

declarations.name: not_finiteDimensional_span_fullTotientKernel
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional infinite dyadic-kernel rank.** The span of all dyadic sections `n ↦ φ(2^j n + r)` is not finite-dimensional over `ℚ`. Indeed, at every depth `e` it contains the canonical independent family of exact rank `2^e+1`; choosing `e` equal to a hypothetical ambient finrank gives an immediate contradiction.

declarations.name: CompressedAdjointCertificate
declarations.docstring: The exact proof object required from a future totient-specific compressed adjoint construction.

declarations.name: false_of_compressedAdjointCertificate
declarations.signature: theorem false_of_compressedAdjointCertificate {v : ℕ} (cert : CompressedAdjointCertificate v) : False
declarations.docstring: A compressed-adjoint certificate is impossible: its boundary is both a nonzero multiple of `Q*v` and strictly smaller than `Q*v`.

declarations.name: IsLargePowerTwo
declarations.docstring: Lacunary spike ranks `2^(k+3)`, beginning at `8`.

declarations.name: largePowerTwoBit
declarations.docstring: The zero-one indicator of the lacunary spike ranks.

declarations.name: parityBaseWeight
declarations.signature: def parityBaseWeight : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | 1 => 1 | 2 => 1 | 3 => 2 | _ => 4 private theorem parityBaseWeight_eq_four_of_four_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n) : parityBaseWeight n = 4
declarations.docstring: Rational base coefficients before adding zero-valued sparse carries.

declarations.name: parityBaseWeight_eq_four_of_four_le
declarations.signature: private theorem parityBaseWeight_eq_four_of_four_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n) : parityBaseWeight n = 4

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight
declarations.docstring: The parity countermodel. Natural subtraction is exact because every negative spike lands on a base coefficient `4`.

declarations.name: largePowerTwoBit_eq_zero_of_lt_eight
declarations.signature: theorem largePowerTwoBit_eq_zero_of_lt_eight {n : ℕ} (hn : n < 8) : largePowerTwoBit n = 0

declarations.name: not_isLargePowerTwo_of_between
declarations.signature: theorem not_isLargePowerTwo_of_between {k n : ℕ} (hlow : 2 ^ (k + 3) < n) (hhigh : n < 2 ^ (k + 4)) : ¬ IsLargePowerTwo n

declarations.name: largePowerTwoBit_eq_zero_of_between
declarations.signature: theorem largePowerTwoBit_eq_zero_of_between {k n : ℕ} (hlow : 2 ^ (k + 3) < n) (hhigh : n < 2 ^ (k + 4)) : largePowerTwoBit n = 0

declarations.name: largePowerTwoBit_pred_forces_base_four
declarations.signature: private theorem largePowerTwoBit_pred_forces_base_four {n : ℕ} (hpred : largePowerTwoBit (n - 1) = 1) : parityBaseWeight n = 4 ∧ largePowerTwoBit n = 0

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_cast
declarations.signature: theorem parityCoboundaryWeight_cast (n : ℕ) : (parityCoboundaryWeight n : ℤ) = (parityBaseWeight n : ℤ) + 2 * largePowerTwoBit n - 4 * largePowerTwoBit (n - 1)
declarations.docstring: The natural subtraction in the definition is genuine integer subtraction; this is the algebraic coboundary normal form.

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_le_self
declarations.signature: theorem parityCoboundaryWeight_le_self (n : ℕ) : parityCoboundaryWeight n ≤ n

declarations.name: totient_even_of_three_le
declarations.signature: private theorem totient_even_of_three_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : Even (Nat.totient n)

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_mod_two_eq_totient
declarations.signature: theorem parityCoboundaryWeight_mod_two_eq_totient (n : ℕ) : parityCoboundaryWeight n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2
declarations.docstring: Exact parity agreement with Euler's totient.

declarations.name: parityBaseWeight_le_four
declarations.signature: private theorem parityBaseWeight_le_four (n : ℕ) : parityBaseWeight n ≤ 4

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_le_six
declarations.docstring: The countermodel uses only the six coefficient values below `7`. Thus finite-valuedness alone does not repair the parity-and-aperiodicity route; one needs a digit/no-carry constraint or genuinely arithmetic information.

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_pow
declarations.docstring: Every lacunary spike really attains the upper value six. Together with `parityCoboundaryWeight_pow_succ`, this exposes the nonperiodic `6,0` carry markers directly, rather than hiding them behind the uniform bound.

declarations.name: summable_parityBaseWeight
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_parityBaseWeight : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (parityBaseWeight n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)

declarations.name: tsum_parityBaseWeight
declarations.signature: private theorem tsum_parityBaseWeight : (∑' n : ℕ, (parityBaseWeight n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) = 3 / 2

declarations.name: summable_largePowerTwoBit
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_largePowerTwoBit : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (largePowerTwoBit n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)

declarations.name: summable_shiftedLargePowerTwoBit
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_shiftedLargePowerTwoBit : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (largePowerTwoBit (n - 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)

declarations.name: tsum_sparse_coboundary_zero
declarations.signature: private theorem tsum_sparse_coboundary_zero : (∑' n : ℕ, (2 * (largePowerTwoBit n : ℝ) - 4 * largePowerTwoBit (n - 1)) / 2 ^ n) = 0

declarations.name: summable_parityCoboundaryWeight
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_parityCoboundaryWeight : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (parityCoboundaryWeight n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)

declarations.name: tsum_parityCoboundaryWeight_eq_three_halves
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_parityCoboundaryWeight_eq_three_halves : (∑' n : ℕ, (parityCoboundaryWeight n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) = 3 / 2
declarations.docstring: Despite parity agreement, linear bounds, and sparse aperiodicity, the countermodel has the rational dyadic value `3/2`.

declarations.name: exists_later_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pair
declarations.signature: theorem exists_later_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pair (N : ℕ) : ∃ n : ℕ, N < n ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight n = 6 ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight (n + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: The explicit `6,0` carry markers occur cofinally, not just at a named lacunary sequence. This is the cutoff-shaped interface used by arguments that would otherwise have to unpack the powers-of-two witness themselves.

declarations.name: exists_later_separated_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pairs
declarations.signature: theorem exists_later_separated_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pairs (N G : ℕ) : ∃ n m : ℕ, N < n ∧ n + G < m ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight n = 6 ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight (n + 1) = 0 ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight m = 6 ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight (m + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: Two visible carry pairs can be found beyond any cutoff with any prescribed gap between them. Thus the rational countermodel retains arbitrarily sparse, cofinally recurring carry markers.

declarations.name: exists_later_arbitrarily_many_separated_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pairs
declarations.signature: theorem exists_later_arbitrarily_many_separated_parityCoboundaryWeight_carry_pairs (N G K : ℕ) : ∃ k : ℕ, N < 2 ^ (k + 3) ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, i < K → 2 ^ (k + i + 3) + G < 2 ^ (k + i + 4) ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight (2 ^ (k + i + 3)) = 6 ∧ parityCoboundaryWeight (2 ^ (k + i + 3) + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: Beyond every cutoff, the rational witness contains arbitrarily long blocks of visible carry pairs with a prescribed gap between consecutive markers. The block uses consecutive powers of two; the base exponent is chosen far enough out that every doubling clears the requested gap.

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_not_eventually_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem parityCoboundaryWeight_not_eventually_periodic : ¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → parityCoboundaryWeight (n + p) = parityCoboundaryWeight n
declarations.docstring: The coefficient word is not eventually periodic.

declarations.name: parityCoboundaryWeight_not_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem parityCoboundaryWeight_not_irrational : ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (parityCoboundaryWeight n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The countermodel's dyadic value is rational.

declarations.name: exists_totientParity_linear_aperiodic_rational_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientParity_linear_aperiodic_rational_countermodel : ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, c n ≤ 6) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, c n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2) ∧ (¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → c (n + p) = c n) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (c n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **Route-pruning theorem for Erdős #249.** Uniform finite-valuedness, natural-valued linear growth, exact agreement with the totient coefficients modulo two, and failure of eventual periodicity do not by themselves force irrationality of a binary coefficient series. The witness is explicit, bounded by six, and has value `3/2`. This theorem rules out only that proof interface; it makes no claim about the actual totient series.

declarations.name: exists_totientParity_explicitCarry_rational_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientParity_explicitCarry_rational_countermodel : ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ k, c (2 ^ (k + 3)) = 6 ∧ c (2 ^ (k + 3) + 1) = 0) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ 6) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, c n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2) ∧ (¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → c (n + p) = c n) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (c n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The route-pruning witness can be chosen with explicit lacunary binary carry pairs: every spike coefficient is six and its successor is zero. Thus the rationality mechanism survives even after the nonperiodicity witness is made completely visible in the theorem statement.

declarations.name: exists_totientParity_cofinalCarry_rational_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientParity_cofinalCarry_rational_countermodel : ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ N, ∃ n, N < n ∧ c n = 6 ∧ c (n + 1) = 0) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ 6) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, c n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2) ∧ (¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → c (n + p) = c n) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (c n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The same rational countermodel has a visible `6,0` carry pair beyond every cutoff. Hence even cofinally recurring, unboundedly located carry markers do not rescue the parity-plus-aperiodicity irrationality route.

declarations.name: exists_totientParity_separatedCarry_rational_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientParity_separatedCarry_rational_countermodel : ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ N G, ∃ n m, N < n ∧ n + G < m ∧ c n = 6 ∧ c (n + 1) = 0 ∧ c m = 6 ∧ c (m + 1) = 0) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ 6) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, c n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2) ∧ (¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → c (n + p) = c n) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (c n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: Even cofinal carry pairs with arbitrarily large prescribed separation do not rescue the parity-and-aperiodicity route: the witness remains bounded, linearly dominated, nonperiodic, and rational-valued.

declarations.name: exists_totientParity_arbitrarilyManySeparatedCarry_rational_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_totientParity_arbitrarilyManySeparatedCarry_rational_countermodel : ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ N G K, ∃ k, N < 2 ^ (k + 3) ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, i < K → 2 ^ (k + i + 3) + G < 2 ^ (k + i + 4) ∧ c (2 ^ (k + i + 3)) = 6 ∧ c (2 ^ (k + i + 3) + 1) = 0) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ 6) ∧ (∀ n, c n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, c n % 2 = Nat.totient n % 2) ∧ (¬ ∃ p N : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → c (n + p) = c n) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (c n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: Arbitrarily many cofinally located and uniformly separated carry markers still do not rescue the parity-and-aperiodicity route. For every requested block length, the same bounded natural-valued witness supplies that entire block while its binary series remains the rational number `3/2`.

declarations.name: positiveForeignResidueKernel_eq_shiftedMobiusPulseTerm
declarations.signature: theorem positiveForeignResidueKernel_eq_shiftedMobiusPulseTerm (d : ℕ+) (N : ℕ) : positiveForeignResidueKernel d N = shiftedMobiusPulseTerm N d
declarations.docstring: The residue kernel postulated by the finite projection lane is exactly the shifted Möbius pulse obtained from the convergent Lambert regrouping.

declarations.name: totientTail_eq_tsum_positiveForeignResidueKernel
declarations.signature: theorem totientTail_eq_tsum_positiveForeignResidueKernel (N : ℕ) : totientTail N = ∑' d : ℕ+, positiveForeignResidueKernel d N
declarations.docstring: **Global analytic kernel identity for the actual residue coordinates.** The literal tail `R_N` is the sum of the positive residue channels used by the finite foreign-projection decomposition.

declarations.name: summable_positiveForeignResidueKernel
declarations.signature: theorem summable_positiveForeignResidueKernel (N : ℕ) : Summable (fun d : ℕ+ => positiveForeignResidueKernel d N)
declarations.docstring: Absolute convergence of the actual residue kernel. Only finitely many channels lie at or below `N`; above `N` the exact stable-range formula is dominated by a pair of geometric series.

declarations.name: positiveResidueIncrement_eq_shiftedMobiusPulse_sub
declarations.signature: theorem positiveResidueIncrement_eq_shiftedMobiusPulse_sub (d : ℕ+) (H : ℕ) : positiveResidueIncrement d H = shiftedMobiusPulseTerm (2 * H) d - shiftedMobiusPulseTerm H d
declarations.docstring: Each diagonal residue increment is literally the difference of the two shifted Möbius pulses at `H` and `2H`.

declarations.name: summable_positiveResidueIncrement
declarations.signature: theorem summable_positiveResidueIncrement (H : ℕ) : Summable (fun d : ℕ+ => positiveResidueIncrement d H)
declarations.docstring: The diagonal increment family is absolutely summable, so subtraction of the two literal tails may be interchanged with the residue-channel sum.

declarations.name: scaleDiagonalTailDifference_eq_tsum_positiveResidueIncrement
declarations.signature: theorem scaleDiagonalTailDifference_eq_tsum_positiveResidueIncrement (H : ℕ) : scaleDiagonalTailDifference H = ∑' d : ℕ+, positiveResidueIncrement d H
declarations.docstring: The actual diagonal is the unconditional sum of all residue increments. This is the global bridge required before splitting divisor and foreign channels at a finite cutoff.

declarations.name: scaleDiagonalTailDifference_eq_finiteResidue_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem scaleDiagonalTailDifference_eq_finiteResidue_add_tail (H D : ℕ) : scaleDiagonalTailDifference H = finiteResidueDiagonal H D + ∑' k : ℕ, residueIncrement (D + 1 + k) H
declarations.docstring: Splitting the absolutely summable residue family at `D` identifies the literal diagonal with the finite residue state plus the exact shifted tail.

declarations.name: summable_moebius_div_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem summable_moebius_div_mersenne : Summable (fun d : ℕ+ => ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius (d : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (d : ℕ) - 1))
declarations.docstring: Absolute convergence of the first-order Möbius--Mersenne series, exposed here because the renormalized residue coordinate spends its exact tail.

declarations.name: firstLambertTailCorrectionRat_cast_eq_tsum
declarations.signature: theorem firstLambertTailCorrectionRat_cast_eq_tsum (D : ℕ) : (firstLambertTailCorrectionRat D : ℝ) = ∑' k : ℕ, ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius (D + 1 + k) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (D + 1 + k) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The rational first-order correction is exactly the shifted infinite tail of the absolutely convergent Möbius--Mersenne series.

declarations.name: residueIncrement_tail_eq_lambert_tails
declarations.signature: theorem residueIncrement_tail_eq_lambert_tails {H D : ℕ} (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) : (∑' k : ℕ, residueIncrement (D + 1 + k) H) = (diagonalCoefficient H : ℝ) * ((firstLambertTailCorrectionRat D : ℝ) + mobiusSquareTail D)
declarations.docstring: Above the full diagonal scale, every omitted residue channel is stable. Its exact tail is the diagonal coefficient times the first-order correction plus the canonical squared-Mersenne tail.

declarations.name: renormalizedResidueAgreement_of_twice_le
declarations.signature: theorem renormalizedResidueAgreement_of_twice_le {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) : RenormalizedResidueAgreement H D
declarations.docstring: **The renormalized residue socket is discharged.** Once the cutoff is past `2H`, the finite residue presentation and the canonical rational squared-Mersenne centre are the same coordinate.

declarations.name: scaleFullTarget_miss_of_renormalized_residue_separation_of_twice_le
declarations.signature: theorem scaleFullTarget_miss_of_renormalized_residue_separation_of_twice_le {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) (hsep : ∀ z : ℤ, lambertSquareComplementBound H D < |renormalizedResidueProjection H D - (z : ℝ)|) : ¬ScaleFullTargetHit H
declarations.docstring: Endpoint-facing form: after the exact coordinate agreement above, the only remaining hypothesis is finite rational separation from every integer.

declarations.name: foreignResidueTailLimit_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem foreignResidueTailLimit_of_le {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hHD : H ≤ D) : ForeignResidueTailLimit H D
declarations.docstring: **The foreign tail-limit socket is discharged.** Once `D` contains `H`, every divisor channel lies in the finite prefix. The remaining actual foreign defect is therefore exactly the absolutely summable residue tail above `D`, whose interval partial sums converge to its `tsum`.

declarations.name: controlledForeignProjection_of_twice_le
declarations.signature: theorem controlledForeignProjection_of_twice_le {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) : ControlledForeignProjection H D
declarations.docstring: The shifted Möbius identity removes the former tail-limit hypothesis from the finite foreign-residue projection. Once the cutoff contains the full diagonal scale, the projected defect is controlled by its explicit geometric complement budget.

declarations.name: scaleFullTarget_miss_of_projected_separation_of_twice_le
declarations.signature: theorem scaleFullTarget_miss_of_projected_separation_of_twice_le {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) (hseparation : ProjectedFullTargetSeparation H D) : ¬ScaleFullTargetHit H
declarations.docstring: Exact separation of the finite residue state now rules out a full-target hit without an analytic socket: the required tail limit is supplied by the shifted Möbius expansion above.

declarations.name: scaleFullTarget_miss_of_projected_separation_of_twice_le_of_forall_int
declarations.signature: theorem scaleFullTarget_miss_of_projected_separation_of_twice_le_of_forall_int {H D : ℕ} (hH : 0 < H) (hcutoff : 2 * H ≤ D) (hseparation : ∀ z : ℤ, foreignComplementBound H D < |scaleExplicitShadow H + projectedForeignDefect H D - (z : ℝ)|) : ¬ScaleFullTargetHit H
declarations.docstring: Expanded exact-rational certificate form of the unconditional projected enclosure.

declarations.name: forwardMultipleShift
declarations.docstring: The least strictly positive shift from `N` to a multiple of `d` when `d > 0`. At a divisor of `N` it is `d`, rather than zero.

declarations.name: forwardMultipleQuotient
declarations.docstring: The quotient of the first multiple of `d` strictly above `N`.

declarations.name: forwardMultipleShift_pos
declarations.signature: theorem forwardMultipleShift_pos (N : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : 0 < forwardMultipleShift N d

declarations.name: forwardMultipleShift_le
declarations.signature: theorem forwardMultipleShift_le (N d : ℕ) : forwardMultipleShift N d ≤ d

declarations.name: add_forwardMultipleShift_eq
declarations.signature: theorem add_forwardMultipleShift_eq (N : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : N + forwardMultipleShift N d = d * forwardMultipleQuotient N d

declarations.name: forwardMultipleShift_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem forwardMultipleShift_dvd (N : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : d ∣ N + forwardMultipleShift N d

declarations.name: forwardMultipleQuotient_eq
declarations.signature: theorem forwardMultipleQuotient_eq (N : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : forwardMultipleQuotient N d = (N + forwardMultipleShift N d) / d

declarations.name: forwardMultipleShift_eq_self_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem forwardMultipleShift_eq_self_of_dvd (N : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hdN : d ∣ N) : forwardMultipleShift N d = d

declarations.name: summable_const_add_mul_geometric
declarations.signature: private lemma summable_const_add_mul_geometric (q x : ℝ) (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => (q + (k : ℝ)) * x ^ k)

declarations.name: tsum_const_add_mul_geometric
declarations.signature: private theorem tsum_const_add_mul_geometric (q x : ℝ) (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) : ∑' k : ℕ, (q + (k : ℝ)) * x ^ k = q / (1 - x) + x / (1 - x) ^ 2

declarations.name: tsum_lambert_pair_regroup_if
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_lambert_pair_regroup_if (w v : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → |w d| ≤ (d : ℝ)) (hv : ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m → |v m| ≤ (m : ℝ)) (P : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred P] {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) : (∑' p : ℕ+ × ℕ+, if P ((p.1 : ℕ) * (p.2 : ℕ)) then w (p.1 : ℕ) * v (p.2 : ℕ) * x ^ ((p.1 : ℕ) * (p.2 : ℕ)) else 0) = ∑' n : ℕ+, if P (n : ℕ) then (∑ e ∈ (n : ℕ).divisors,
declarations.docstring: Product-to-divisor regrouping after restricting to an arbitrary predicate of the product index. Absolute summability makes the restriction and the antidiagonal regroup unconditional.

declarations.name: shiftedMobiusPulseTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftedMobiusPulseTerm (N d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The closed contribution of one divisor `d` to the shifted tail at `N`.

declarations.name: div_two_pow_eq
declarations.signature: private lemma div_two_pow_eq (a : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : a / (2 : ℝ) ^ n = a * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n

declarations.name: tsum_shiftedDivisorFiber
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_shiftedDivisorFiber (N : ℕ) (d : ℕ+) : (∑' k : ℕ, ((moebius (d : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * (((forwardMultipleQuotient N d : ℕ) : ℝ) + (k : ℝ)) / (2 : ℝ) ^ (forwardMultipleShift N d + (d : ℕ) * k)) = shiftedMobiusPulseTerm N d
declarations.docstring: Exact evaluation of a shifted divisor fibre. This is the residue-class geometric identity underlying the shifted Möbius formula for `totientTail`.

declarations.name: abs_moebius_real_le
declarations.signature: private theorem abs_moebius_real_le (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : |((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ (d : ℝ)

declarations.name: abs_natCast_le
declarations.signature: private theorem abs_natCast_le (m : ℕ) (_hm : 0 < m) : |(m : ℝ)| ≤ (m : ℝ)

declarations.name: sum_divisors_moebius_mul_div_real
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_divisors_moebius_mul_div_real (n : ℕ+) : (∑ e ∈ (n : ℕ).divisors, ((moebius e : ℤ) : ℝ) * ((((n : ℕ) / e : ℕ) : ℝ))) = (Nat.totient (n : ℕ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: tailMobiusPair
declarations.signature: private noncomputable def tailMobiusPair (N : ℕ) (p : ℕ+ × ℕ+) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The absolutely summable product family whose product indices lie strictly past `N`.

declarations.name: summable_tailMobiusPair
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_tailMobiusPair (N : ℕ) : Summable (tailMobiusPair N)

declarations.name: tsum_tailMobiusPair_eq_pnatTotientTail
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_tailMobiusPair_eq_pnatTotientTail (N : ℕ) : (∑' p : ℕ+ × ℕ+, tailMobiusPair N p) = ∑' n : ℕ+, if N < (n : ℕ) then (Nat.totient (n : ℕ) : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (n : ℕ) else 0
declarations.docstring: Möbius inversion turns the restricted product family into the positive totient tail in absolute binary coordinates.

declarations.name: pnatTotientTail
declarations.docstring: The positive-index form of the absolute totient tail.

declarations.name: summable_totient_half_pow
declarations.signature: private theorem summable_totient_half_pow : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.totient n : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n)

declarations.name: pnatTotientTail_eq_tsum_nat
declarations.signature: private theorem pnatTotientTail_eq_tsum_nat (N : ℕ) : pnatTotientTail N = ∑' j : ℕ, (Nat.totient (N + 1 + j) : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ (N + 1 + j)

declarations.name: totientTail_eq_two_pow_mul_pnatTotientTail
declarations.signature: theorem totientTail_eq_two_pow_mul_pnatTotientTail (N : ℕ) : totientTail N = (2 : ℝ) ^ N * pnatTotientTail N
declarations.docstring: Scaling the absolute positive-index tail by `2^N` recovers the local tail `R_N`, whose exponent starts again at one.

declarations.name: tailMobiusPair_fiber_reindex
declarations.signature: private theorem tailMobiusPair_fiber_reindex (N : ℕ) (d : ℕ+) : (∑' m : ℕ+, tailMobiusPair N (d, m)) = ∑' k : ℕ, ((moebius (d : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * (((forwardMultipleQuotient N d : ℕ) : ℝ) + (k : ℝ)) * ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ ((d : ℕ) * (forwardMultipleQuotient N d + k))

declarations.name: two_pow_mul_tailMobiusPair_fiber_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem two_pow_mul_tailMobiusPair_fiber_eq (N : ℕ) (d : ℕ+) : (2 : ℝ) ^ N * (∑' m : ℕ+, tailMobiusPair N (d, m)) = shiftedMobiusPulseTerm N d

declarations.name: totientTail_eq_tsum_shiftedMobiusPulse
declarations.signature: theorem totientTail_eq_tsum_shiftedMobiusPulse (N : ℕ) : totientTail N = ∑' d : ℕ+, shiftedMobiusPulseTerm N d
declarations.docstring: **Exact shifted Möbius formula for the literal totient tail.** Every divisor fibre is evaluated at its first multiple strictly past `N`; no foreign term is defined by subtracting an approximation from the target.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_totient_eq
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_totient_eq (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail Nat.totient N = totientTail N
declarations.docstring: The generic coefficient tail specializes definitionally to the local totient tail used by the period-killer modules.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffSeries_totient_eq
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffSeries_totient_eq : binaryCoeffSeries Nat.totient = ∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n
declarations.docstring: The shifted-index generic series is the original totient series; the missing zeroth term is `φ(0)=0`.

declarations.name: totient_temperedOrbit_eq_scaledTail
declarations.signature: theorem totient_temperedOrbit_eq_scaledTail {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (N : ℕ) : (u N : ℝ) = (v : ℝ) * totientTail N
declarations.docstring: A tempered totient carry is exactly its positive multiplier times the local totient tail.

declarations.name: totient_carryShift_cast
declarations.signature: theorem totient_carryShift_cast {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (N k : ℕ) : ((u (N + k) - u N : ℤ) : ℝ) = (v : ℝ) * (totientTail (N + k) - totientTail N)
declarations.docstring: Exact displacement form of tail-orbit rigidity.

declarations.name: carryShift_dvd_iff_tailDiff_mem_int
declarations.signature: theorem carryShift_dvd_iff_tailDiff_mem_int {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hv : 0 < v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (N k : ℕ) : (v : ℤ) ∣ u (N + k) - u N ↔ totientTail (N + k) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: For a positive-multiplier tempered totient carry, integrality of a tail difference is exactly divisibility of the corresponding carry displacement. This is the carry-side form of the tail-period law.

declarations.name: carryShift_ediv_cast_eq_tailDiff
declarations.signature: theorem carryShift_ediv_cast_eq_tailDiff {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hv : 0 < v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (N k : ℕ) (hdvd : (v : ℤ) ∣ u (N + k) - u N) : (((u (N + k) - u N) / (v : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℝ) = totientTail (N + k) - totientTail N
declarations.docstring: Exact normalization of a divisible carry displacement. Dividing by the orbit multiplier does not create a compressed carry state: it recovers the integer tail difference itself.

declarations.name: totient_forcing_vanishes_mod_of_dvd_multiplier
declarations.signature: theorem totient_forcing_vanishes_mod_of_dvd_multiplier {p v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hpv : p ∣ v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) (N : ℕ) : u (N + 1) ≡ 2 * u N [ZMOD (p : ℤ)]
declarations.docstring: Reduction modulo any divisor of the orbit multiplier erases the totient forcing term. Thus a finite-field reduction at a prime dividing `v` sees only the homogeneous doubling recurrence, not the totient grid minor.

declarations.name: totient_carry_modEq_geometric_of_dvd_multiplier
declarations.signature: theorem totient_carry_modEq_geometric_of_dvd_multiplier {p v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hpv : p ∣ v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u) : ∀ N : ℕ, u N ≡ (2 : ℤ) ^ N * u 0 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)]
declarations.docstring: The preceding loss is global: modulo a divisor of `v`, the whole carry is the geometric orbit generated by its initial state.

declarations.name: carryShift_mul_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem carryShift_mul_dvd {v h N₀ : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → (v : ℤ) ∣ u (N + h) - u N) (m N : ℕ) (hN : N₀ ≤ N) : (v : ℤ) ∣ u (N + m * h) - u N
declarations.docstring: Divisibility of one eventual carry period propagates to every multiple of that period by telescoping.

declarations.name: CarrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod
declarations.signature: def CarrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod (v h N₀ : ℕ) (u : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Uniform quotient-periodicity of all dyadic carry sections. The period is measured in the section variable; its ambient-index shift is `2^j h`.

declarations.name: carrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod_of_shift_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem carrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod_of_shift_dvd {v h N₀ : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → (v : ℤ) ∣ u (N + h) - u N) : CarrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod v h N₀ u
declarations.docstring: An eventual period of the base carry displacement gives the same eventual period modulo `v` on every dyadic section, with one common threshold for all levels and residues.

declarations.name: not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_eventual_mod_period
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_eventual_mod_period (hirr : ¬ Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries Nat.totient)) : ∃ v : ℕ, 0 < v ∧ ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u ∧ ∃ h : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, CarrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod v h N₀ u
declarations.docstring: Rationality supplies one positive-multiplier tempered carry whose dyadic sections are uniformly eventually periodic modulo the multiplier.

declarations.name: not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_mod_period_and_unbounded_rank
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_mod_period_and_unbounded_rank (hirr : ¬ Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries Nat.totient)) : ∃ v : ℕ, 0 < v ∧ ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit Nat.totient v u ∧ (∀ e : ℕ, 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ Module.finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))) ∧ ∃ h : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, CarrySectionsEventuallyPeriodicMod v h N₀ u
declarations.docstring: **Exact rationality frontier.** The same rationality-supplied carry has uniform eventual periodicity modulo `v` and unbounded torsion-free dyadic section rank. Hence quotient periodicity is the valid compression theorem; it cannot be promoted to finite `ℚ`-rank without extra totient arithmetic.

declarations.name: totientAdjugateTailCost
declarations.signature: noncomputable def totientAdjugateTailCost {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w : ι → ℚ) (x : ι → ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The crude two-tail cost attached to an inverse/adjugate row. Recovering `φ(x)` as `2 R_(x-1) - R_x` and applying `R_M ≤ M+2` termwise gives the factor `2(x+1) + (x+2)`.

declarations.name: three_le_totientAdjugateTailCost
declarations.signature: theorem three_le_totientAdjugateTailCost {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w : ι → ℚ) (x : ι → ℕ) (hisolate : ∑ i, w i * (Nat.totient (x i) : ℚ) = 1) : (3 : ℚ) ≤ totientAdjugateTailCost w x
declarations.docstring: **Universal absolute-adjugate no-go.** Any rational row that exactly isolates one totient channel already has crude two-tail cost at least `3`. Indeed `φ(x) ≤ x` forces `1 ≤ Σ |w_i| x_i`, while reconstructing each coefficient from two tails costs `3 x_i + 4`. This is independent of the matrix height, row translation, determinant, and choice of target channel.

declarations.name: not_totientAdjugateTailCost_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem not_totientAdjugateTailCost_lt_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w : ι → ℚ) (x : ι → ℕ) (hisolate : ∑ i, w i * (Nat.totient (x i) : ℚ) = 1) : ¬ totientAdjugateTailCost w x < 1
declarations.docstring: Therefore the absolute-adjugate strategy can never reach its required strict `< 1` tail-error threshold, at any finite grid height.

declarations.name: idCoeff_binaryCoeffTail_eq
declarations.signature: theorem idCoeff_binaryCoeffTail_eq (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail id N = (N : ℝ) + 2
declarations.docstring: The completely multiplicative control sequence `c(n)=n` has the exact tail `T_c(N)=N+2`. In particular its marked binary value is rational, while every positive shift has an integral tail difference.

declarations.name: idCoeff_binaryCoeffTail_sub
declarations.signature: theorem idCoeff_binaryCoeffTail_sub (N K : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail id (N + K) - binaryCoeffTail id N = (K : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact shift law for the multiplicative rational control.

declarations.name: idCoeff_mersenneModulus_does_not_annihilate_tailShift
declarations.signature: theorem idCoeff_mersenneModulus_does_not_annihilate_tailShift {K q : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K) (hKq : K < q) (hqM : q ∣ 2 ^ K - 1) : binaryCoeffSeries id = 2 ∧ q ∣ 2 ^ K - 1 ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℝ) = binaryCoeffTail id (N + K) - binaryCoeffTail id N ∧ ¬ (q : ℤ) ∣ z
declarations.docstring: **Primitive-Mersenne congruence no-go.** Suppose `q` is any modulus strictly above `K` which divides `2^K-1`; this includes the size conclusion supplied by a primitive prime divisor. The rational, completely multiplicative control `c(n)=n` has an integral `K`-shift at every `N`, but that integer is `K` and hence is nonzero modulo `q`. Thus a primitive factor of the homogeneous multiplier `2^K-1` supplies no contradiction from tail integrality alone. A successful use of such a factor must add a genuinely totient-specific residue/size restriction.

declarations.name: four_dvd_totient_of_prime_modEq_one_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem four_dvd_totient_of_prime_modEq_one_dvd {r n : ℕ} (hr : r.Prime) (hr4 : r ≡ 1 [MOD 4]) (hrn : r ∣ n) : 4 ∣ Nat.totient n
declarations.docstring: A prime divisor congruent to one modulo four forces four to divide the totient.

declarations.name: exists_prime_deltaTotient_four_mul_mod_four_two
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_deltaTotient_four_mul_mod_four_two (h B : ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) : ∃ p : ℕ, B < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ deltaTotient (4 * h) p ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]
declarations.docstring: Every positive shift divisible by four has cofinally many prime inputs where its totient increment is exactly `2 mod 4`. Choose a fresh prime `r = 1 mod 4` above the shift and use Dirichlet on the coprime progression `p = (3r - H) mod 4r`, where `H = 4h`. Then `p = 3 mod 4`, so `φ(p) = 2 mod 4`, while `r ∣ p+H` forces `4 ∣ φ(p+H)`. Unlike a homogeneous Mersenne factor, this is a genuinely totient-specific residue and is supplied beyond every threshold.

declarations.name: deltaTotient_even_of_three_le
declarations.signature: theorem deltaTotient_even_of_three_le (H n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : Even (deltaTotient H n)
declarations.docstring: Once both arguments exceed two, a totient increment is even.

declarations.name: integral_four_mul_tailDiff_mod_four_two_of_delta_pulse
declarations.signature: theorem integral_four_mul_tailDiff_mod_four_two_of_delta_pulse {h N₀ p : ℕ} (hpLarge : N₀ + 3 < p) (hpulse : deltaTotient (4 * h) p ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]) (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → totientTail (N + 4 * h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℝ) = totientTail (p + 4 * h) - totientTail p ∧ z ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]
declarations.docstring: A fixed arithmetic pulse transfers to the integral tail orbit. This is the pointwise form used below: eventual integrality is only needed two steps before `p`, while the conclusion is the `2 mod 4` state at `p`.

declarations.name: eventual_integral_four_mul_tailDiff_has_cofinal_mod_four_pulse
declarations.signature: theorem eventual_integral_four_mul_tailDiff_has_cofinal_mod_four_pulse {h N₀ : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → totientTail (N + 4 * h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, B < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℝ) = totientTail (p + 4 * h) - totientTail p ∧ z ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]
declarations.docstring: **Cofinal mod-four tail-orbit pulse.** If the `4h` tail difference is eventually integral, the preceding arithmetic producer forces cofinally many prime positions where its integer representative is `2 mod 4`. The first recurrence step makes the predecessor representative even because both totients are even. At the prime pulse, twice that predecessor vanishes modulo four and the `2 mod 4` increment leaves another `2 mod 4` state. This is a new rationality-side constraint on the actual totient orbit; the completely multiplicative control `c(n)=n` has shift `4h = 0 mod 4` and cannot realize it.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_sub
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit_sub (h N : ℕ) (d e : ℤ) : ∀ L : ℕ, carryOrbit h N d L - carryOrbit h N e L = (2 : ℤ) ^ L * (d - e)
declarations.docstring: Two carry orbits driven by the same totient increments differ only by the homogeneous multiplier `2^L`. In particular, changing the integral tail state at the left endpoint cannot change the right endpoint modulo `2^L`.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_zero_eq_neg_windowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit_zero_eq_neg_windowDiscrepancy (h N L : ℕ) : carryOrbit h N 0 L = -windowDiscrepancy h N L
declarations.docstring: The orbit launched from zero is exactly the negative signed prefix word. Thus `windowDiscrepancy` is not an additional state coordinate: it is the forcing response of the same affine carry recurrence.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_eq_twoPow_mul_sub_windowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit_eq_twoPow_mul_sub_windowDiscrepancy (h N : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (L : ℕ) : carryOrbit h N d L = (2 : ℤ) ^ L * d - windowDiscrepancy h N L
declarations.docstring: **Closed form for every integral carry trajectory.** After `L` steps, the initial state contributes only `2^L d`; all lower binary digits are the negative discrepancy word.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_modEq_neg_windowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit_modEq_neg_windowDiscrepancy (h N : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (L : ℕ) : carryOrbit h N d L ≡ -windowDiscrepancy h N L [ZMOD (2 : ℤ) ^ L]
declarations.docstring: Fixed-depth reset in its pure integer-orbit form.

declarations.name: integral_tailDiff_endpoint_modEq_neg_windowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: theorem integral_tailDiff_endpoint_modEq_neg_windowDiscrepancy {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N) (L : ℕ) : ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℝ) = totientTail (N + L + h) - totientTail (N + L) ∧ z ≡ -windowDiscrepancy h N L [ZMOD (2 : ℤ) ^ L]
declarations.docstring: **Exact fixed-depth reset for an integral totient tail difference.** Once the left endpoint is integral, the right endpoint is integral and its residue modulo `2^L` is forced by the last `L` totient increments alone: `D_h(N+L) = -windowDiscrepancy(h,N,L) (mod 2^L)`. Consequently, splitting the orbit into eventual-period blocks, choosing two Dirichlet progressions separated by a period, or telescoping the recurrence cannot produce a second incompatible endpoint residue. Any contradiction using the cofinal mod-four pulse must add an independent archimedean strip or size restriction.

declarations.name: integral_tailDiff_has_endpointSurvivor
declarations.signature: theorem integral_tailDiff_has_endpointSurvivor {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N) (L : ℕ) : endpointSurvivor h N L (-carryOrbit h N d L)
declarations.docstring: **The independent archimedean coupling.** Negating the true integral endpoint gives an `endpointSurvivor`: it has the discrepancy residue forced by the reset theorem, and the analytic tail bound keeps it inside the signed strip. This is the exact place where congruence information and size information meet.

declarations.name: BoundedTailCarry
declarations.signature: def BoundedTailCarry (h N : ℕ) (d : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: An integer launch survives every carry depth inside the sharp integer strip forced by the analytic tail bound. The radius is one below the real bound because the orbit is integer-valued.

declarations.name: boundedTailCarry_of_integral_tailDiff
declarations.signature: theorem boundedTailCarry_of_integral_tailDiff {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N) : BoundedTailCarry h N d
declarations.docstring: An integral tail difference launches a carry that survives forever. This is the infinite-orbit half of the edge-lock classification.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mem_int_of_boundedTailCarry
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_mem_int_of_boundedTailCarry {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hbounded : BoundedTailCarry h N d) : totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Conversely, a linearly bounded integer carry cannot evade every finite central-arc certificate unless the original tail difference is integral. Certificate completeness supplies a killing depth for every non-integral tail; the bounded carry supplies an endpoint survivor at that same depth.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mem_int_iff_exists_boundedTailCarry
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_mem_int_iff_exists_boundedTailCarry (h N : ℕ) : (totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) ↔ ∃ d : ℤ, BoundedTailCarry h N d
declarations.docstring: **Exact edge-lock classification.** A shifted totient-tail difference is an integer iff some integer launch of the affine carry recurrence remains inside the linear strip at every depth. Thus the apparent infinite lock and the analytic integrality obstruction are the same mathematical object.

declarations.name: no_certifiedKill_iff_exists_boundedTailCarry
declarations.signature: theorem no_certifiedKill_iff_exists_boundedTailCarry (h N : ℕ) : (∀ L : ℕ, ¬ certifiedKill h N L) ↔ ∃ d : ℤ, BoundedTailCarry h N d
declarations.docstring: No finite endpoint certificate exists exactly when an infinite bounded carry survives. This is the certificate-level form of the classification: finite extinction and infinite lock are complementary, with no gap.

declarations.name: tail_diff_directed_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_directed_bounds (h N : ℕ) : -((N : ℝ) + 2) < totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∧ totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N < (N : ℝ) + h + 2
declarations.docstring: Positivity of both tails gives the directed bounds that are lost when `abs_tail_diff_lt` symmetrizes the interval.

declarations.name: directedCertifiedKill
declarations.signature: def directedCertifiedKill (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The asymmetric central-arc certificate. Its low radius is only `N+L+2`, while its high wrap radius remains `N+h+L+2`. It is therefore strictly weaker—and potentially strictly more useful—than `certifiedKill` when `h>0`.

declarations.name: tail_diff_notMem_int_of_directedCertifiedKill
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_notMem_int_of_directedCertifiedKill {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : directedCertifiedKill h N L) : totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Soundness of the directed certificate. The proof keeps the positive and negative endpoint radii separate instead of replacing both by their maximum.

declarations.name: directedCertifiedKill_of_certifiedKill
declarations.signature: theorem directedCertifiedKill_of_certifiedKill {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : directedCertifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Every symmetric certificate is a directed certificate; the converse can fail on the newly exposed one-sided band.

declarations.name: exists_directedCertifiedKill_iff_tail_diff_notMem_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_directedCertifiedKill_iff_tail_diff_notMem_int (h N : ℕ) : (∃ L : ℕ, directedCertifiedKill h N L) ↔ totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The directed certificate is complete as well as sound: its wider finite arc changes the first firing depth, not the underlying pointwise proposition.

declarations.name: directedCertifiedKill_periodLcm_three_depth_six
declarations.docstring: Concrete strictness witness on the canonical LCM diagonal: the directed strip kills height `t=3` at depth six, one full binary level before the symmetric certificate can fire.

declarations.name: irrational_totientSeries_of_multiple_directedCertificateSupply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totientSeries_of_multiple_directedCertificateSupply (hsupply : ∀ h₀ : ℕ, 0 < h₀ → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ m, 0 < m ∧ ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ∃ L, directedCertifiedKill (m * h₀) N L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: Multiple-period reduction using the sharper directed strip.

declarations.name: CofinalDirectedLcmCertificateSupply
declarations.docstring: The canonical diagonal version of the directed certificate supply.

declarations.name: irrational_totientSeries_iff_cofinalDirectedLcmCertificateSupply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totientSeries_iff_cofinalDirectedLcmCertificateSupply : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ↔ CofinalDirectedLcmCertificateSupply
declarations.docstring: **Exact ceiling of the directed LCM route.** Cofinal directed certificates are equivalent to Erdős #249 itself. The asymmetric strip is a real finite-depth improvement, but the current LCM diagonal does not turn it into an independent sieve theorem: proving its cofinal supply is already proving the original irrationality statement.

declarations.name: modFourPulseCertifiedKill
declarations.signature: def modFourPulseCertifiedKill (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The two extra input bits supplied by `d = 2 mod 4` lift the usual depth-`L` endpoint test from modulus `2^L` to modulus `2^(L+2)`. The target residue is the half-turn `2^(L+1)` minus the discrepancy word. This reduces the explicit start-state search, but it is only a shifted-coordinate view of the ordinary depth-`(L+2)` certificate once the two-letter pulse prefix is included; no stronger cofinal supply is claimed.

declarations.name: abs_gt_of_emod_mem_central
declarations.signature: theorem abs_gt_of_emod_mem_central {x P B : ℤ} (hP : 0 < P) (hlow : B < x % P) (hhigh : x % P < P - B) : B < |x|
declarations.docstring: Any representative of a residue in the central arc has absolute value larger than the excluded boundary radius.

declarations.name: carryOrbit_emod_twoPow_add_two_of_modFourPulse
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit_emod_twoPow_add_two_of_modFourPulse {h N : ℕ} {d : ℤ} (hdmod : d ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]) (L : ℕ) : carryOrbit h N d L % (2 : ℤ) ^ (L + 2) = ((2 : ℤ) ^ (L + 1) - windowDiscrepancy h N L) % (2 : ℤ) ^ (L + 2)
declarations.docstring: Exact lifted endpoint residue for a `2 mod 4` start state.

declarations.name: modFourPulseSurvivorKill
declarations.signature: def modFourPulseSurvivorKill (h N K : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A finite survivor certificate restricted to the only start states that the cofinal arithmetic pulse permits. Compared with `survivorKill`, this checks only candidates congruent to `2 mod 4`, a fourfold reduction of the initial strip.

declarations.name: modFourPulseSurvivorKill_of_certifiedKill
declarations.signature: theorem modFourPulseSurvivorKill_of_certifiedKill {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : modFourPulseCertifiedKill h N L) : modFourPulseSurvivorKill h N L
declarations.docstring: The lifted one-residue certificate eliminates every pulse-compatible start state by depth `L`; hence it implies the finite restricted survivor certificate without enumerating those states individually.

declarations.name: tail_diff_ne_int_of_modFourPulseSurvivorKill
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_ne_int_of_modFourPulseSurvivorKill {h N K : ℕ} (hkill : modFourPulseSurvivorKill h N K) {d : ℤ} (hdmod : d ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4]) : (d : ℝ) ≠ totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N
declarations.docstring: Soundness of the restricted certificate: it rules out equality with any integral tail state in the pulse class.

declarations.name: irrational_totientSeries_of_cofinal_modFourPulseSurvivorKill
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totientSeries_of_cofinal_modFourPulseSurvivorKill (hsupply : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, B < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ deltaTotient (4 * h) p ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4] ∧ ∃ K : ℕ, modFourPulseSurvivorKill (4 * h) p K) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **Pulse-prime survivor reduction for Erdős #249.** It is enough to kill the `2 mod 4` candidate states at one cofinal arithmetic-pulse prime for each putative primitive period. Every cell of the remaining producer is finite and decidable.

declarations.name: irrational_totientSeries_of_cofinal_modFourPulseCertificateSupply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totientSeries_of_cofinal_modFourPulseCertificateSupply (hsupply : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, B < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ deltaTotient (4 * h) p ≡ (2 : ℤ) [ZMOD 4] ∧ ∃ L : ℕ, modFourPulseCertifiedKill (4 * h) p L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: Single-residue version of the preceding reduction. Its finite cell is one central-arc test modulo `2^(L+2)` at a cofinal pulse prime, so no explicit candidate-state enumeration remains. The supply ceiling is unchanged: the two pulse bits exactly replace the two earlier recurrence steps.

declarations.name: totientTail
declarations.docstring: The local totient tail `R_N = ∑_{j≥0} φ(N+1+j)/2^{j+1} = ∑_{m≥1} φ(N+m)/2^m`: the fractional layer of `2^N · S`.

declarations.name: totientPrefix
declarations.docstring: The integer prefix `Φ_N = ∑_{n=0}^{N} φ(n)·2^{N-n}` of `2^N · S`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: def windowDiscrepancy (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The window discrepancy `A_{h,N,L} = ∑_{j=0}^{L-1} (φ(N+h+1+j) - φ(N+1+j))·2^{L-1-j}`: the depth-`L` truncation of `2^L·(R_{N+h} - R_N)`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill
declarations.signature: def certifiedKill (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The decidable period-killer certificate: the residue of `A_{h,N,L}` modulo `2^L` avoids the radius-`(N+h+L+2)` neighbourhood of `0`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_depth_floor
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_depth_floor {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : (2 * (N + h + L + 2) : ℤ) < 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: Every endpoint certificate has enough dyadic room for both excluded boundary arcs. In particular, certificate depth cannot remain fixed while `N+h` tends to infinity.

declarations.name: div_two_pow_eq
declarations.signature: private lemma div_two_pow_eq (a : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : a / 2 ^ n = a * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n
declarations.docstring: Every endpoint certificate has enough dyadic room for both excluded boundary arcs. In particular, certificate depth cannot remain fixed while `N+h` tends to infinity. -/ theorem certifiedKill_depth_floor {h N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : (2 * (N + h + L + 2) : ℤ) < 2 ^ L := by rcases hcert with ⟨hleft, hright⟩ linarith instance (h N L : ℕ) : Decidable (certifiedKill h N L) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _)) /-! ## Geometric-linear summability spine

declarations.name: summable_linear_half
declarations.signature: private lemma summable_linear_half : Summable (fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j)

declarations.name: summable_const_add_mul_half
declarations.signature: private lemma summable_const_add_mul_half (C : ℝ) : Summable (fun j : ℕ => (C + (j : ℝ)) * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j)

declarations.name: tsum_const_add_mul_half
declarations.signature: private lemma tsum_const_add_mul_half (C : ℝ) : ∑' j : ℕ, (C + (j : ℝ)) * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j = 2 * C + 2
