declarations.name: positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt
declarations.signature: theorem positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (w : ι → ℝ) (e Y : ι → ℕ) (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < w i) (he : ∀ i ∈ s, 1 ≤ e i) (hY : ∀ i ∈ s, 4 ≤ Y i) : (1 : ℝ) / 480 < (∑ i ∈ s, w i * rankOneSubrankQuotient (e i) (Y i)) / (∑ i ∈ s, w i) - mobiusMersenneTheta 2
declarations.docstring: Positive finite direct sums do not evade the obstruction: a positively weighted average of admissible rank-one quotients still overshoots `Θ₂` by more than `1/480`.

declarations.name: primitive_form_abs_gt
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_form_abs_gt {e Y q : ℕ} {p : ℤ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hY : 4 ≤ Y) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hquot : rankOneSubrankQuotient e Y = (p : ℝ) / q) : (q : ℝ) / 480 < |(q : ℝ) * mobiusMersenneTheta 2 - p|
declarations.docstring: Primitive integer linear forms arising from these quotients are bounded away from zero. In fact the lower bound grows linearly with the denominator.

declarations.name: DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap
declarations.docstring: Cofinal prime escape at the sharp threshold consumed by the existing finite-window singleton route. Unlike the legacy `4/5` socket, this assumes only a strict gap below `9/10`, with an adaptive truncation budget.

declarations.name: naturalPivotPointEscape_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap
declarations.docstring: A strict `9/10` gap in the exact infinite phase leaves a positive adaptive truncation budget and supplies the legacy finite `9/10` point escape.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap (hgap : DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The strict prime-orbit producer closes Erdős #249 through the existing singleton-certificate endpoint. The producer itself remains unproved.

declarations.name: prime0
declarations.docstring: Zero-based prime enumeration.

declarations.name: primeGap0
declarations.docstring: Zero-based consecutive prime gap.

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ
declarations.signature: def dyadicPartialSumQ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Finite zero-based dyadic partial sum of a rational sequence.

declarations.name: prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ
declarations.docstring: The finite zero-based normalization with denominator `2^i`, matching the displayed indexing used by the formal conjecture.

declarations.name: prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ_eq_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ_eq_two_mul (n : ℕ) : prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ n = 2 * dyadicPartialSumQ (fun i => (prime0 i : ℚ)) n
declarations.docstring: Exact factor-of-two indexing normalization: the zero-based displayed partial sum is twice the convention with denominator `2^(i+1)`.

declarations.name: dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ
declarations.signature: def dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Finite dyadic partial sum of the forward differences of a sequence.

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem dyadicPartialSumQ_succ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ P (n + 1) = dyadicPartialSumQ P n + P n / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ_succ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P (n + 1) = dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P n + (P (n + 1) - P n) / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: can
declarations.signature: theorem can be used before any analytic convergence argument. -/ theorem dyadicPartialSumQ_eq_start_add_differences (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ P (n + 1) = P 0 + dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P n - P n / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ_eq_start_add_differences
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicPartialSumQ_eq_start_add_differences (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ P (n + 1) = P 0 + dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P n - P n / 2 ^ (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite summation by parts. The endpoint term is retained, so the theorem can be used before any analytic convergence argument.

declarations.name: prime0_mono_step
declarations.signature: theorem prime0_mono_step (n : ℕ) : prime0 n ≤ prime0 (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Consecutive zero-based primes are increasing.

declarations.name: primeGap0_cast
declarations.signature: theorem primeGap0_cast (n : ℕ) : (primeGap0 n : ℚ) = (prime0 (n + 1) : ℚ) - prime0 n
declarations.docstring: Casting the natural prime gap agrees with subtraction in `ℚ`.

declarations.name: primeGapPartialSumQ
declarations.docstring: Finite dyadic partial sum of the actual consecutive prime gaps.

declarations.name: prime0_dyadic_summation_by_parts
declarations.signature: theorem prime0_dyadic_summation_by_parts (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ (fun i => (prime0 i : ℚ)) (n + 1) = 2 + primeGapPartialSumQ n - (prime0 n : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite prime-gap reformulation, including the initial gap and the endpoint correction. Passing to an infinite series requires a separate proof that the endpoint tends to zero.

declarations.name: primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The real term in the normalized zero-based prime series.

declarations.name: primeDisplayedDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The term with denominator `2^n` used by the displayed formal conjecture.

declarations.name: primeGapDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The real term in the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap series.

declarations.name: primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_two_mul (n : ℕ) : primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n = 2 * primeDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Infinite-series version of the exact factor-two normalization.

declarations.name: primeGapDyadicTerm_eq
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapDyadicTerm_eq (n : ℕ) : primeGapDyadicTerm n = 2 * primeDyadicTerm (n + 1) - primeDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Each gap term is the dyadic discrete derivative of the prime term.

declarations.name: summable_primeGapDyadicTerm_of_summable_primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: Summability of the normalized prime series automatically supplies summability of the actual prime-gap series. This closes the analytic interface left implicit by the finite summation-by-parts identity.

declarations.name: tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) = 2 + ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Exact infinite prime-gap reformulation. Whenever the normalized prime series is summable, its sum is `2` plus the sum of the actual consecutive prime gaps.

declarations.name: irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: Erdős #251 is therefore exactly equivalent to irrationality of the consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series, once summability of the displayed prime series is supplied.

declarations.name: tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_four_add_two_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_four_add_two_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : (∑' n : ℕ, primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n) = 4 + 2 * ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: The zero-based displayed series is `4` plus twice the normalized prime-gap series.

declarations.name: irrational_tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: Direct irrationality equivalence for the indexing used in the formal conjecture.

declarations.name: DyadicTailRecurrence
declarations.signature: def DyadicTailRecurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (T : ℕ → ℚ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Abstract dyadic tail recurrence with integer digits. The actual infinite prime-gap tail is a future analytic instance once summability is established.

declarations.name: tailShift
declarations.signature: def tailShift (T : ℕ → ℚ) (h N : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Difference between two tail states separated by `h` steps.

declarations.name: tailShift_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) : tailShift T h (N + 1) = 2 * tailShift T h N - ((g (N + h + 1) : ℚ) - (g (N + 1) : ℚ))
declarations.docstring: The exact propagation identity for a fixed tail shift.

declarations.name: RatIntegral
declarations.docstring: A rational number is integral when it is the cast of an integer.

declarations.name: dyadicTailBlock
declarations.signature: def dyadicTailBlock (g : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => 0 | h + 1 => 2 * dyadicTailBlock g N h + g (N + h + 1) /-- Iterating the tail recurrence for `h` steps gives the exact finite block identity `T_(N+h) = 2^h T_N - B_(h,N)`. -/ theorem tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : T (N + h) = 2 ^ h * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: The integer block accumulated through `h` dyadic tail steps beginning at index `N`. Recursively, this is `g (N+1) * 2^(h-1) + ⋯ + g (N+h)`.

declarations.name: tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : T (N + h) = 2 ^ h * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: Iterating the tail recurrence for `h` steps gives the exact finite block identity `T_(N+h) = 2^h T_N - B_(h,N)`.

declarations.name: tailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : tailShift T h N = ((2 ^ h : ℚ) - 1) * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: The shifted-tail difference is a scaled copy of `T_N`, up to the explicit integer block.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_sub_int_iff
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_sub_int_iff (x : ℚ) (z : ℤ) : RatIntegral (x - z) ↔ RatIntegral x
declarations.docstring: Subtracting an integer does not change whether a rational number is integral.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_totientMultiplier_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_totientMultiplier_of_odd_den (x : ℚ) (hodd : Odd x.den) : RatIntegral (((2 : ℚ) ^ x.den.totient - 1) * x)
declarations.docstring: Euler's congruence turns an odd reduced denominator into an explicit integral multiplier: if `d = x.den` is odd, then `(2^(phi d) - 1) * x` is an integer.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_iff_scaledTail
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_iff_scaledTail {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N) ↔ RatIntegral (((2 ^ h : ℚ) - 1) * T N)
declarations.docstring: Exact algebraic core of the integral-shift criterion: one tail shift is integral exactly when `(2^h - 1) * T_N` is integral. Connecting `T_N` to the actual infinite prime-gap series remains a separate analytic interface.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_totient_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_totient_of_odd_den {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N : ℕ) (hodd : Odd (T N).den) : RatIntegral (tailShift T (T N).den.totient N)
declarations.docstring: If one tail state has odd reduced denominator `d`, its shift by `Nat.totient d` steps is integral. This is the explicit finite-algebraic consequence of rationality supplied by Euler's theorem.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) {h N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: Once a fixed tail shift is integral, the recurrence keeps it integral at the next index. This is the exact finite algebra behind the eventual-shift criterion; no prime-distribution input is used.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_add
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_add {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) {h N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : ∀ k, RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + k)) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: Integrality therefore propagates through every later index.

declarations.name: exists_twoPow_mul_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem exists_twoPow_mul_odd_den (q : ℚ) : ∃ k : ℕ, Odd (((2 : ℚ) ^ k * q).den)
declarations.docstring: Repeated doubling removes the entire power-of-two part of a rational denominator. The remaining reduced denominator is therefore odd.

declarations.name: exists_odd_den_state
declarations.signature: theorem exists_odd_den_state {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ∃ N : ℕ, Odd (T N).den
declarations.docstring: Every rational-valued dyadic tail recurrence has an odd-denominator state. The index is exactly the number of doublings needed to clear the initial power-of-two denominator.

declarations.name: exists_eventually_integral_tailShift
declarations.signature: theorem exists_eventually_integral_tailShift {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ∃ h N : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ ∀ k, RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + k))
declarations.docstring: Rationality forces one fixed positive shift to be integral from some point onwards. This is the exact contrapositive consumer for a prime-specific cofinal non-integrality theorem.

declarations.name: RealDyadicTailRecurrence
declarations.signature: def RealDyadicTailRecurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (T : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Real-valued version of the dyadic tail recurrence.

declarations.name: realTailShift
declarations.signature: def realTailShift (T : ℕ → ℝ) (h N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Difference between two real tail states separated by `h` steps.

declarations.name: RealIntegral
declarations.docstring: A real number is integral when it is the cast of an integer.

declarations.name: rationalDyadicOrbit
declarations.signature: def rationalDyadicOrbit (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : ℕ → ℚ | 0 => q | N + 1 => 2 * rationalDyadicOrbit g q N - g (N + 1) theorem rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : DyadicTailRecurrence g (rationalDyadicOrbit g q)
declarations.docstring: Rational orbit with prescribed initial state and integer digits.

declarations.name: rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : DyadicTailRecurrence g (rationalDyadicOrbit g q)

declarations.name: realTail_eq_ratCast_rationalDyadicOrbit
declarations.signature: theorem realTail_eq_ratCast_rationalDyadicOrbit {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (q : ℚ) (hzero : T 0 = q) : ∀ N, T N = (rationalDyadicOrbit g q N : ℝ) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: A real recurrence with rational initial state is the real cast of the corresponding rational recurrence at every later index.

declarations.name: CofinalNonintegralTailShifts
declarations.docstring: Cofinal failure of integral shifts for every fixed positive length.

declarations.name: above
declarations.signature: theorem above produces one fixed shift integral at every sufficiently late index. -/ theorem irrational_initial_of_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (hescape : CofinalNonintegralTailShifts T) : Irrational (T 0)

declarations.name: irrational_initial_of_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_initial_of_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (hescape : CofinalNonintegralTailShifts T) : Irrational (T 0)
declarations.docstring: Exact proof consumer: to prove the initial value irrational, it is enough to rule out eventual integrality cofinally for every fixed positive shift. Rationality would produce a rational orbit, and the denominator-collapse theorem above produces one fixed shift integral at every sufficiently late index.

declarations.name: carryCoeff
declarations.signature: def carryCoeff (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The coefficient emitted by an unrestricted integer carry.

declarations.name: carryPartialSum
declarations.signature: def carryPartialSum (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The finite dyadic series emitted by `carryCoeff`.

declarations.name: carryPartialSum_eq
declarations.signature: theorem carryPartialSum_eq (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : carryPartialSum K n = K 0 - K n / 2 ^ n
declarations.docstring: Exact telescoping: arbitrary carries can produce a rational dyadic series without making the coefficient stream periodic.

declarations.name: natCarryCoeff
declarations.signature: def natCarryCoeff (K : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Natural-valued carries emit nonnegative coefficients when the next carry is at most twice the current one.

declarations.name: natCarryCoeff_cast
declarations.signature: theorem natCarryCoeff_cast (K : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hK : K (n + 1) ≤ 2 * K n) : (natCarryCoeff K n : ℚ) = carryCoeff (fun j => (K j : ℚ)) n

declarations.name: UniversalMersenneSubseriesIrrationality
declarations.docstring: The universal irrationality assertion in Erdős #257.

declarations.name: exists_rational_half_counterexample_of_terminalScaledVanishing
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rational_half_counterexample_of_terminalScaledVanishing (S : HalfTerminalOnlyScaledVanishingSequence) : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (1 : ℝ) / 2
declarations.docstring: Any terminal scaled-vanishing sequence supplies an infinite rational counterexample of exact value `1/2`.

declarations.name: not_universal_of_terminalScaledVanishing
declarations.docstring: The same producer negates the original universal irrationality claim.

declarations.name: selectedMersenneTail
declarations.signature: noncomputable def selectedMersenneTail (J : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Mersenne tails restricted to an arbitrary set of future offsets.

declarations.name: summable_selectedMersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_selectedMersenneTail (J : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Summable (J.indicator (fun k => mersenneWeight (n + k + 1)))

declarations.name: selectedMersenneTail_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem selectedMersenneTail_lt_weight (J : Set ℕ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : selectedMersenneTail J n < mersenneWeight n
declarations.docstring: Strict superincreasingness is hereditary under deleting any collection of future Mersenne weights.

declarations.name: SupportedMersenneDigits
declarations.docstring: Binary digit strings supported on `J`.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneDigitValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def supportedMersenneDigitValue (J : Set ℕ) (b : SupportedMersenneDigits J) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The ordinary Mersenne digit map restricted to a chosen support.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneDigitValue_injective
declarations.signature: theorem supportedMersenneDigitValue_injective (J : Set ℕ) : Function.Injective (supportedMersenneDigitValue J)
declarations.docstring: Every Mersenne subseries retains unique binary coding.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneDigitSet
declarations.signature: def supportedMersenneDigitSet (J : Set ℕ) : Set (ℕ → Fin 2)
declarations.docstring: Supported binary strings as a closed subset of the full product space.

declarations.name: isClosed_supportedMersenneDigitSet
declarations.signature: theorem isClosed_supportedMersenneDigitSet (J : Set ℕ) : IsClosed (supportedMersenneDigitSet J)

declarations.name: supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: def supportedMersenneAchievementSet (J : Set ℕ) : Set ℝ
declarations.docstring: The achievement set obtained by allowing digits only on `J`.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneAchievementSet_eq_image
declarations.signature: theorem supportedMersenneAchievementSet_eq_image (J : Set ℕ) : supportedMersenneAchievementSet J = positiveMersenneDigitValue '' supportedMersenneDigitSet J

declarations.name: isCompact_supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: theorem isCompact_supportedMersenneAchievementSet (J : Set ℕ) : IsCompact (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)
declarations.docstring: Every support-restricted Mersenne achievement set is compact.

declarations.name: isClosed_supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: theorem isClosed_supportedMersenneAchievementSet (J : Set ℕ) : IsClosed (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)

declarations.name: supportedMersenneAchievementSet_subset
declarations.signature: theorem supportedMersenneAchievementSet_subset (J : Set ℕ) : supportedMersenneAchievementSet J ⊆ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Deleting coordinates really produces a subset of the full Mersenne achievement set; unique coding prevents any hidden re-entry through another digit string.

declarations.name: isNowhereDense_supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Nowhere density is hereditary for every selected support, finite or infinite. In particular no support-restricted Mersenne achievement set can contain an interval.

declarations.name: preperfect_supportedMersenneDigitSet
declarations.signature: theorem preperfect_supportedMersenneDigitSet {J : Set ℕ} (hJ : J.Infinite) : Preperfect (supportedMersenneDigitSet J)
declarations.docstring: If the selected support is infinite, its closed digit subspace has no isolated point: every basic product neighbourhood leaves some selected coordinate free to flip.

declarations.name: preperfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: theorem preperfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet {J : Set ℕ} (hJ : J.Infinite) : Preperfect (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)

declarations.name: perfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet
declarations.signature: theorem perfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet {J : Set ℕ} (hJ : J.Infinite) : Perfect (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)
declarations.docstring: Every infinite selected support produces a compact perfect nowhere-dense set with unique coding.

declarations.name: summable_mersenneDigitTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_mersenneDigitTerm (b : ℕ → Fin 2) : Summable (fun k => mersenneDigitTerm k b)
declarations.docstring: Every infinite selected support produces a compact perfect nowhere-dense set with unique coding. -/ theorem perfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet {J : Set ℕ} (hJ : J.Infinite) : Perfect (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J) := ⟨isClosed_supportedMersenneAchievementSet J, preperfect_supportedMersenneAchievementSet hJ⟩ /-! ## One-coordinate splitting

declarations.name: positiveMersenneDigitValue_update
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneDigitValue_update (b : ℕ → Fin 2) (k : ℕ) (a : Fin 2) : positiveMersenneDigitValue (Function.update b k a) = ((((a : ℕ) : ℝ) - ((b k : ℕ) : ℝ)) * mersenneWeight (k + 1)) + positiveMersenneDigitValue b
declarations.docstring: Updating one binary coordinate changes the coded value by exactly the corresponding signed Mersenne weight.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneAchievementSet_insert
declarations.signature: theorem supportedMersenneAchievementSet_insert {J : Set ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k ∉ J) : supportedMersenneAchievementSet (insert k J) = supportedMersenneAchievementSet J ∪ (fun x : ℝ => mersenneWeight (k + 1) + x) '' supportedMersenneAchievementSet J
declarations.docstring: Adding one previously forbidden coordinate splits the achievement set into its zero face and a translate of that face.

declarations.name: disjoint_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_translate
declarations.signature: theorem disjoint_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_translate {J : Set ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k ∉ J) : Disjoint (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J) ((fun x : ℝ => mersenneWeight (k + 1) + x) '' supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)
declarations.docstring: The two faces in the one-coordinate split are disjoint. This is exactly where unique coding is spent.

declarations.name: volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_insert
declarations.signature: theorem volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_insert {J : Set ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k ∉ J) : volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet (insert k J)) = 2 * volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J)
declarations.docstring: Allowing one new coordinate doubles Lebesgue measure: the two faces are disjoint translates of the same compact measurable set.

declarations.name: volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_finset_compl_scaled
declarations.signature: theorem volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_finset_compl_scaled (F : Finset ℕ) : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ F.card * volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet ((↑F : Set ℕ)ᶜ)) = 1
declarations.docstring: Finite-coordinate face volume in a division-free form. Deleting the coordinates in `F` and then multiplying by `2^|F|` recovers the full measure-one Mersenne achievement set.

declarations.name: volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_finset_compl
declarations.signature: theorem volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_finset_compl (F : Finset ℕ) : volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet ((↑F : Set ℕ)ᶜ)) = ((2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ F.card)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: Exact finite-codimension volume. Forbidding exactly the coordinates in `F` leaves a face of Lebesgue measure `2^(-|F|)`.

declarations.name: supportedMersenneAchievementSet_mono
declarations.signature: theorem supportedMersenneAchievementSet_mono {J K : Set ℕ} (hJK : J ⊆ K) : supportedMersenneAchievementSet J ⊆ supportedMersenneAchievementSet K
declarations.docstring: Enlarging the set of allowed coordinates enlarges its achievement set.

declarations.name: volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_eq_zero_of_compl_infinite
declarations.signature: theorem volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_eq_zero_of_compl_infinite {J : Set ℕ} (hJ : Jᶜ.Infinite) : volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J) = 0
declarations.docstring: If infinitely many binary coordinates are forbidden, the supported Mersenne achievement set has Lebesgue measure zero. The proof traps it below finite-codimension faces of arbitrarily small dyadic measure.

declarations.name: volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_dichotomy
declarations.signature: theorem volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_dichotomy (J : Set ℕ) : (∃ F : Finset ℕ, J = (↑F : Set ℕ)ᶜ ∧ volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J) = ((2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ F.card)⁻¹) ∨ (Jᶜ.Infinite ∧ volume (supportedMersenneAchievementSet J) = 0)
declarations.docstring: Complete Lebesgue-measure classification of supported Mersenne achievement sets. Either only the finite set `F` of coordinates is omitted, in which case the volume is exactly `2^(-|F|)`, or infinitely many coordinates are omitted and the volume is zero.

declarations.name: leastPositiveResidue
declarations.docstring: Canonical positive representative of an integer modulo `C`: a zero residue is represented by `C`, and every nonzero residue by its nonnegative Euclidean remainder.

declarations.name: leastPositiveResidue_pos_le
declarations.signature: theorem leastPositiveResidue_pos_le {C : ℕ} (hC : 0 < C) (x : ℤ) : 0 < leastPositiveResidue C x ∧ leastPositiveResidue C x ≤ C
declarations.docstring: The least positive representative really lies in the canonical interval `1, ..., C` when the modulus is positive.

declarations.name: leastPositiveResidue_modEq
declarations.signature: theorem leastPositiveResidue_modEq {C : ℕ} (hC : 0 < C) (x : ℤ) : Int.ModEq C (leastPositiveResidue C x : ℤ) x
declarations.docstring: The canonical positive representative is congruent to the source integer.

declarations.name: ResidueEscapesWindow
declarations.signature: def ResidueEscapesWindow (C bound residue : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A residue representative escapes a tail window when it is strictly above the window but still lies in the canonical positive range `1, ..., C`.

declarations.name: no_bounded_positive_state_of_residue_escape
declarations.signature: theorem no_bounded_positive_state_of_residue_escape {C bound residue c : ℕ} (hcpos : 0 < c) (hcbound : c ≤ bound) (hescape : ResidueEscapesWindow C bound residue) (hmod : c % C = residue % C) : False
declarations.docstring: No positive state bounded by `bound` can represent, modulo `C`, a least positive residue which escapes that bound. This is the finite contradiction at the end of the prime-channel residue-escape strategy.

declarations.name: residue_le_bound_of_bounded_positive_state
declarations.signature: theorem residue_le_bound_of_bounded_positive_state {C bound residue c : ℕ} (hcpos : 0 < c) (hcbound : c ≤ bound) (hresidueC : residue ≤ C) (hmod : c % C = residue % C) : residue ≤ bound
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive form used by a rational-tail argument: if a positive state in the short window has the prescribed congruence, then that residue cannot escape the window.

declarations.name: no_bounded_positive_int_state_of_leastPositiveResidue
declarations.signature: theorem no_bounded_positive_int_state_of_leastPositiveResidue {C bound : ℕ} {x c : ℤ} (hC : 0 < C) (hcpos : 0 < c) (hcbound : Int.natAbs c ≤ bound) (hescape : bound < leastPositiveResidue C x) (hmod : Int.ModEq C c x) : False
declarations.docstring: Integer-valued form of the finite contradiction.

declarations.name: windowBase
declarations.signature: def windowBase (b : ℕ → ℤ) (lo : ℕ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => 1 | len + 1 => b (lo + len) * windowBase b lo len /-- Affine forcing accumulated across the same local window. -/ def windowForcing (b e : ℕ → ℤ) (lo : ℕ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => 0 | len + 1 => b (lo + len) * windowForcing b e lo len + e (lo + len) /-- Any first-order affine recurrence unrolls exactly into the local base and local forcing. -/ theorem affineRecurrence_window (A b e : ℕ → ℤ) (lo len : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ n, A (n + 1) = b n * A n + e n) :
declarations.docstring: Multiplicative base accumulated across a local window.

declarations.name: windowForcing
declarations.signature: def windowForcing (b e : ℕ → ℤ) (lo : ℕ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => 0 | len + 1 => b (lo + len) * windowForcing b e lo len + e (lo + len) /-- Any first-order affine recurrence unrolls exactly into the local base and local forcing. -/ theorem affineRecurrence_window (A b e : ℕ → ℤ) (lo len : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ n, A (n + 1) = b n * A n + e n) : A (lo + len) = windowBase b lo len * A lo + windowForcing b e lo len
declarations.docstring: Affine forcing accumulated across the same local window.

declarations.name: affineRecurrence_window
declarations.signature: theorem affineRecurrence_window (A b e : ℕ → ℤ) (lo len : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ n, A (n + 1) = b n * A n + e n) : A (lo + len) = windowBase b lo len * A lo + windowForcing b e lo len
declarations.docstring: Any first-order affine recurrence unrolls exactly into the local base and local forcing.

declarations.name: windowForcing_const_mul
declarations.signature: theorem windowForcing_const_mul (b e : ℕ → ℤ) (B : ℤ) (lo len : ℕ) : windowForcing b (fun n => B * e n) lo len = B * windowForcing b e lo len
declarations.docstring: Scaling every forcing term scales the accumulated local numerator by the same constant.

declarations.name: integralCarry_window
declarations.signature: theorem integralCarry_window (c b m : ℕ → ℤ) (B : ℤ) (lo len : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ n, c (n + 1) = b n * c n - B * m n) : c (lo + len) = windowBase b lo len * c lo - B * windowForcing b m lo len
declarations.docstring: Integral-carry form of the local-window identity.

declarations.name: CofinalLocalWindowEscape
declarations.signature: def CofinalLocalWindowEscape (b m : ℕ → ℕ) (shortBound : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The exact remaining producer after local-window compression. The short bound is denominator-dependent because a rational carry bound scales with the reduced denominator `B`.

declarations.name: no_positive_reducedCarry_of_cofinalLocalWindowEscape
declarations.signature: theorem no_positive_reducedCarry_of_cofinalLocalWindowEscape (b m : ℕ → ℕ) (shortBound : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (hescape : CofinalLocalWindowEscape b m shortBound) (B : ℕ) (hBpos : 0 < B) (hBcoprime : Nat.Coprime B 30) (d : ℕ → ℤ) (hrec : ∀ n, d (n + 1) = (b n : ℤ) * d n - (B : ℤ) * (m n : ℤ)) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < d n) (hbound : ∀ n, Int.natAbs (d n) ≤ shortBound B n) : False
declarations.docstring: A denominator-dependent cofinal local-window escape rules out every positive reduced carry satisfying the matching bound.

declarations.name: smooth3Val
declarations.signature: def smooth3Val (p q r i j k : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The `{p,q,r}`-smooth lattice point with exponent vector `(i,j,k)`.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight
declarations.signature: def threePrimeHeight (p q r x : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The product of the largest pure `p`-, `q`-, and `r`-powers not exceeding `x`. For a `{p,q,r}`-smooth `x`, this is the running LCM of the smooth prefix.

declarations.name: threePrimeKernelQ
declarations.signature: def threePrimeKernelQ (p q r i j k : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The exact rational lattice kernel attached to the running-LCM height.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixExponents
declarations.signature: def smoothPrefixExponents (p q r x : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
declarations.docstring: Exponent vectors of the actual `{p,q,r}`-smooth prefix up to `x`. The logarithmic box makes the prefix finite; the final filter keeps only products which really lie below `x`.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm
declarations.signature: def smoothPrefixLcm (p q r x : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The literal running LCM of the finite smooth prefix.

declarations.name: smooth3Val_dvd_threePrimeHeight_of_mem
declarations.signature: theorem smooth3Val_dvd_threePrimeHeight_of_mem {p q r x : ℕ} {e : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ} (he : e ∈ smoothPrefixExponents p q r x) : smooth3Val p q r e.1 e.2.1 e.2.2 ∣ threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: Every actual smooth prefix value divides the coordinatewise maximal pure-power product.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_dvd_threePrimeHeight
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_dvd_threePrimeHeight (p q r x : ℕ) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r x ∣ threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: The literal smooth-prefix LCM divides the computational height.

declarations.name: pureFirst_mem_smoothPrefixExponents
declarations.signature: theorem pureFirst_mem_smoothPrefixExponents {p q r x : ℕ} (hx : x ≠ 0) : (Nat.log p x, 0, 0) ∈ smoothPrefixExponents p q r x
declarations.docstring: The pure `p` height component occurs in the actual prefix.

declarations.name: pureSecond_mem_smoothPrefixExponents
declarations.signature: theorem pureSecond_mem_smoothPrefixExponents {p q r x : ℕ} (hx : x ≠ 0) : (0, Nat.log q x, 0) ∈ smoothPrefixExponents p q r x
declarations.docstring: The pure `q` height component occurs in the actual prefix.

declarations.name: pureThird_mem_smoothPrefixExponents
declarations.signature: theorem pureThird_mem_smoothPrefixExponents {p q r x : ℕ} (hx : x ≠ 0) : (0, 0, Nat.log r x) ∈ smoothPrefixExponents p q r x
declarations.docstring: The pure `r` height component occurs in the actual prefix.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_eq_threePrimeHeight
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_eq_threePrimeHeight {p q r x : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) (hx : x ≠ 0) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r x = threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: Exact running-LCM identity for three pairwise-distinct primes.

declarations.name: SameThreePrimeLogCell
declarations.signature: def SameThreePrimeLogCell (p q r x y : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Two cutoffs lie in the same three-prime logarithmic cell when none of the three maximal pure-power coordinates changes between them.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight_eq_of_sameLogCell
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeHeight_eq_of_sameLogCell {p q r x y : ℕ} (hcell : SameThreePrimeLogCell p q r x y) : threePrimeHeight p q r x = threePrimeHeight p q r y
declarations.docstring: The computational height is exactly constant on every logarithmic cell.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_eq_of_sameLogCell
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_eq_of_sameLogCell {p q r x y : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hcell : SameThreePrimeLogCell p q r x y) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r x = smoothPrefixLcm p q r y
declarations.docstring: For pairwise-distinct primes, the literal smooth-prefix LCM is constant on every three-prime logarithmic cell. This is the finite formal interface behind the prime-power jump expansion: the LCM can change only when one logarithmic coordinate changes.

declarations.name: threePrimeKernelQ_eq_of_sameLogCell
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeKernelQ_eq_of_sameLogCell {p q r i j k i' j' k' : ℕ} (hcell : SameThreePrimeLogCell p q r (smooth3Val p q r i j k) (smooth3Val p q r i' j' k')) : threePrimeKernelQ p q r i j k = threePrimeKernelQ p q r i' j' k'
declarations.docstring: The rational lattice kernel is likewise constant whenever its two smooth arguments occupy the same logarithmic cell.

declarations.name: positivePrimePowers
declarations.signature: def positivePrimePowers (p count : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The first `count` positive powers of one prime base. Exponent zero is omitted because it is the common initial value `1` in every channel.

declarations.name: positivePrimePowers_card
declarations.signature: theorem positivePrimePowers_card {p count : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : (positivePrimePowers p count).card = count
declarations.docstring: A prime base has no repeated positive powers.

declarations.name: one_not_mem_positivePrimePowers
declarations.signature: theorem one_not_mem_positivePrimePowers {p count : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : 1 ∉ positivePrimePowers p count
declarations.docstring: The common origin `1` is absent from every positive prime-power channel.

declarations.name: positivePrimePowers_disjoint
declarations.signature: theorem positivePrimePowers_disjoint {p q pcount qcount : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) : Disjoint (positivePrimePowers p pcount) (positivePrimePowers q qcount)
declarations.docstring: Positive power channels of two distinct primes are disjoint.

declarations.name: threePrimePositiveJumpSet
declarations.signature: def threePrimePositiveJumpSet (p q r count : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The finite union of the first `count` positive powers in each of the three prime channels.

declarations.name: threePrimePositiveJumpSet_card
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimePositiveJumpSet_card {p q r count : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) : (threePrimePositiveJumpSet p q r count).card = 3 * count
declarations.docstring: For three pairwise-distinct primes, the finite positive jump channels have exactly `3 * count` elements: there are no cross-channel duplicate powers.

declarations.name: threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin
declarations.signature: def threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin (p q r count : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The finite jump set including the unique common origin `1`.

declarations.name: threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin_card
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin_card {p q r count : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) : (threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin p q r count).card = 3 * count + 1
declarations.docstring: Including the common origin turns the `3 * count` positive candidates into exactly `3 * count + 1` distinct finite jump values.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight_firstLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeHeight_firstLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x + 1) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x) : threePrimeHeight p q r y = p * threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: If only the first logarithmic coordinate advances by one, the height is multiplied by the first base.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight_secondLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeHeight_secondLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x + 1) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x) : threePrimeHeight p q r y = q * threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: If only the second logarithmic coordinate advances by one, the height is multiplied by the second base.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight_thirdLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeHeight_thirdLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x + 1) : threePrimeHeight p q r y = r * threePrimeHeight p q r x
declarations.docstring: If only the third logarithmic coordinate advances by one, the height is multiplied by the third base.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_firstLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_firstLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (pprime : p.Prime) (qprime : q.Prime) (rprime : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x + 1) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r y = p * smoothPrefixLcm p q r x
declarations.docstring: A first-coordinate jump multiplies the literal running LCM by `p`.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_secondLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_secondLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (pprime : p.Prime) (qprime : q.Prime) (rprime : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x + 1) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r y = q * smoothPrefixLcm p q r x
declarations.docstring: A second-coordinate jump multiplies the literal running LCM by `q`.

declarations.name: smoothPrefixLcm_thirdLogStep
declarations.signature: theorem smoothPrefixLcm_thirdLogStep {p q r x y : ℕ} (pprime : p.Prime) (qprime : q.Prime) (rprime : r.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hp : Nat.log p y = Nat.log p x) (hq : Nat.log q y = Nat.log q x) (hr : Nat.log r y = Nat.log r x + 1) : smoothPrefixLcm p q r y = r * smoothPrefixLcm p q r x
declarations.docstring: A third-coordinate jump multiplies the literal running LCM by `r`.

declarations.name: smoothExponentBox
declarations.signature: def smoothExponentBox (hp hq hr : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
declarations.docstring: A finite rectangular exponent box. This is the exact finite domain used before passing to the infinite three-prime smooth series.

declarations.name: smoothPointHeight
declarations.signature: def smoothPointHeight (p q r : ℕ) (e : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The running-LCM height attached to one smooth exponent triple.

declarations.name: smoothHeightFiber
declarations.signature: def smoothHeightFiber (p q r hp hq hr H : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
declarations.docstring: The points of a finite exponent box with one fixed running-LCM height.

declarations.name: smoothHeightFiber_kernel_sum
declarations.signature: theorem smoothHeightFiber_kernel_sum (p q r hp hq hr H : ℕ) : (∑ e ∈ smoothHeightFiber p q r hp hq hr H, threePrimeKernelQ p q r e.1 e.2.1 e.2.2) = (smoothHeightFiber p q r hp hq hr H).card • ((H : ℚ)⁻¹)
declarations.docstring: On a fixed height fiber, every lattice-kernel summand is the reciprocal of that common height, so the fiber sum is exactly its multiplicity times that reciprocal.

declarations.name: finiteSmoothKernelSum_groupedByHeight
declarations.signature: theorem finiteSmoothKernelSum_groupedByHeight (p q r hp hq hr : ℕ) : (∑ e ∈ smoothExponentBox hp hq hr, threePrimeKernelQ p q r e.1 e.2.1 e.2.2) = ∑ H ∈ (smoothExponentBox hp hq hr).image (smoothPointHeight p q r), (smoothHeightFiber p q r hp hq hr H).card • ((H : ℚ)⁻¹)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite normal form obtained by grouping the smooth lattice kernel by its genuine running-LCM heights. The coefficient of each height is the cardinality of its fiber. Together with logarithmic-cell constancy, this is the checked finite core of the prime-power jump expansion.

declarations.name: threePrimeHeight_le_cube
declarations.signature: theorem threePrimeHeight_le_cube (p q r x : ℕ) (hx : x ≠ 0) : threePrimeHeight p q r x ≤ x ^ 3
declarations.docstring: Each pure-power component of the height is at most `x`, so the three-prime height is bounded by `x³`.

declarations.name: kernel_235_origin
declarations.docstring: Each pure-power component of the height is at most `x`, so the three-prime height is bounded by `x³`. -/ theorem threePrimeHeight_le_cube (p q r x : ℕ) (hx : x ≠ 0) : threePrimeHeight p q r x ≤ x ^ 3 := by have hp := Nat.pow_log_le_self p hx have hq := Nat.pow_log_le_self q hx have hr := Nat.pow_log_le_self r hx calc threePrimeHeight p q r x ≤ (x * x) * x := Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul hp hq) hr _ = x ^ 3 := by ring /-! The first exact `{2,3,5}` kernel values.

declarations.name: kernel_235_not_rankOne
declarations.signature: theorem kernel_235_not_rankOne : threePrimeKernelQ 2 3 5 0 0 0 * threePrimeKernelQ 2 3 5 1 1 0 ≠ threePrimeKernelQ 2 3 5 1 0 0 * threePrimeKernelQ 2 3 5 0 1 0
declarations.docstring: The smallest exact witness that the three-prime kernel is not rank one. The two sides are `1/60` and `1/12`.

declarations.name: tailStateStep
declarations.signature: def tailStateStep (base digit state : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: One step of the exact variable-base tail orbit from the jump expansion.

declarations.name: tailStateStep_eq
declarations.signature: theorem tailStateStep_eq (base digit state next : ℤ) : next = tailStateStep base digit state ↔ next = base * state - base * digit

declarations.name: smoothExponentShell
declarations.signature: def smoothExponentShell (p q r lo hi hp hq hr : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
declarations.docstring: Exponent triples in a half-open multiplicative shell, with explicit coordinate bounds. The coordinate bounds are the interface to the pure-power jump heights; the interval filter is the actual smooth-number shell.

declarations.name: exponent_unique_in_short_interval
declarations.signature: theorem exponent_unique_in_short_interval {base lo hi weight a b : ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hwidth : hi ≤ base * lo) (haLo : lo ≤ base ^ a * weight) (haHi : base ^ a * weight < hi) (hbLo : lo ≤ base ^ b * weight) (hbHi : base ^ b * weight < hi) : a = b
declarations.docstring: In an interval of multiplicative width at most `base`, fixing the other factors leaves at most one exponent of `base`.

declarations.name: smoothExponentShell_card_le_dropFirst
declarations.signature: theorem smoothExponentShell_card_le_dropFirst {p q r lo hi hp hq hr : ℕ} (hpPos : 0 < p) (hwidth : hi ≤ p * lo) : (smoothExponentShell p q r lo hi hp hq hr).card ≤ (hq + 1) * (hr + 1)
declarations.docstring: Projecting away the first exponent is injective on a shell whose width is at most the first base. Consequently the shell has at most the size of the other two exponent ranges.

declarations.name: smoothExponentShell_card_le_dropThird
declarations.signature: theorem smoothExponentShell_card_le_dropThird {p q r lo hi hp hq hr : ℕ} (hrPos : 0 < r) (hwidth : hi ≤ r * lo) : (smoothExponentShell p q r lo hi hp hq hr).card ≤ (hp + 1) * (hq + 1)
declarations.docstring: The symmetric projection needed when the third height is the largest: fixing the first two exponents leaves at most one exponent of the third base.

declarations.name: sorted_pair_quadratic
declarations.signature: theorem sorted_pair_quadratic {a b c j : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) (hsum : a + b + c = j) : 9 * ((a + 1) * (b + 1)) ≤ (j + 3) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: If `a ≤ b ≤ c` and the three heights sum to `j`, then the product of the two smaller shifted heights satisfies the clean quadratic estimate used in the scaled-tail analysis. This is the denominator-free form of `(a+1)(b+1) ≤ (j+3)²/9`.

declarations.name: smoothExponentShell_card_quadratic
declarations.signature: theorem smoothExponentShell_card_quadratic {p q r lo hi hp hq hr j : ℕ} (hrPos : 0 < r) (hwidth : hi ≤ r * lo) (hpq : hp ≤ hq) (hqr : hq ≤ hr) (hsum : hp + hq + hr = j) : 9 * (smoothExponentShell p q r lo hi hp hq hr).card ≤ (j + 3) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: The exact smooth shell inherits the uniform quadratic multiplicity bound once its height coordinates are sorted and sum to the jump index.

declarations.name: DyadicInternalPower
declarations.signature: def DyadicInternalPower (p a e : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A positive `p`-power lies strictly inside the dyadic block `(2^a, 2^(a+1))`. Endpoints are excluded because the dyadic jump itself is the distinguished terminal factor of the compressed block.

declarations.name: dyadicInternalPower_exponent_unique
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicInternalPower_exponent_unique {p a e f : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (he : DyadicInternalPower p a e) (hf : DyadicInternalPower p a f) : e = f
declarations.docstring: A channel contributes at most one internal pure-power jump to a dyadic block. This is the exact reason that a compressed `{2,3,5}` block contains at most the dyadic jump together with one `3`-jump and one `5`-jump.

declarations.name: dyadicBlockBase235
declarations.docstring: The exact radix of the dyadic block after compressing all internal `3`- and `5`-power jumps. Each internal channel contributes its prime once, and the terminal dyadic jump contributes the factor `2`.

declarations.name: dyadicBlockBase235_cases
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicBlockBase235_cases (a : ℕ) : dyadicBlockBase235 a = 2 ∨ dyadicBlockBase235 a = 6 ∨ dyadicBlockBase235 a = 10 ∨ dyadicBlockBase235 a = 30
declarations.docstring: Every actual compressed dyadic radix is one of `2, 6, 10, 30`. This replaces the generic interval `[2,30]` by the exact four-symbol alphabet consumed by the integer certificate engine.

declarations.name: dyadicBlockBase235_mem_interval
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicBlockBase235_mem_interval (a : ℕ) : 2 ≤ dyadicBlockBase235 a ∧ dyadicBlockBase235 a ≤ 30
declarations.docstring: In particular, the actual dyadic block radix satisfies the hypotheses of the checked bounded-radix escape theorem, with no hidden larger base.
